title: Oxfam Yemen C&F Supporting Peace Proces
description:
This project falls under the thematic area Conflict <(>&<)> Fragility (C<(>&<)>F). Through our work Oxfam Novib and SOMO aim to achieve a stronger voice for marginalized groups in policies that affect their lives; governments and international institutions support inclusion of women and promote protection of marginalized groups in security and peace building; and the private sector contributes to peace and development.

Within this Theory of Change, this project in Yemen has set the following long term objective: needs and voices of Yemeni women affected by conflict in Yemen are represented at sub-, national and international levels in conflict to ensure inclusive and gender-sensitive peace building through a strengthened and effective civil society and community based initiatives.

Oxfam Yemen together with AWAM Foundation for Development and Culture  and  Yemeni Leadership Development Foundation will ensure the voices of Yemeni women are heard in the peace and security processes and new alliances are built to sustain coordination and inclusive gender responsive policy development. They will do this through capacity support to civil society, engagement with governmental authorities and informal leaders and engagement with the international community.

About 30 local civil society organizations andtheir leaders will be supported to become change agents on national level and who will initiate women#s platforms in 3 districts (Sana#a, Taiz, and Aden) with the aim to influence peace and security processes  such as peace building policy development so that these reflect women's needs. The main strategies employed will be training, alliance building, international and national campaigning, and addressing interests of women affected by conflict at the grassroots and conveying this through national and international platforms. From this leadership position the organizations will also be able to offer advice to government, especially at the governoratelevel, on gender mainstreaming and gender sensitive conflict prevention and peace building.

In order to strengthen the alliance, the project partners will closely collaborate with Yemeni Women Pact for Peace and Security, Women Partners for Peace as well as International Support Group on Women#s Participation in theYemen Peace Processes (ISGWPY) and other actors such as UN Women Officer of Special Envoy, donors and governments to contribute to setting up common agendas and joining resources in advocating for women#s rights in peace and security.

title: Water distribution in Yemen
description: In partnership with the National Foundation for Development and Humanitarian response, Oxfam in Yemen is using this contribution for a water distribution program. The country is in war and the UN estimate is that 70% of the population depends on humanitarian aid.In this program water supply constructions to 10 schools are constructed or rehabilitated. This will reach over 15.000 children in 3 districts in Sa'ada gouvernorate. Women are taking leadership roles in these efforts. This gives women a more active and visible role in community affairs compared to the pre-conflict situation. This is an unplanned outcome of the was, but one that needs support, so that women don't lose the social gains after the war.

description:
The Project’s expected effect(s) on society is to prevent and solve violent conflicts and building lasting peace. Through our work Conflict and Fragility Oxfam Novib and SOMO aim to achieve that more marginalized groups have a say in policies that affect theirlives; governments and international institutions support inclusion of women and promote protection of marginalized groups in security and peace building; and the private sector contributes to peace and development.

From 2016 to 2018 the project focused on raising awareness of the governmental entities on gender and UNSCR 1325 WPS Agenda and building capacities of CSOs on gender, UNSCR 1325 and the advocacy for women, peace and security. As a result 7 coalitions were formed to advocate for women peace and security. Despite challenging and escalating conflict we saw signs of political will amongst government officials. In the coming years the project aims to advocate for systemic change systematic change. The alliances will step-up their advocacy and lobby on the local and national levels to gain womens influential engagement in peace building processes and for women leadership. We continue to adapt to the local context and in view of aggravation of security situations we will mitigate by condensing activities in the safer locations if necessary and where possible.
Given the lessons in view of the Yemeni context, we will focus on political will for the women peace andsecurity agenda in and outside of Yemen instead of policy change, because change of policy is considered near impossible with multiple authorities in conflict. The long term outcome remains the same as we aim to achieve that needs and voices of Yemeni women affected by conflict in Yemen are represented at sub-, national and international levels in conflict to ensure inclusive and gender-sensitive peace building through a strengthened and effective civil society and community based initiatives.

Oxfam Yemen will continue working with with AWAM Foundation for Development and Culture and Yemeni Leadership Development Foundation and engage with Hudaydah Girls Foundation, SoS in support of the 7 alliances formed of about 30 local civil society organizations.

Vulnerability criteria will be developed in consultationwith the community and it should be agreed upon among the YJR members (harmonized tool and approaches). Following the initial beneficiary identification. Oxfam#s MEAL team will conduct eligibility verification through door to door assessments, through direct interviews of the initial list provided by community committees and indirectly from the community. Upon completion of the verification process, the final list of beneficiaries will post in several public places, so that eligible beneficiaries are aware and those whom are not selected can make appeals through thecomplaints box mechanism, which will be placed in a strategic location within the community.

description: Humanitarian support (Child Protection): Most vulnerable children are protected against violence, abuse and violations of children’s rights: This programme aims to ensure that the most vulnerable children are protected from violence, abuse and violations of their rights by strengthening the safety and resilience of the environments around them. It focuses on preventing harm by addressing underlying risks such as poverty, harmful norms, weak protection systems and limited access to services, while also providing timely, child-centred support when protection concerns arise. Working with families, communities, schools and local authorities, the programme builds the capacity of caregivers and institutions to recognize risks early and respond safely and inclusively in line with international child protection standards. It expands access to essential protection services—such as case management, psychosocial support and clear referral pathways—designed to meet the specific needs of girls and boys of different ages and abilities. The programme also empowers children with knowledge of their rights and life skills that help them stay safe and express their needs. By reinforcing community-based protection mechanisms and strengthening coordination with national systems, the programme fosters a more protective environment that upholds children’s well-being in both everyday situations and during crises. All SC programmes are gender mainstreamed, inclusive and aims to strengthens resilience.

The response will support 2,000 families with cash transfers to help them meet immediate necessities, complemented by the distribution of 300,000 hygiene kits and the installation of 120 handwashing points in affected schools and shelters to reduce waterborne disease risks. To restore access to learning as quickly as possible, Save the Children will provide logistical support to clean and rehabilitate 40 schools that were flooded or used as shelters, enabling 10,800 students to return to class, and will distribute 3,000 student kits and 120 teacher kits to replace essential materials lost in the disaster. Protection efforts will prioritize girls and other vulnerable groups through the distribution of 800 dignity kits and expanded SGBV prevention sessions in shelters and affected communities. In total, the project aims to reach 14,720 people, including 13,800 children—among them 50 children with disabilities.  With its established presence and strong local partnerships, Save the Children will maximize the impact of this life-saving support, while post-distribution monitoring will help assess and strengthen the effectiveness of the cash and kit interventions. All SC programmes are gender mainstreamed, inclusive and aims to strengthen resilience.

title: Safer Salvage Operation
description: This project aims to prevent a catastrophic oil spill occurring in the Red Sea and its potentially disastrous impacts. This shall be achieved by mobilising salvage assets (including a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) and installation of a Catenary Anchor Leg Mooring (CALM) Buoy, offloading the oil from FSO Safer to the VLCC, placing an oil-spill contingency response on standby.\nThe Floating Storage and Offloading (FSO) vessel Safer is moored approximately 8 kilometres off the coast of Yemen and 50 kilometres northeast of the port of Hodeida. Constructed in 1976 as an oil tanker and converted in 1987 to be a floating storage facility, the vessel is single-hulled, 362 meters in length, and is believed to contain an estimated 1.148 million barrels of light crude oil. Safer has been under the de facto authorities (DFA) in Sana’a since March 2015. Production and offloading operations are suspended due to the conflict, and no maintenance operations have been undertaken for seven years. The FSO is now uninsurable, with an expired certificate of seaworthiness. The Safer’s age and lack of maintenance have deteriorated its structural integrity. The vessel is at risk of spilling oil due to leakages, an explosion from the accumulation of volatile explosion gases, or a strike from a floating sea mine. A significant spill could occur at any time, discharging up to 1,148 million barrels of its cargo of oil along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and towards its neighbouring countries. Heavy contamination and pollution could extend as far as the Bab-El-Mandab strait, with some oil passing beyond the Gulf of Aden.

As students are taught in wrecked wet classrooms, number of students- especially girls- are dropped out as they frequently get sick because of the unhealthy environment in the classes.

title: Providing the marginalized group with clean water

The project aims at improving the access of the marginalized people to clean water for drinking, cooking and personal and domestic hygiene. The project will contribute to reducing outbreak of Cholera and other dirty water-borne diseases that have spread in the targeted area due to inaccessibility to clean water.

Our goal would be to meet these needs and go further by replacing all substandard enclosures providing more jobs.

title: Yemen: Health System Strengthening
description: One of GAVI’s strategic goals is to “contribute to strengthening the capacity of integrated health systems to deliver immunisation”. The objective of GAVI cash support is to address system bottlenecks to achieve better immunisation outcomes, including coverage and equity. The GAVI approach is results oriented. The objective of GAVI support for Health Systems Strengthening (HSS) is to address system bottlenecks to achieve better immunisation outcomes, including coverage and equity. As such, it is necessary for applications for HSS support by countries to be based on a strong bottleneck and gap analysis, and present a clear results chain demonstrating the link between proposed activities and improved immunisation outcomes. GAVI’s approach intends to deliver and document results. From 2013, the HSS cash-based funding stream replaces the previous support to Immunisation Services Support (ISS), Health Systems Funding Platform (HSFP) and Civil Society funding.

title: Yemen: Inactivated Polio Vaccine
description: The Vaccine Alliance supported one of the fastest roll-outs in the history of vaccination: the introduction of at least one dose of IPV into the routine immunisation schedules of Gavi-supported countries, which was achieved in April 2019, less than five years after the initial launch.  Countries introducing IPV received a one-time cash grant from Gavi, funded by GPEI, to support some of the additional activity costs related to introducing the new vaccine. These activities may include health worker training, social mobilisation, micro-planning, expansion or rehabilitation of cold chain equipment, printing of materials (such as immunisation cards), technical assistance and modifications to the surveillance systems.

title: Yemen: Immunisation Safety Devices
description: Injected medicines are commonly used in healthcare settings for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various illnesses. Unsafe injection practices put patients and healthcare providers at risk of infectious and non-infectious adverse events and have been associated with a wide variety of procedures and settings. This harm is preventable. Safe injection practices are part of Standard Precautions and are aimed at maintaining basic levels of patient safety and provider protections. As defined by the World Health Organization, a safe injection does not harm the recipient, does not expose the provider to any avoidable risks and does not result in waste that is dangerous for the community

title: Yemen: Measles and Measles-rubella
description: GAVI’s support for new vaccines presents an opportunity for countries to not only implement vaccines that protect against diseases causing substantial morbidity and/or mortality, but also to build upon the vaccine investments in order to increase immunisation coverage rates, and strengthen routine immunisation services and primary health care systems. GAVI helps protect children in eligible countries against measles by providing support for a second dose of measles-containing vaccine, to be introduced into the routine immunisation programme. Providing a second opportunity for measles vaccination is a very powerful tool to reach children who missed the first dose and to produce immunity in a number of persons who failed to develop measles immunity after the first dose. Support for the measles vaccine and associated injection safety materials is for a period of five years.

title: Yemen: Cholera
description:
Gavi has supported the global oral cholera vaccine stockpile since 2014

Oral cholera vaccine stockpile

The global oral cholera vaccine (OCV) stockpile was founded in mid-2013 by five donors.

In 2013, the Gavi Board approved support for the stockpile as part of our Vaccine Investment Strategy. Our contribution of over US$ 110 million for the 2014–2018 period aims to increase access to OCV during emergencies and in countries that regularly experience cholera outbreaks.

title: Yemen: Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines
description: GAVI’s support for new vaccines presents an opportunity for countries to not only implement vaccines that protect against diseases causing substantial morbidity and/or mortality, but also to build upon the vaccine investments in order to increase immunisation coverage rates, and strengthen routine immunisation services and primary health care systems. Pneumococcal vaccines can protect children from Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is the most common cause of severe pneumonia among children living in the developing world, and can also causes meningitis and sepsis. In line with WHO recommendations, GAVI support for pneumococcal vaccines is for routine infant immunisation. Two pneumococcal conjugate vaccines are currently available with GAVI support: a 10-valent (PCV10) and a 13-valent (PCV13).

title: Yemen: Pentavalent
description: GAVI’s support for new vaccines presents an opportunity for countries to not only implement vaccines that protect against diseases causing substantial morbidity and/or mortality, but also to build upon the vaccine investments in order to increase immunisation coverage rates, and strengthen routine immunisation services and primary health care systems. The pentavalent vaccine, administered in a three-dose schedule, offers protection against five diseases: diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis (DTP), heptatitis B and Haemophilius influenzae type b. Until 2013, GAVI has helped to introduce the pentavalent in 70 of the 73 GAVI-eligible countries, with the aim of reaching all 73 by the end of 2014. GAVI support for pentavalent vaccine is in line with WHO recommendations, for routine infant immunisation and primarily targeting children under one year of age.

title: Yemen: Rotavirus
description: GAVI’s support for new vaccines presents an opportunity for countries to not only implement vaccines that protect against diseases causing substantial morbidity and/or mortality, but also to build upon the vaccine investments in order to increase immunisation coverage rates, and strengthen routine immunisation services and primary health care systems. Rotavirus vaccine protects children against rotavirus disease and the severe and deadly diarrhoea that it causes in children. WHO recommends that rotavirus vaccination be included in all national immunization programmes, and the use of rotavirus vaccines should be part of a comprehensive strategy to control diarrhoeal diseases. Two oral rotavirus vaccines are currently available for routine infant immunisation with GAVI support: a two-dose schedule and the three-dose schedule vaccine.

title: OGB Yemen Joint Response III
description:
Nearly 3 million people have fled their homes since the start of the conflict, most of whom  over 2.8 million  remain inside Yemen. Almost two thirds of IDPs have been displaced for 10 months or more, resulting inprotracted displacement situations. More than half of current Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) are sheltering in Hajjah, Taizz and Sanaa. Just over 1 million IDPs have provisionally returned to their areas of origin, although the sustainability of these returns remains precarious. Nearly 70 per cent of returnees are in Aden, Sanaa or Taizz, with more than 85 per cent living in their original residences. Substantial numbers are living in damaged houses, are unable to afford repairs and face serious protection risks.
The project will focus on increasing access to basic food needs for the most vulnerable conflict affected households in Abbs district of Hajjah governorates through conditional and unconditional cash transfers as well as ensuring gender and protection is mainstreamed throughout the project.
Targeted women, men, boys and girls affected by conflict have increased access to food and have protected and restored livelihood opportunities.
The project duration is from March to end December 2017 and the expected results are:
-900 conflict affected vulnerable households receive unconditional cash grants to meet their basic minimum food requirements in Abbs district of Hajjah governorates.
-300 conflict affected vulnerable households were provided with conditional cash grants for their livelihood protection and restoration in Abbs district of Hajjah governorates.
-the community based protection network has been improved to reduce the risks among IDPs and Host communities. 21000 people receivedkey message on community and self-protection through trained community members, local partner, CHVs, community mobilizer.
The project will target the most vulnerable conflict affected and food insecure households among IDPs and host communities including female- and child headed households and households  headed by a disabled member.

title: PSD Toolkit – Phase 2
description: The PSD Toolkit is a comprehensive set of tools designed to support embassies in promoting private sector development (PSD) in low and middle-income countries. By leveraging various tools within the toolkit, embassies can advance a business-enabling environment, stimulate the development of SMEs and fair value chains, and facilitate connections between local and Dutch businesses. These efforts are part of the implementation of the Dutch agenda for Aid, Trade, and Investment and contribute directly to Sustainable Development Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth.The tools that can be leveraged vary from matchmaking and Government-to-Government assistance to entrepreneurial training, trade missions, and the transfer of knowledge between universities and knowledge institutions in the Netherlands and partner countries.The PSD Toolkit also includes the Impact Clusters programme to support clusters of companies to demonstrate new technologies to the local private sector, and the Orange Corners and Orange Corners Innovation Fund programmes to support young entrepreneurs with training and access to finance.Url = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Impact+Cluster%3AUrl = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Orange+Corners%3AUrl = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Orange+Corners+Innovation+Fund%3AFor more information: Private Sector Development Toolkit (in Dutch)Url = https://www.rvo.nl/onderwerpen/private-sector-development-toolkit

By leveraging various tools within the toolkit, embassies can advance a business-enabling environment, stimulate the development of SMEs and fair value chains, and facilitate connections between local and Dutch businesses. These efforts are part of the implementation of the Dutch agenda for Aid, Trade, and Investment and contribute directly to Sustainable Development Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth.The tools that can be leveraged vary from matchmaking and Government-to-Government assistance to entrepreneurial training, trade missions, and the transfer of knowledge between universities and knowledge institutions in the Netherlands and partner countries.The PSD Toolkit also includes the Impact Clusters programme to support clusters of companies to demonstrate new technologies to the local private sector, and the Orange Corners and Orange Corners Innovation Fund programmes to support young entrepreneurs with training and access to finance.Url = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Impact+Cluster%3AUrl = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Orange+Corners%3AUrl = https://projects.rvo.nl/search?search_api_fulltext=Orange+Corners+Innovation+Fund%3AFor more information: Private Sector Development Toolkit (in Dutch)Url = https://www.rvo.nl/onderwerpen/private-sector-development-toolkit

title: Governance Integration for Stabilization and Resilience (GISR)
description: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)):  .The primary objective of this line of effort is to sustainably strengthen local and national systems to adapt to shocks and stressors in the MENA region. Programming will support U.S. foreign policy objectives by promoting stable, democratic governance in the region through expanding USAID's knowledge base and tools by advancing analysis of governance, resilience, and stabilization needs. Programming, analysis, and training will include democracy and governance components and approaches such as engaging youth, civil society & media, marginalized groups, for example, religious and ethnic minorities, and formal/informal institutions to address instability. This is a centrally managed mechanism into which Missions can invest their bilateral funds. ..During FY 2022 this mechanism will program $75,000 to meet the Women, Peace and Security through earmark through potential pilot programming and research to support survivors of gender-based violence.  Furthermore, pending receipt of funds we will look to partner with regional operating units to advance region specific analytics around women's participation in peace and conflict resolution. ..In addition, efforts will provide support for effective technical assistance in programming across the region on critical topics including Women, Peace, Security, Democracy, Stabilization, CVE, governance, civil society, anti-corruption, youth engagement and conflict prevention..

description: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)):  .The primary objective of this line of effort is to sustainably strengthen local and national systems to adapt to shocks and stressors in the MENA region. Programming will support U.S. foreign policy objectives by promoting stable, democratic governance in the region through expanding USAID's knowledge base and tools by advancing analysis of governance, resilience, and stabilization needs. Programming, analysis, and training will include democracy and governance components and approaches such as engaging youth, civil society & media, marginalized groups, for example, religious and ethnic minorities, and formal/informal institutions to address instability. This is a centrally managed mechanism into which Missions can invest their bilateral funds. ..During FY 2022 this mechanism will program $75,000 to meet the Women, Peace and Security through earmark through potential pilot programming and research to support survivors of gender-based violence.  Furthermore, pending receipt of funds we will look to partner with regional operating units to advance region specific analytics around women's participation in peace and conflict resolution. ..In addition, efforts will provide support for effective technical assistance in programming across the region on critical topics including Women, Peace, Security, Democracy, Stabilization, CVE, governance, civil society, anti-corruption, youth engagement and conflict prevention..

title: Strengthened policies and programmes on enterprises,  productivity and working conditions in SMEs, green jobs and cooperatives
description: MSMEs in Yemen face significant challenges due to prolonged conflict, leading to slow recovery and reliance on international aid. Data shows that 35% of medium-sized businesses have shut down, small enterprises have a negative growth rate, and only 6% of adults have bank accounts. Despite this, the private sector remains vital, employing over 80% of the workforce, with significant roles in agriculture, fishing, services, and manufacturing.\nThe ILO aims to support MSMEs through a multi-dimensional package promoting inclusive entrepreneurship, value chain development, access to finance, and strengthened cooperatives. \nAdditionally, the ILO seeks to boost the competitiveness and productivity of Yemen's coffee supply chain, which has potential for supporting peace and well-being. Coffee exports have declined due to conflict, low productivity, poor quality, inadequate institutional capacity, land use issues, water scarcity, and policy constraints. The ILO’s intervention will target the entire coffee supply chain—from production to export—through comprehensive measures to enhance competitiveness and export potential, advancing decent work in Yemen.

title: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations
description: Most of the industries and business owners have left the country. In the last biennium the Federation with ILO support regained visibility and introduced governance mechanisms and consultative processes leading to the definition of a 2-year Strategic Plan. Most of the actions of these business plans have been implemented under these difficult circumstances. Nevertheless, the Federation still needs to work to increase its capacity to regularly analyze the business environment and produce reports on policy issues. This needs to be encompassed with a sustainability strategy aiming to capacitate and increase its team working on policy topics. \nILO will support the efforts of the Federation to rethink its research model. After a workshop and capacity-building programme with the largest companies in the country, the ILO will define with the Federation a business model to support the Yemen Federation in research and advocacy, targeting mainly the relevance of the private sector as an actor for the sustainable economic recovery of the country.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants in Yemen
description: Since the escalation of conflict in March 2015, Yemen continues to face the world's largest humanitarian crisis. The ongoing crisis and conflict, combined with the hardening attitudes of authorities against migrants, has increased migrants' exposure to abuse and violence. In line with humanitarian, national and donor priorities for Yemen and in response to these widespread needs, through this project, IOM aims to implement a comprehensive multisectoral response to migrants in Yemen. IOM is targeting vulnerable migrants with urgent protection support (including emergency assistance) and healthcare services through static Migrant Response Points (MRPs) and mobile teams. IOM is also contributing to informing the overall humanitarian and protection response by employing its Flow Monitoring activities, through its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) programme.

title: Urgent Intevention in WASH Cluster for (3) Yemeni Governorates
description: In line with the national Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Cluster strategy, IOM seeks to improve the living conditions of internally displaced persons by restoring access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services. IOM’s WASH solutions are immediate, scalable, and sustainable, with the overall aim of reducing morbidity and mortality rates and the spread of water borne diseases among communities affected by the ongoing conflict.

title: Alleviating The Impact Of The Ukraine Crisis On Yemen Through The Provision Of Provision Of Life-Saving Multi-Sectoral Assistance To Food Insecure Communities
description: Since the escalation of conflict in March 2015, the humanitarian situation in Yemen has led to unprecedented suffering across the country.  Trends point to a deteriorating humanitarian and food security situation in Yemen, with fighting and clashes exacerbating existing vulnerabilities, stalled development gains made in the years preceding, and has driven the country to the brink of famine.  The conflict in Ukraine is contributing to even further deteriorating conditions in Yemen, and experts predict that Yemen will continue to grapple with the ripple effects of the recent hikes in the price of petroleum and diesel and project that direct and indirect ramifications of the Russia-Ukraine war on the prices of minimum food baskets would be devastating. In line with Yemen’s Humanitarian Response Plan for 2022 and IOM’s Crisis Response Plan for Yemen, IOM proposes to contribute towards alleviating the immediate suffering of food insecure populations with timely and high-impact multi-sectoral (Health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), Protection, and multi-purpose cash) interventions, as well as complementary interventions such as assessments through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) that are crucial for informing the integrated response.

title: Provision of Integrated Protection and Life-Saving Health Services to Migrants and IDPs in Yemen
description: Migration through Yemen has become a riskier process over the past 2-3 years and COVID-19 has exacerbated or accelerated certain trends. Migrants are amongst the most marginalized, excluded and vulnerable groups of people in need in Yemen. The on-going crisis and conflict, combined with the hardening attitudes of authorities against migrants, has increased their exposure to abuse and violence. As Yemen’s humanitarian situation worsens, critical indicators such as access to health care, water and sanitation, food insecurity and malnutrition are worsening, and civilians are becoming increasingly exposed to conflict. This action aims to build on IOM and partners' current migrant assistance and response capacity that meets the most critical needs of migrants traveling through Yemen. The action contributes to this goal through the continued employment of an integrated health and protection approach that prioritizes the most vulnerable migrants in Yemen at disembarkation points, along transit routes and hubs, and in locations where migrants are stranded or trapped as a result of conflict, crisis barriers and/or the impact of COVID-19 border closures. IOM and partners are providing migrants with access to health assistance, information on safe migration, individualized protection support and immediate short-term and emergency support that addresses demonstrated needs.

title: Emergency Relief and Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Marib, Al Hudaydah, and Taizz Governorates, Yemen
description: Through this action, IOM is providing coordination, information management and emergency relief services, including cash and voucher assistance (CVA), that supports vulnerable populations and humanitarian actors in Yemen. This project is advancing humanitarian response in Marib and the west coast region (Hudaydah and southern Taizz) where urgent interventions are required to meet the needs of acutely displaced populations. More specifically, IOM is providing shelter and non-food items, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), CVA and camp coordination and camp management support to internally displaced persons (IDPs) in 43 IOM-supported IDP sites (34 in Marib, and 9 in Al Hudaydah). WASH services will also be extended to underserved IDP sites in southern Taizz.

title: Provision of Life-Saving Multi-Sectoral Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Other Conflict-Affected Communities in Yemen
description: Yemen is facing the world’s worst humanitarian crisis. Nearly two thirds of the total population (20.7 million people) requires some form of humanitarian and protection assistance, and an estimated 4 million people have been internally displaced since the onset of the conflict. Humanitarian needs are widespread in relation to shelter and non-food items, camp coordination and camp management, and water, sanitation, and hygiene sectors, and cash-based interventions are greatly needed. IOM is committed to ensuring that multi-sectoral assistance is available to the most vulnerable people in Yemen and that internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities, and migrants are able to live with dignity and access to assistance that meets their most critical needs. IOM is contributing to the improvement of the living conditions and protection of IDPs and conflict affected communities in Yemen, particularly at a time when COVID-19 has eroded coping mechanisms, increased dependency on aid and reduced access to services. Proposed multi-sector humanitarian activities are contextualized to needs, integrating and mainstreaming COVID-19 response outcomes across all programmes.

title: Multisectoral Humanitarian Assistance to IDP Sites in Al Khukhah District, Al Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen, Priority 1
description: Between 11 and 14 November 2021, a reported 895 households fled the renewal of violent hostilities to sites in Al Khukhah district, Al-Hodeidah Governorate, Yemen. The new arrival of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and worsening security situation has compounded the already pressing multisectoral needs of vulnerable groups in the West Coast. In response to the widespread needs and recent displacements in the West Coast, the project provides a comprehensive and integrated multisectoral intervention that establishes/improves site management support, coordinates of service delivery, and provides integrated water, sanitation and hygiene, health, and protection assistance across 12 IDP sites in the underserved district of Al Khukhah.

title: Scholarship for tuition fees at Swedish higher education institution
description: Students from countries on the OECD/DAC's list of recipient countries studying at a Swedish university can apply for scholarships to finance their education in Sweden. Students who participate in the program are given increased international understanding and development of methods and working methods when studying at a Swedish university. Through the program, Swedish universities are given a strategic and competitive tool on the global education market. They can offer international mobility programmes and skills development for students from low- and middle-income countries by recruiting specially qualified fee-paying students from these countries. The funds are used to reduce the whole or some part of the tuition fees for the students who are awarded scholarships. The scholarship program stimulates and facilitates mobility, international cooperation and contributes to the supply of skills.

title: Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) in Developing Markets
description: Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) in Developing Markets is an innovation competition with several calls running on specific challenges in developing countries.SBIR in Developing Markets supports Dutch entrepreneurs to come up with innovative solutions for certain challenges and use their knowledge and skills in cooperation with local entrepreneurs. SBIR in Developing Markets support focusses on research and development, and ultimately aims to make a positive contribution to local entrepreneurship and to have local impact. Local impact is translated into fitting an innovation and entrepreneurship in the local context of each formulated challenge, taking into account local systems, networks and markets and a solution for a longer period of time, based on an actual business model.The Netherlands Enterprise Agency administers SBIR in Developing Markets at the request of the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

MEG will support requests from the ME Bureau field operating units for assessments and diagnostics, program designs and model scopes of work, technical briefs and case studies, and pilot and bridge activities. title: Provision of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to Vulnerable IDP Households in Yemen (Rapid Response Mechanism), Priority 2
description: In 2021, 491,000 people were displaced in Yemen due to protracted and intensified conflict (HNO 2022), and in the first five months of 2022, over 42,000 people have been displaced. Additionally, the conflict in Ukraine has impacted the rise of food prices, compounding the pre-existing food insecurity for vulnerable groups across Yemen. The deteriorating economic conditions in Yemen have placed an additional burden on vulnerable groups, including women, children and persons with disabilities, to adopt negative coping strategies, including incurring significant debt burdens, agreeing to early marriage and, with constrained access to basic services, becoming even more dependent on external assistance. In this project, IOM aims to improve the living conditions of newly displaced crisis affected households and families affected by disasters related to natural hazards through the provision of multi-purpose cash assistance as part of the rapid response mechanism assistance package.

title: Supporting the Protection of Internally Displaced Persons, Migrants and Host Communities
description: Overlapping crisis and conflict in Yemen for over six years threatens to push Yemen to the brink in 2021. According to the Yemen Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) over 20.7 million people need some form of humanitarian and protection assistance. Of these some 4 million are facing protracted displacement or facing repeat and renewed displacement as hostilities continue risking loss of life, loss of basic means of survival, and exacerbation of protection risks as safety nets, while social support mechanisms are compromised. Through this project, IOM seeks to maintain and expand protection support with a focus on Marib, Aden, Sana'a, as well as southern Hudaydah and southern Taizz. Specifically, IOM intends to provide protection support in Marib, southern Taiz and southern Hodeida where internally displaced persons' needs and the potential for new and repeat displacements are high, while access to protection services is extremely limited. In addition to the widespread humanitarian needs evident across conflict-affected communities in Yemen, humanitarian needs are also prevalent among migrant communities. IOM is seeking resources to expand its migrant response programme to provide humanitarian and protection support to migrants, in the form of humanitarian assistance, screening and return support through IOM's Voluntary Humanitarian Returns programme.

title: Global Health Supply Chain - Procurement and Supply Management (GSHC-PSM) IDIQ - Family Planning/Reproductive Health (PRH) Task Order
description: Building on decades of USAIDs work procuring health commodities and strengthening supply chains, the Global Health Supply Chain-Procurement and Supply Management project is working to transform global and national supply chains for health commodities. The project integrates two former USAID programs into one efficient supply chain that serves many of the worlds most vulnerable and difficult-to-reach communities. The project is designed to meet todays critical global health challenges  eliminating HIV and AIDS, providing universal malaria coverage, and helping women meet their family planning and reproductive health needs. By bringing together advanced technical solutions, a team of highly qualified experts, and proven commercial processes and principles, USAID Global Health Supply Chain works to reduce costs and increase efficiencies in global and national supply chains. In addition to optimizing supply chains, the project is strengthening national supply chain systems and fostering collaboration among supply chain stakeholders worldwide.

title: Provision of Lifesaving Humanitarian Assistance through Comprehensive Site Management and Coordination Services in Displacement Sites in Ma’rib and Al Hodeidah, Yemen
description: To address the urgent needs of the most vulnerable populations in displacement sites across Yemen, IOM provides essential camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) activities across 53 displacement sites, hosting a total of 161,370 internally displaced persons (IDPs) or 31,207 households in Ma'rib and Al Hodeidah. The intervention is strengthening IDPs' access to lifesaving services and safe and dignified living conditions for people living in IDP-hosting sites and surrounding areas. IOM's CCCM field teams spearhead the coordination of IOM's multisectoral, integrated response within displacement sites, which both promotes a holistic approach to site management and reduces gaps in urgently needed services. To promote localization, IOM trains and equips community camp committees to respond to gaps in services, mitigate the impact of fires and floods, and address site care and maintenance.

title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (DSS MHPSS)
description: The Dutch Surge Support – Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (DSS MHPSS) programme aims to provide relevant expertise to set up coordination structures to provide mental health and psychosocial support during natural disasters and emergencies caused by armed conflict, violence and influx of refugees.A request for support during or shortly after a humanitarian crisis can be submitted by international humanitarian organisations, such as WHO, IOM, and UNHCR. title: Provision of Rapid Financial Assistance to Vulnerable Households in Yemen
description: The project has the objective to provide immediate livelihood assistance to vulnerable households to meet urgent needs. Project activities will support vulnerable, crisis affected families who are not able to meet their basic needs, through direct cash assistance to provide an immediate boost to local economies and to contribute to improved livelihood conditions, that will ultimately support them in meeting their most urgent needs. Through this approach, the project will empower local communities and contribute towards reducing reliance on external aid. This project will directly support 1,690 vulnerable, crisis affected individuals (and another 10,140 members of their households) to have improved access to basic goods and services in the short term while simultaneously supporting long term livelihood opportunities for people in need.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants in Yemen
description: Since the escalation of conflict in March 2015, Yemen continues to face the world's largest humanitarian crisis. In 2021, more than 20 million people are in need (two-thirds of the population), over 12 million of whom are in acute need of humanitarian assistance (Yemen Humanitarian Needs Overview 2021). Migrants are amongst the most marginalized, excluded, and vulnerable groups of people in need in Yemen and face considerable xenophobic and discriminatory treatment. The ongoing crisis and conflict, combined with the hardening attitudes of authorities against migrants, has increased migrants? exposure to abuse and violence. Through this project, IOM aims to contribute to address the urgent needs of migrants on the move or stranded in Yemen. IOM is targeting vulnerable migrants with urgent protection support (including emergency assistance) and healthcare services through static Migrant Response Points and mobile teams. IOM is also contributing to informing the overall humanitarian and protection response by employing its Flow Monitoring activities, through its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) programme.

title: Providing Life-Saving Humanitarian Assistance to the Most Vulnerable and Contributing to Reduced Aid Dependency in Yemen
description: Although the UN-brokered truce has brought a period of reduced conflict driven displacement to Yemen, the impact of years of destruction of remains undeniable. The proposed multisectoral intervention ensures conflict-affected populations in Ma’rib, Al Hodeidah, Ibb and Taiz have access to core services that contribute to safe and dignified living conditions and meet household needs. The intervention not only addresses these needs in the short term but also simultaneously contributes to a progressive reduction of aid dependency through integrating more sustainable solutions to Shelter and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) needs and providing key data to inform transitional programming as actors look towards durable solutions. The activities implemented under this action are further complimented by IOM protection and health interventions under other initiatives that provide critical health and protection services to vulnerable populations. IOM is utilizing its direct implementation modality and resulting strong field presence to ensure coordination with partners and local authorities to avoid duplication and ensure synergies for an effective response.

title: Supporting Food Security via the Rapid Provision of Multipurpose Cash Assistance and Health Services in Yemen
description: Under this intervention, IOM is providing one off multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) and health services with an aim to contribute to reduced food insecurity for crisis-affected populations in Al Hodeidah and Taiz governorates.

title: Provision Of Life-Saving Multi-Sectoral Assistance To Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities in Yemen
description: After more than eight years of conflict, the humanitarian needs continued to worsen across Yemen, especially for families living in protracted displacement and close to frontlines. There are 2,302,346 internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 1,240,944 IDP returnees in 13 governorates in the south of Yemen. In 2022, conflict-related reasons were still reported as a main driver of displacement and the needs of IDPs were aggravated by a weakened economy, rains and flooding, and fuel shortages. Vulnerable communities are likely to resort to negative coping mechanisms. Urgent support is needed, through an integrated evidence-based approach, for vulnerable households to purchase critical items and services in line with their needs; have access to safe water, health and sanitation services; and receive specialized and general protection and camp coordination and camp management services. \n \nIn line with an ongoing Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance funded project, as well as Yemen’s 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan and the International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s 2023 Crisis Response Plan, the Organization is contributing towards alleviating immediate suffering of food insecure populations with timely and high impact multi-sectoral interventions, as well as complementary interventions, such as assessments through the DTM, that are crucial for informing the integrated response.

title: Provision of Integrated Protection and Life-Saving Health Services to Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Yemen
description: The humanitarian situation in Yemen has led to considerable suffering across the country. An estimated 4.3 million internally displaced persons, 300,000 migrants, refugees and asylum seekers and millions of conflict-affected host community members are caught in the midst of an active armed conflict where the most basic resources are not available to ensure safety, dignity or protection. Fighting has exacerbated high-risk coping mechanisms, stalled development gains made in the years preceding and driven the country to the brink of famine. \n \nThe International Organization for Migration (IOM) and its partners are providing integrated life-saving health and protection support that prioritizes the most vulnerable migrants in Yemen at disembarkation points, along transit routes and hubs, and in locations where migrants are stranded or trapped as a result of conflict. IOM is also providing the wider humanitarian community in Yemen with greater access to information and strategies on how to better support migrants in this complicated and dynamic operational context. While migrant needs will be prioritized under this action, IOM is provide vulnerable internally displaced persons, host community members, and other vulnerable populations in Yemen with critically needed protection and health support, ensuring equal access for all population groups if/when they are encountered.

title: Rehabilitation And Operation of Ta'iz Humanitarian Hub
description: In this 12-month project, IOM proposes to support with the rehabilitation of the humanitarian hub within the first six months of the project and the operation of the hub for the following six months. The humanitarian hub, which has been informally approved by local authorities, is providing secure and safe office and accommodation services to humanitarian partners - facilities required to operate in Ta’iz.

title: Provide Based Needs Protection and Medical Assistance to the Yemenis Affected Populations, Returnees, and Migrants in Yemen Yemen
description: Due to the escalation of violent events and the constant shifts in fighting along frontlines between the conflicting parties, Yemen has plunged into one of the most severe and large-scale humanitarian crises presently experienced in the world. With over three years since the conflict escalated, Yemenis are still struggling with the deterioration of economic situation; the already precarious humanitarian situation has continued to deteriorate as a result of damage to civilian infrastructure and the disruption of what were already threadbare basic services. \n \nThe proposed intervention is geared to contribute to the strengthening of capacities, awareness, and direct assistance for a greater protection and wellbeing of the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Yemen and to the Yemeni returnees from aboard. Through this intervention, IOM is planning to implement a series of actions aimed at reducing suffering, mortality, and morbidity among communities.

title: Responding to Urgent Needs of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Yemen with Shelter and Cash Assistance
description: In line with the overall allocation strategy to improve living conditions and local integration for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Yemen who do not wish to relocate, IOM is providing transitional shelter, shelter rehabilitation support, and multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) under this intervention.

title: Protection of Vulnerable Migrants in Sa’dah Governorate (RMMS), Pillar 1
description: Through this project, IOM aims to reduce the morbidity, mortality and suffering of migrants and protect migrants along the northern border of Yemen in Sa’dah governorate through the provision of multisectoral lifesaving assistance and specialized protection services to migrants on the move in Sa’dah governorate. IOM will target an estimated 14,533 individuals with case management, support for gender-based violence (GBV) cases, establishment of safe spaces, integrated protection and health interventions - including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) -, emergency migrants' protection assistance, and awareness raising about protection risks and available services.

title: Yemen: Multisectoral Crisis Response 2023
description: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen, as result of more than eight years of conflict, has left millions grappling to meet their most basic needs. Under the proposed intervention, IOM in Yemen is implementing multisectoral activities to address life-saving needs of vulnerable internally displaced persons, migrants, and host community members. In addition, IOM seeks to support target individuals to transition from emergency to recovery conditions, via programming that restores access to basic services.

title: Strengthening Response and Prevention of Disease Outbreak in Shabwah , Reserve Allocation 8
description: Through this project, IOM is scaling up essential Health and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services in underserved areas in Yemen to support the urgent prevention and response to water-related and communicable disease outbreaks in the Radum and Habban districts in Shabwah. IOM is ensuring direct assistance in acute watery diarrhoea (AWD)/Cholera hotspots for an estimated 26,340 affected internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities, with specific modalities to reach migrants who are one of the most vulnerable groups in Yemen and disproportionally suffer from lack of access to basic services.

title: Addressing Urgent Water Supply Needs in Al Makha City, Reserve Allocation 9
description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is bringing critically needed freshwater to an estimated 120,000 host community members and internally displaced persons living in Al Makha City (Ta’iz). IOM is finalizing the long awaited Al Makha City water supply scheme by installing the final 8.5 km of the transmission line, completing efforts of nearly two years to bring fresh water to individuals who are currently utilizing highly salinated water sources. The nine-month intervention includes the installation of the transmission line via a local contractor, construction of 5 inspection rooms to support monitoring and maintenance of the system, provision and installation of six borehole monitoring devices to measure water depletion, and installation of an automatic chlorine dosing system to ensure proper disinfection of the water supply. As part of efforts to ensure sustainability of the water supply scheme, IOM is providing capacity building to the Local Water and Sanitation Corporation on effective chlorination techniques. Further, community hygiene promoters are being trained to disseminate key messages on safe water practices and the responsible use of water resources.

title: Ehancing Access To Essential WASH And Health Services For Conflict Affected Populations In Yemen
description: Due to years of conflict in Yemen, millions of individuals are faced with increased challenges in accessing basic services. Internally displaced populations (IDPs) and migrants are often disproportionally affected by lack of water, sanitation, hygiene (WASH), and health services due to living in remote and often under-resourced settlements, and other barriers such as cost and availability. \n \nUnder this project, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is enhancing access to safe water through the rehabilitation and expansion of water supply systems that will cover the immediate water needs of an estimated 120,000 people, including IDPs and host communities in Yemen. Complementing this activity, IOM is hosting various hygiene promotion activities and providing community members with technical skills trainings to fill WASH-related labour gaps and strengthen community ownership and maintenance of the water systems.

title: Provide Engineering Technical Support and Assistance for the Supervision of Construction/Renovation Works of the OCHA Office Located at Khormakser, Aden, Yemen
description: OCHA has hired a company to renovate, repair, and strengthen the security of its office facility in Aden (the "Works"). IOM Yemen is helping/supporting with technical supervision, and the contractor is handling all technical activities. OCHA has hired IOM to oversee and monitor the work in order to make sure that the terms and conditions of the agreement, as well as all of its appendices, are followed in execution by both OCHA and the vendor.

title: Providing Life-Saving Humanitarian Assistance to the Most Vulnerable and Contributing to Reduced Aid Dependency in Yemen
description: Although the de facto United Nations-brokered truce has brought a period of reduced conflict driven displacement to Yemen, the impact of years of destruction and continued instability remains undeniable. The proposed multisectoral intervention ensures conflict-affected populations in Ma’rib, Al Hodeidah, Ibb and Ta’iz have access to core services that contribute to safe and dignified living conditions and meet household needs. The intervention not only addresses these needs in the short term but simultaneously contributes to a progressive reduction of aid dependency through integrating more sustainable solutions and providing key data to inform transitional programming as actors look towards durable solutions. As a result of the proposed water, sanitation and hygiene; camp coordination and camp management; multi-purpose cash assistance; and shelter and non-food item activities, over internally displaced persons and conflict affected host community members are supported by interventions in 86 sites supported by the International Organization for Migration and other areas where displaced populations outside of sites (and surrounding host community) are in critical need of assistance.

title: Provision of Comprehensive Protection and Health Services to Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Yemen
description: In 2024, approximately 1.8 million people residing in and around internally displaced persons (IDP) sites require camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) support, reflecting a decrease from 2023 largely due to insecurity and lack of services. As Yemen remains on the transit route for many trying to access Saudi Arabia and Oman, an estimated 380,077 migrants, refugees and asylum seekers will need humanitarian assistance and protection. Reduced funding has strained partner capacities, jeopardizing monitoring, improvements and progress toward solutions for site populations. Consistent limitations in access to vital services have further eroded people's coping abilities. While the conflict, food insecurity and political instability affect both the Yemeni and non-Yemeni populations, the overwhelming needs for the latter are protection-based due to alarmingly high levels of vulnerability. Through this action, the International Organization for Migration and its partners are providing protection and health assistance to migrants, IDPs and host communities in Yemen through the provision of integrated life-saving health and protection support.

title: Comprehensive Multi-Sectoral Assistance To Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities in Yemen
description: After more than eight years of conflict, the humanitarian needs continue to worsen across Yemen, especially for families living in protracted displacement and close to frontlines. Based on an Area Assessment (Mobility Tracking) conducted from July to September 2023, the International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) estimates there are 2,791,603 internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 1,878,906 IDP returnees in 13 governorates in the south of Yemen. Conflict-related reasons were still reported as a main driver of displacement and the needs of IDPs were aggravated by a weakened economy, rains, flooding and fuel shortages. IOM is contributing towards the alleviation of immediate suffering of food insecure populations in Yemen with timely and high impact multi-sectoral interventions, as well as complementary interventions that are crucial for informing the integrated response. This includes assessments through the DTM, providing water, sanitation and hygiene solutions, multi-purpose cash assistance, healthcare assistance, shelter assistance, non-food items, nutrition services; strengthening social and protection structures to mitigate, prevent and respond to risks and reduce reliance on negative coping mechanisms; and enhancing site coordination, community participation and care/maintenance at IDP collective sites.

title: Improving Sanitation Services for Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities in Ma'rib, Yemen
description: In line with the National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Cluster Strategy, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) seeks to contribute to safe and dignified living conditions by improving access to sanitation facilities and waste management services in target areas. The proposed intervention is in line with IOM’s WASH Strategy in Yemen to implement solutions that are immediate, scalable and sustainable. IOM aims to support 185,178 individuals (direct and indirect beneficiaries), including direct support to 44,119 internally displaced persons, 2,937 host community members and 542 refugees under this intervention. IOM proposes to increase access to safe sanitation services in Ma’rib for the most vulnerable crisis affected households through the construction and rehabilitation of latrines and cesspits, as well as support in faecal sludge and solid waste collection and garbage dump site improvement across sites in Ma’rib, also increasing local capacity to provide sanitation services.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants And IDPs In Yemen
description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) aims to contribute to addressing the urgent needs of 93,650 internally displaced people (IDP), 400 members of host communities and 11,250 migrants in Yemen. IOM is targeting internally displaced crisis-affected households and migrants by providing access to safe and sustainable sanitation and hygiene solutions, lifesaving health services and mental health and psychosocial support, with increased awareness of acute watery diarrhea/cholera prevention practices, and delivering one-off multipurpose cash assistance allowing to increase the capacity of food insecure households to meet their basic needs. This intervention also benefits crisis-affected households and host community population by enabling their access to enhanced safety and dignified living conditions through lifesaving shelter and non-food items assistance, while also improving essential site management, sustainable prevention and mitigation of hazards for people residing in IDP hosting sites. In line with the key objectives of the Regional Migrant Response Plan for the Horn of Africa and Yemen, IOM is facilitating the movement and voluntary informed and dignified return of vulnerable migrants stranded in Yemen to their countries of origin. IOM is also contributing towards informing the overall humanitarian and protection response by employing its flow monitoring activities, through its Displacement Tracking Matrix programme.

title: Water for Peace in Yemen: Strengthening the Role of Women in Water Conflict Resolution and Resource Management across the HDPN
description: The project will address the immediate risks of water scarcity and conflict whilst at the same time working on the establishment of adaptive pathways to manage and mitigate the risks of flooding and environmental degradation. IOM will contribute to improved capacity among target communities in Hadramawt to mitigate and manage water-related conflicts, with an emphasis on infrastructure rehabilitation and establishment of community-led conflict resolution mechanisms. IOM will also support long-term resilience of target communities by providing livelihood opportunities.

title: IOM – Multi Country Humanitarian Assistance – CAP 2022
description: The ongoing conflict in Yemen has continued to exacerbate humanitarian needs. Populations throughout the country, among whom the most vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs), migrants, returnees and conflict affected host community members, are in dire need of humanitarian assistance. In order to ensure the most vulnerable receive assistance that meets their most pressing needs, timely, accurate and reliable data is required to inform the humanitarian response, ultimately ensuring assistance provided is effective. With the support of the Government of Canada, IOM in Yemen continues to provide humanitarian actors with critical and timely information on IDPs and returnees to support an informed humanitarian response. IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) is developing a range of information products including Rapid Displacement Tracking (RDT), Flow Monitoring Registry (FMR), Flow Monitoring Survey (FMS), Intention Surveys and Area Assessment (AA) under mobility tracking reports, as well as datasets and dashboards to help prioritize humanitarian interventions and transition and recovery activities in Yemen.

title: Mobility Tracking through Area Assessments in Yemen
description: Under this 12-month project, IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) aims to continue improving on its data collection and products to provide the humanitarian response with high-quality information on trends and needs in Yemen mainly in the north of Yemen, where information gaps are the largest. IOM is carrying out two rounds of the Area Assessment across 15 governorates across the north of Yemen. The Area Assessment aims to quantify the presence of population categories, reasons for displacement or migration, length of displacement or migration and needs with defined location, with a frequency that captures mobility dynamics.

title: Area-Based Programmes for Durable Development Solutions to Displacement in Aden, Marib, Taiz, and Lahj: Building Local Capacity and Experience to Implement Yemen’s 2013 National Policy on IDPs.
description: This Joint Project by UNDP, UNHCR, IOM, and FAO (the PUNOs) will support the Government of Yemen’s national authorities (the Executive Unit for IDPs) and local authorities to design and implement gender and conflict-sensitive area-based, development-oriented durable solutions to displacement by inducing systemic change through 1. Developing joint assessments of the situations, needs, and solutions preferred by IDPs and host communities, while building the capacity of local Government to shape evidence-based innovative investment and to measure progress; 2. Supporting national and local authorities' efforts to facilitate the integration of IDPs through integrated policy innovation, legal reform, and institutional change; and 3. Testing innovative measures to amplify locally tailored, community-led, needs-based development solutions in pilot locations in Aden, Marib, Taiz, and Lahj, drawing lessons for eventual scaling up.

title: Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction and Surge Support (DRRS)
description: RVO provides water-related experts through its Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction & Surge Support (DRRS) programme. DRRS aims to prevent and reduce the impact of water and climate-related disasters worldwide and increase the resilience of affected areas and populations.The DRRS programme operates in all disaster management cycle phases: mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery. Foreign governments and humanitarian actors can request support. Every intervention is tailor-made. DRRS can assemble a team with relevant stakeholders and (local) experts based on the challenge and expertise needed.

title: Yemen 2023 - WFP HUM 2022-2025 UNHAS central fund
description:
The current contribution provides Sida funding to the World Food Programme (WFP) to support the organisation’s humanitarian response to acute food insecurity in countries such as Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Cuba, Democratic Republic of the Congo, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Guinea, Haiti, Honduras, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Myanmar, Niger, Nigeria, Palestine, Somalia, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine, Venezuela and Zambia.

The support amounts to a total of SEK 2,307,500,000 over the agreement period, including SEK 257,000,000 to reach crisis-affected populations in 12 countries in 2026.

The intervention also includes support to the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) to facilitate access for humanitarian actors to people in need of assistance in areas that cannot be reached by other means.

title: DRRS Yemen 2024 – WHO IPC/WASH Specialist
description: Assignment at the request of the WHO Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)/Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH).In the northern governorates of Yemen, an Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) has been declared with, and rapid increase in cases over the last 2 weeks (more than 2,000 suspected cases in week 11 and 12, 2024 with 28 associated death). There is also an increase in confirmed cholera cases in the Southern governorates and response will be scaled up.WHO WASH response needs to scale up quickly, to given the rapid increase of cases and weak WASH capacities in the country. An experienced international WASH officer is urgently required to support development detailed and prioritized WASH response plan for the North and supervise the implementation of WHO WASH response. The outbreak response is significantly underfunded and no funds for surge support consultants are available.

title: DRRS 2024 UNDP Yemen Hydrological study Tuban
description: The objective of this study is to analyze the hydrological characteristics of the Tuban (sub-)catchments to understand the overall water availability and utilization patterns within the (sub-)catchments.The study conducts a comprehensive assessment of the water balance and hydrological processes for the Tuban (sub-)catchments. The study should be implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Water and Environment (MoWE) and its affiliated body of National Water Resources Authority (NWRA) which are responsible for water resource planning and monitoring, enforcement of water rights, and regulating of drilling activities for different uses.The study should also engage with the Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Fisheries (MoAIF) and its offices/branches in Taiz and Lahj, which is responsible for the development of irrigation water management plans, allocation of storage water to farmers based on the results of the studies, preparation of inventories for irrigation structures and their inflows and outflows, and preparation of mitigation plans of flashfloods.

title: DRRS 2025 UNICEF Yemen Groundwater Remote Sensing Taizz
description: The objective of this study is to assess the groundwater resources that can be used for the water supply of Taizz City through remote sensing and Georgraphic Information System (GIS) analysis to produce preliminary groundwater potential maps. The geographical area for these studies will cover the whole Upper Wadi Rasyan to be used in a different project to develop an integrated water resources management plan for Taizz City. The expert will then identify high potential areas for further groundwater investigations and suggest appropriate and realistic methods to carry out these investigations.All data used to carry out the tasks, including geospatial data, models and maps created, will be handed over to the Yemen' Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) and UNICEF at the end of the contract to be used in future projects.The study shall include - but is not limited to - the following components:•\tAssessment of the Upper Wadi Rasyan watershed: •\tDevelop a preliminary groundwater potential map using GIS analysis of existing datasets, remote sensing for groundwater potential and groundwater pollution indicators;•\tIdentify high potential areas for further groundwater investigations and suggest appropriate and realistic methods to carry out these investigations.

title: Female Judges Training in MENA Region
description: This tailor-made “Access to Justice – Female Judiciary in Yemen and the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region” programme aims to better equip the current and potential female judiciary to navigate the many challenges and gender biases that hinder female professionals in the judiciary in Yemen and the MENA region. The training programme should be designed to help aspiring female professionals develop the critical leadership skills to influence, persuade, empower, and mentor other women. Those preparing to transition into more senior roles will be able to deepen their leadership knowledge by reflecting on crucible moments and approaches to challenging situations.The training programme should serve those aiming to overcome gender barriers in the judiciary, and grow both within their careers and organisation. Next to leadership skills, the training will also focus on enhancing the participant’s knowledge on Dutch and international judicial processes and procedures which should in turn help to inspire and apply lessons learnt in their own contexts.

title: Tailor-made Training Water Management – Desalination Yemen
description: Yemen is a country in conflict in which water resources are scarce. The scarcity of water is a driver of conflict and can lead to (internal) migration. Water is an essential basic requirement for economic development and reconstruction in Yemen. In order to support a sustainable water source for its people, the Yemeni Ministry of Water and Energy (MoWE) seeks to establish sustainable desalination plants with a starting point in Aden, one of the governorates without natural water resources. With an overwhelming support from the donor community, the MoWE is in need of a strategy and enhanced knowledge on determining how to best approach this. Through this project, MoWE civil servants will follow a training in the Netherlands to visit both governmental and private institutions with regards to desalination. Next to the study visit, an important element of the training is the development of a roadmap to navigate the sustainable development of desalination plants. Once the project is finalised, MoWE will be able to follow the steps in the roadmap to ultimately provide its people with a safe and reliable water source.

title: Yemen 2021 - NRC Humanitarian Country programmes 2021-2025
description:
NRC has applied as well to Sida for funding of 364.5 million SEK to carry out “the Humanitarian Programme for 2021” in 26 humanitarian crisis settings: Afghanistan, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Honduras, El Salvador, Mexico, Palestine, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania/Burundi, Uganda, Venezuela, Yemen. The application includes provision of 40 million SEK to replenish the Rapid Response Mechanism funding instrument and 7 individual projects for method, capacity-building and coordination.
The intervention’s tentative total budget is 4 263 200 000 Norwegian krona (NOK), that the organisation is financing with Sida’s funding in a proportion of 8% approximately. Other donors, like the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, DG ECHO, UNHCR, etc. are the largest contributors, besides a dozen of other donors in agreement with NRC. Sida provides NRC with the opportunity to allocate resources flexibly within individual country programmes (Programme-Based Approach – PBA).
NRC's catalytic support for coordination and capacity building contributes greatly to the link between humanitarian aid, development and peace. NRC's advocacy work and activities enable, at least contribute to, sustainable solutions for refugees and displaced people in a significant way in cooperation with other actors. In the long run, the NRC will reduce humanitarian needs. The NRC prioritizes self-sufficiency in its programs. The NRC's analysis capability, not least through its Internal Displacement Monitoring Center (IDMC), is an advantage for relevant programming according to the nexus orientations. Among the 26 crises in NRC's portfolio that Sida prioritizes, there are 15 where Sida implements Sweden's development strategies in synergy with humanitarian aid.
Sida’s contribution to NRC for 2022 will cover around 6.5% of NRC’s total financial requirements of the supported programmes and projects. It will provides humanitarian services to almost 9 million persons (53% female). HUM adds 50 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Ukraine benefiting 90,000 people with protection, shelter, WaSH and cash assistance. Decision 5 April. Amendment nr. 5.
HUM adds 7.5 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in Cameroon from the 2022 mid-year allocation (food security, legal advice for 600 households/4200 individuals in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga). Decision 9 June 2022. Contract amendment No 6.
HUM adds 10 MSEK for NRC's 2022 country programme in South Sudan from the end-of-the-year allocation. Decision 16 November 2022 nr 2022-002341. Contract amendment No 7.
NRC targets 7.7 million unique beneficiaries in total within Sida-funded humanitarian programmes in 2023, (52% female), who will receive protection and humanitarian services from NRC: Education, WASH, Shelter and settlement, Food security and livelihoods, including multi-purpose cash assistance, Protection, Legal assistance, Humanitarian mediation (community-based peace-building). Advocacy and support to humanitarian coordination and durable solution to displacements working groups in the field are part of NRC's engagement that Sida is funding. NRC's annual budget 2023 in the settings and thematics prioritized by Sida amounts to 5620 million Norwegian crowns in total. Sida's share weighs so far 8% of it: NRC's third largest donor whose cumulated 2021-2025 grant is 80% softly earmarked (programme-based approach) and 34% multi-year.
Earlier granted multi-year funding for 2023 was disbursed in January (52 MSEK) in support to continued humanitarian operations in DR Congo, Mali and Nigeria with strong emphasis on emergency response.
