title: SRHR Yemen
description:
Context Analysis Yemen Sept 2020

The war that started at the beginning of 2015 has escalated over time. It is impossible to give a brief and complete overview that includes all the nuances and complexities. The war between the Houthi movement and the internationally recognized government of President Hadi is the result of a failed political transition after the Arab Spring in 2011. In the meantime the Houthi movement has taken the capital of Sanaa and is still expanding its zone of control. The international recognized government -  that is in  exile in Saudi Arabia – is losing territory over time. Saudi Arabia is supporting the Hadi government. Iran is supporting the Houthi movement. The war is now fragmenting. The main warring parties are fragmenting regionally and locally in different groups. There are now more warring factions and frontlines than ever. Also aerial bombardments still occur. The escalation of the war has devastating humanitarian consequences for the population.

The crisis in Yemen is the worst in the world, and all indicators point towards a massive deterioration. There is no other country in the world with a higher percentage of people in need of some sort of humanitarian assistance or protection in order to survive. 80% of Yemen’s population need our help – there is no other country with comparable statistics. Half of all of the people in Yemen are what we call acutely vulnerable, meaning that they will not make it without the assistance we provide them. There is no other country on earth where half the population is acutely vulnerable. 
•	2/3 of the entire population wakes up hungry everyday 
•	1/4 of the population is malnourished 

The UN-run humanitarian operation in Yemen is the largest UN humanitarian operation in the world – 11 UN agencies and 215 frontline partners are providing all kinds of aid and assistance throughout the country. One of the largest food programs in UN history is being run in Yemen, with the World Food Programme delivering food to 14 million people – half of the Yemeni population. We reached close to 11 million people with healthcare before the pandemic, and we were reaching 9 million people with water and sanitation before the funding crisis. 
The crisis has gotten significantly worse throughout the war. While Yemen was always poor, but with every year of war the number of people humanitarian assistance has increased. 
From 15 million people in need of help when the war started, next year 16 million, after that 20 million and now 25 million. 
The crisis has multiple waves: 
- Yemen has experienced the worst cholera outbreak in modern history 
- Famine 
- Once-in-a-generation flooding 
- Unchecked, unmitigated spread of COVID-19, with probably the highest case mortality rate in the world 
- Once again a famine is appearing.

The situation is going to get worse until the warring parties put down arms. 

Funding and operational crisis 
The International Community (IC) has a funding crisis and an operational crisis too.
While commending the generosity of donors throughout the war, this year the I.C only received USD $1 billion of the $3.2 billion needed. 
The UN has 41 major programmes, and the past 4 months we have been forced to shut down or reduce 15 of the programmes. Without additional funding the next few weeks, another 26 programmes face the same risk. The consequences will of course be death and suffering. 
The operational crisis referred to has to do with our abilities as humanitarians to deliver assistance in accordance with the four core humanitarian principles. These are the principles of humanity, independence, impartiality and neutrality. 
Most of the problems we face are in northern Yemen. 
When faced with cases where the IC simply cannot deliver in accordance with those principles, it is forced to roll back the assistance it is providing until it is able to manage the level of risk we are facing. There is no more restrictive, non-permissive operating environment in the world than the one in Yemen.

description: Based up selection criteria following cluster guidelines, the Health Facilities will be selected for rehabilitation. description: Overall objective: In response Cordaid/ YWBOD will contribute to increased access to basic services including food improving nutritional status of some of the most vulnerable people in Yemen.\n\nSpecific Objective: Conflict affected men, women and children in target districts (Sallah and Almaqatrah) in Taiz and Lahj have access to food and hygiene information and items.

title: Yemen Joint Response 2022-2023
description: - The rehabilitation of HFs is targeting children, women and men of all age groups that are in need of improved access to health services. However, as we target HFs with SRH services, we focus on women of reproductive age and children under 5. Both groups are disproportionately affected by the different crisis and are bearing the brunt of the conflict, high levels of food insecurity and malnutrition. They are also more likely to seek health services and prone to disease. HFs are selected in consultation with SCMCHA and MoH, based on set criteria. - Treatment of people with NCD is targeting people with a non-communicable disease. Because of the years of conflict half of the HFs are not functioning and medication is scarce/ unavailable and for many, also unaffordable. Also, very little funding is made available to address the needs of people with NCD, making them extra vulnerable and in high need. Approx 10% of the people with NCD do have a disability as well as a consequence of their disease. They will be specifically targeted. Patients are selected in consultation with the HFs. Yamaan and HFs will select a number of NCDs, depending on data and recurrence of the NCD. Vulnerability criteria will be maintained for the selection of beneficiaries. \n- MHPSS counselling and treatment: unmet psychological needs can widen the cause deterioration in mental health, increase dependency on others for assistance, and decrease quality of life and affect the whole family's well-being. These adverse outcomes can have broad social and psychological implications for individuals, families, and communities. Especially when it concerns women, as families detain them to hide the shame. The project will therefore focus its MHPSS staff training efforts in HFs where SRH services are being provided, directly targeting women (PLW/women of reproductive age). \n- Persons with disabilities must be able to access humanitarian assistance that provided by Cordaid, Yamaan, and FCDF on the same terms as other members of the population. Cordaid, Yamaan, and FCDF will identify and reduce barriers and risks that face people with disability. Cordaid, Yamaan, and FCDF will use a rights-based inclusive approach to recognize the capacity of persons with disabilities and contribute to the humanitarian response as active participants.

reporting: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
title: Pledge for the Salvaging of the Decrepit Oil Tanker FSO Safer in Yemen.
description: The FSO Safer is moored in the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen. No maintenance has been carried out on the vessel since 2015 and there is an imminent risk of a catastrophic spill or explosion. More than a million barrels of oil could leak out into the surrounding sea. Such an event would destroy vulnerable and unique ecosystems. The fishing industry on which hundreds of thousands of Yemenis depend for their livelihoods would come to a complete standstill. Humanitarian aid, on which 70% of Yemenis depend, would no longer be able to reach the country’s ports. A disaster with the Safer would mean an unprecedented deepening of the already critical humanitarian crisis in Yemen. The UN has brokered a viable plan to salvage the oil from the FSO Safer and store it in a safe replacement vessel. This plan has the support of all parties involved. With the present activity, the Netherlands supports the UN in the execution of this plan to prevent a disaster from happening.

title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI)  - RYADH - 2017 to 2018
description: The Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) supports small projects proposed and implemented by local organizations in Yemen. The CFLI contributes to the overall goal of reducing poverty by providing funding for small projects that offer direct social, economic or technical assistance to local populations.  The CFLI retains the same broad themes set out since 2016, which align closely with the 6 pillars of the Feminist International Assistance Policy. This allows flexibility to respond to and focus on themes relevant to local needs. The six thematic priorities include: (1) contributing to inclusive governance, including diversity and LGBTQ2, democracy, human rights and the rule of law; (2) contributing to gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls; (3) contributing to peace and security, with a focus on conflict prevention and building peace; (4) contributing to growth that works for everyone, including women’s economic rights, decent jobs and entrepreneurship, investing in the poorest and most vulnerable, and safeguarding economic gains; (5) contributing to environment and climate action, focusing on adaptation, mitigation and  water management; and (6) contributing to human dignity, covering health, education and nutrition.

reporting: Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada (DFATD)
title: Emergency Assistance in Specific Countries - International Organization for Migration 2018
description: January 2018 - This grant represents Canada's support to the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in the following countries:  Afghanistan, Bangladesh, DRC, CAR, Libya, Sudan, South Sudan and Yemen. IOM provides humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees, migrants, and host communities. IOM provides assistance in multiple sectors, including protection, shelter, emergency non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene services, livelihoods and camp coordination and management.  With the support of Canada and other donors, IOM is facilitating access to essential relief items and adequate living conditions for crisis-affected populations as well as vulnerable populations, including IDPs, refugees, migrants, returnees, and host communities. Project activities include: (1) providing emergency shelter kits, non-food items and multi-purpose cash; (2) coordinating camp management for internally displaced people in UN bases; (3) deploying mobile teams to remote locations where affected populations lack water, sanitation and hygiene services; (4) providing emergency water, sanitation and hygiene; (5) supporting humanitarian organizations by establishing lightweight camps in deep field locations and heavy base camps and national NGO support centres and providing common transport services of cargo for humanitarian organizations; (6) data collection including mapping of vulnerable populations at points of entry and at the district and community level for enhanced targeting and delivery of assistance; and (7) protection and gender mainstreaming across activities with provision for extremely vulnerable individuals including unaccompanied migrant children and single females.

title: UNFPA-UNICEF Joint Programme on the Elimination of Female Genital Mutilation
description: The UNFPA-UNICEF Joint Programme to Eliminate Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) contributes to ending female genital mutilation or cutting (FGM or cutting) by 2030 through accelerated collective and multi-sectoral action by mobilizing a broad spectrum of actors at community, national, regional and global levels. It is the largest global programme to accelerate the abandonment of this harmful traditional practice and thereby advance women’s and girls’ rights, health and well-being.  Project activities include: (1) providing capacity development (including comprehensive sexuality and life skills education) that promotes gender-equitable norms, including the eliminating FGM or cutting; (2) implementing an alternative rites of passage programme by supported communities; (3) supporting medical and paramedical schools to mainstream FGM or cutting into curricula training; (4) supporting institutions and systems (education, health, child protection) to integrate the prevention of and response to FGM or cutting in policies and plans; (5) creating a multi-sectoral evidence-based, gender-transformative FGM or cutting elimination policy or strategy; and (6) supporting the development of budgeted emergency preparedness and response and disaster risk reduction plans that integrate sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and harmful practices.  Direct beneficiaries are girls and women at risk of (68 million) or affected by (200 million) FGM or cutting, and their families, communities, local and national institutions, particularly in 17 targeted countries (Burkina Faso, Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Kenya, Mali, Mauritania, Nigeria, Senegal, Somalia, Sudan, Uganda and Yemen) and especially in hard-to-reach areas.

title: FSO Safer Oil Tanker Salvage Operation
description: This project seeks to prevent a catastrophic oil spill in the Red Sea. It aims to salvage and replace a decaying tanker off the coast of Yemen, near the port city of Hodeida. Production and offloading operations, suspended due to lengthy conflict in the area, prevented proper access and maintenance operations. This has resulted in the vessel decaying and loss of structural integrity. The tanker, FSO Safer, is at imminent risk of spilling, breaking apart or exploding. The UN has called on the international community to fund an emergency action plan to remove the oil from the tanker and replace the vessel. Project activities include: (1) providing ship-to-ship transfer of oil from the FSO Safer to the Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC); (2) providing tank-cleaning and demucking; and (3) replacing the FSO with a floating CALM Buoy, permanently attached to a VLCC lightly modified to be an FSO.

title: Yemen Economic Stabilisation Programme
description: he Yemen Economic Stabilisation (YES) Programme strengthens the Government of Yemen’s (GoY) capability to deliver essential, inclusive services by addressing core drivers of economic instability through targeted, politically informed technical assistance. Through a politically oriented and conflict sensitive approach, YES supports reforms in public financial management, monetary stability, electricity sector, and the financial sector, while creating conditions for private-sector investment and job creation. By stabilising essential GoY economic governance, the programme over time enhances the government’s credibility and legitimacy, maintaining a pathway to a political process, and reduces humanitarian needs. Beneficiaries include Yemeni citizens (particularly in GoY-controlled areas) and vulnerable households, as well as core economic institutions such as the Central Bank, Ministry of Finance, and energy authorities.

reporting: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
title: UNHCR operation in Yemen
description: Yemen remains one of the world's largest humanitarian crises. After seven years of devastating and unrelenting conflict, some 23.4 million Yemenis (73% of the country's population) depend on humanitarian assistance to survive, including 4.3 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). The country has the fourth-largest IDP population due to conflict in the world.   Escalation of conflict, ongoing insecurity, embargoes and a collapsed economy have pushed an estimated 80% of the population below the poverty line. The protection environment throughout the country remains dire, and civilians keep bearing the brunt of the conflict.   Yemen hosts 95,815 refugees and asylum-seekers, mainly from Somalia and Ethiopia. It remains the only country in the Arabian Peninsula signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and a geographic crossroad for migratory and transitory movements from the Horn of Africa and beyond.  UNHCR leads the Protection, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), and Shelter/Non-Food Items clusters as part of the inter-agency humanitarian response to assist those most in need in Yemen. In addition, UNHCR remains the only agency addressing the protection and well-being of refugees and asylum-seekers across the country. UNHCR's response focuses primarily on protection interventions, shelter support, CCCM services, cash assistance, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion projects, and comprehensive refugee response.  Today, the Operation has a well-established presence across the country. It covers most of its 22 governorates and 333 districts through its Country Office in Sana'a, a Sub-Office in Aden, field offices in Marib, Al-Hudaydah, Sa'ada and Ibb, and a field unit in Kharaz refugee camp in Lahj Governorate.   At this critical time, humanitarian action in Yemen and the support of the international community to save lives, alleviate suffering, and give a sense of dignity and hope to the displaced remain imperative.  This activity shows details of the UNHCR operation in Yemen for 2025 and future years including the budget, funding, expenditure and results. For specific details on the objectives of this operation, please use the document link "Strategy".

reporting: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
title: Promoting Inclusive Access to Justice in Yemen (PIAJY) - Phase II
description: Access to justice in Yemen remains elusive in all dimensions: people, problems, and processes. Justice deficits are affecting vulnerable people most: women, juveniles, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), Persons with Disabilities and Muhamasheen. Housing, Land, Property (HLP) problems are most salient. Justice processes for vulnerable people are near non-existent, as formal justice institutions have deteriorated further. People are resorting to informal, community-based justice for self-help: more accessible and affordable, but subject to patriarchal and gerontocratic dynamics, posing challenges to  inclusive justice. The project aims at 3 Outputs, focusing on “justice seekers” more than providers: 1) civil and property justice promoted, 2) gender and inclusive justice enhanced,  3) comprehensive detainee protection expanded. Building upon hybrid justice platforms fostered during the previous phase through a “justice ecosystems” approach, the project will work towards more inclusive A2J at three levels of services.

title: Capacity Building in desalination for Yemen's Water Sector
description: IHE Delft is providing capacity building in desalination to the Ministry of Water and Environment (MoWE) in Aden. This initiative is a follow up of the roadmap for desalination in Aden, which was developed by a delegation of the Yemeni Minister of MoWE & his team that visited IHE Delft in October 2024. The roadmap is key part of Aden's efforts to address water scarcity through the development of seawater desalination. IHE Delft, leveraging its expertise in this domain and experience in the Middle East region, is partnering with the Saudi Water Authority (SWA) to provide support to Yemeni water professionals in Aden, helping them to develop and improve their skills in seawater quality monitoring at training facilities provided by the Saudi Water Authority. IHE Delft will shortly sign an MoU with SWA for further collaboration as a consequence of this activity (but not as part of this activity).

reporting: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
title: UNHCR operation in Yemen (2024)
description: Yemen remains one of the world's largest humanitarian crises. After seven years of devastating and unrelenting conflict, some 23.4 million Yemenis (73% of the country's population) depend on humanitarian assistance to survive, including 4.3 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). The country has the fourth-largest IDP population due to conflict in the world.   Escalation of conflict, ongoing insecurity, embargoes and a collapsed economy have pushed an estimated 80% of the population below the poverty line. The protection environment throughout the country remains dire, and civilians keep bearing the brunt of the conflict.   Yemen hosts 95,815 refugees and asylum-seekers, mainly from Somalia and Ethiopia. It remains the only country in the Arabian Peninsula signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and a geographic crossroad for migratory and transitory movements from the Horn of Africa and beyond.  UNHCR leads the Protection, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), and Shelter/Non-Food Items clusters as part of the inter-agency humanitarian response to assist those most in need in Yemen. In addition, UNHCR remains the only agency addressing the protection and well-being of refugees and asylum-seekers across the country. UNHCR's response focuses primarily on protection interventions, shelter support, CCCM services, cash assistance, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion projects, and comprehensive refugee response.  Today, the Operation has a well-established presence across the country. It covers most of its 22 governorates and 333 districts through its Country Office in Sana'a, a Sub-Office in Aden, field offices in Marib, Al-Hudaydah, Sa'ada and Ibb, and a field unit in Kharaz refugee camp in Lahj Governorate.   At this critical time, humanitarian action in Yemen and the support of the international community to save lives, alleviate suffering, and give a sense of dignity and hope to the displaced remain imperative.  This activity shows details of the UNHCR operation in Yemen for 2024 and future years including the budget, funding, expenditure and results. For specific details on the objectives of this operation, please use the document link "Strategy".

reporting: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
title: Strengthening the scientific capacities of young Yemeni researchers by providing remote access to scientific knowledge, research infrastructure, laboratory facilities, data, and international scientific collaboration opportunities through Open Science and remote laboratory access mechanisms.
description:
Yemen's prolonged crisis has severely affected its higher education and scientific research systems, limiting the ability of universities and research institutions to generate knowledge, support innovation, and contribute to national recovery efforts. Young researchers face significant barriers, including limited access to scientific literature, research data, laboratory facilities, advanced analytical equipment, funding opportunities, and international scientific networks. These challenges have contributed to the isolation of the country's scientific community and constrained the development of evidence-based solutions to pressing national challenges such as water scarcity, food insecurity, climate change, environmental degradation, renewable energy, and disaster risk reduction.

The UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science and the UNESCO Remote Access to Lab Equipment initiative (UNESRALE), offer a practical mechanism for addressing one of the most critical gaps facing Yemeni researchers: access to modern scientific infrastructure. Through remote access technologies, researchers can utilize sophisticated laboratory equipment hosted by partner institutions worldwide without the need for costly travel or physical presence. This approach enables Yemeni scientists to conduct experiments, acquire technical skills, engage in international research collaborations, and contribute to high-quality scientific outputs despite the challenging national context.
 
Key Activities: 
	Improvement of access to Open Scientific Knowledge and Research Resources for Yemeni scientists.
	Remote access to international laboratory facilities through UNESRALE.

Key beneficiaries:
	Researchers, scientists, and academics from universities, research centers, and technical institutions. 
	Young professionals and students, particularly those pursuing STEM-related fields. 
Key partners: 
	Yemen National Commission.
	UNESCO Headquarters and Field Offices.
	Yemeni Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.
	Yemeni universities and research centers.
	UNESRALE partner laboratories and universities.
	International research organizations and scientific networks.
	Arab and Gulf universities and research institutions.

reporting: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
title: Supporting documentary heritage preservation in GCC and Yemen
description: Documentary heritage is a vital source of collective memory, cultural identity, and knowledge transmission. In Yemen, years of conflict have continued to place documentary heritage collections at risk due to physical deterioration, limited preservation capacities, insufficient documentation systems, and the absence of comprehensive emergency preparedness mechanisms. At the same time, GCC countries are increasingly investing in the preservation, digitization, and accessibility of documentary heritage, creating opportunities for regional cooperation and knowledge exchange.\nBuilding on the documentary heritage mapping and needs assessment conducted in the Arab region and in KSA, as well as the strategic partnership established with Qatar National Library and the creation of the new established MOWCAR, UNESCO will continue supporting the preservation, safeguarding, and promotion of documentary heritage in Yemen while fostering regional collaboration among memory institutions across the GCC. Activities will include strengthening capacities in collection management, inventorying, digitization, preventive conservation, disaster risk management, and emergency preparedness; supporting the identification and nomination of documentary heritage collections to the UNESCO Memory of the World Programme; promoting digital access to documentary heritage; and facilitating regional knowledge-sharing among libraries, archives, museums, and other memory institutions.\nThe programme will also support the development of practical tools, guidelines, and institutional partnerships aimed at enhancing the long-term resilience, accessibility, and visibility of documentary heritage collections. Particular attention will be given to protecting documentary heritage at risk, advancing digital preservation practices, and mobilizing partnerships and resources for larger-scale preservation initiatives in Yemen and the Gulf region.

reporting: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
title: Supporting Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Policies and Digital Initiatives to Build Resilience to Disinformation, Misinformation and Hate Speech in GCC Countries and Yemen
description:
The rapid expansion of digital technologies, social media platforms, and artificial intelligence is transforming how information is produced, shared, and consumed across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and Yemen. While these developments create new opportunities for participation and innovation, they also increase exposure to misinformation, disinformation, hate speech, online manipulation, and harmful content, particularly among young people.
Building on UNESCO’s global leadership in Media and Information Literacy (MIL) and the achievements of the previous biennium, UNESCO will support governments, educational institutions, media organizations, municipalities, youth organizations, and civil society actors in strengthening digital resilience and critical thinking skills. The programme will focus on advancing MIL policies and strategies, integrating MIL into education systems, empowering youth and educators, promoting digital citizenship, and supporting local initiatives that counter misinformation and hate speech.
Particular attention will be given to Qatar and Yemen, while expanding partnerships and opportunities in other GCC countries, including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain. Activities will include policy dialogue, development of national frameworks and educational resources, capacity-building programmes for teachers, youth leaders and media professionals, support for MIL Cities initiatives, research and evidence generation, and the promotion of innovative digital literacy approaches aligned with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Through these interventions, UNESCO will contribute to building more informed, inclusive, resilient and digitally empowered societies capable of navigating today's complex information ecosystem while promoting social cohesion, intercultural dialogue and peaceful coexistence.

reporting: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
title: Strengthening GCC capacities to expand access to reliable and accurate information through digital public goods, including open solutions
description:
Access to reliable information, knowledge sharing, and open digital ecosystems are essential foundations for inclusive knowledge societies and sustainable development. Building on UNESCO’s Information for All Programme (IFAP), the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Educational Resources (OER), and UNESCO’s broader work on access to information and digital cooperation, this programme will support GCC countries in strengthening policies, institutional capacities, and partnerships that promote open access, open data, and equitable access to knowledge.
The programme will focus on raising awareness of UNESCO’s Information for All Programme and supporting interested Member States in establishing National IFAP Committees as national platforms for dialogue and cooperation on digital inclusion, access to information, multilingualism, information ethics, and digital literacy. It will also support the follow-up implementation of UNESCO’s Recommendation on Open Educational Resources through policy dialogue, knowledge sharing, and capacity-building initiatives. Activities will include high-level policy discussions, regional consultations, advocacy events, technical information sessions, and participation in major regional forums such as ICEGOV 2026 in Riyadh and other relevant digital governance events.
The programme will also support the promotion of Universal Acceptance and multilingualism in the digital environment through the dissemination of the UNESCO–ICANN Policy Brief Advancing Universal Acceptance of All Domain Names and Email Addresses for a Multilingual Internet. Activities will aim to raise awareness among policymakers, regulators, technical communities, academia, and digital stakeholders on the importance of ensuring that all domain names and email addresses, regardless of language or script, function equally across digital systems. The programme will further support regional advocacy and awareness-raising initiatives linked to the International Day for Universal Access to Information (IDUAI), reinforcing UNESCO’s commitment to inclusive access to information and digital participation for all.
Expected results include strengthened national capacities to promote open knowledge policies, increased awareness of UNESCO’s normative frameworks on access to information and Open Educational Resources, enhanced regional cooperation through the Information for All Programme, and greater engagement of GCC stakeholders in developing inclusive and knowledge-based digital societies.

reporting: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
title: Supporting GCC States policies and building capacities for digital transformation
description: Countries across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and Yemen are accelerating digital transformation as part of their national development agendas, with growing investments in artificial intelligence, data governance, digital public services, and digital inclusion. To ensure that these transformations are human-centred, sustainable, and rights-based, UNESCO will support national institutions in strengthening policies, capacities, and multi-stakeholder cooperation on digital transformation.\nThe programme will focus on promoting responsible and sustainable artificial intelligence, including Green AI and AI for sustainability; strengthening capacities of public sector institutions through UNESCO’s Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in the Public Sector Programme and its Arabic online learning platform; advancing data governance and digital policy dialogue; and promoting the use of UNESCO’s Internet Universality Indicators framework to support evidence-based digital policy development. Activities will include high-level policy discussions, regional consultations, capacity-building programmes, technical information sessions, and partnerships with national schools of public administration, universities, digital transformation authorities, and national commissions for UNESCO. The programme will also support regional advocacy and knowledge-sharing during major digital governance forums, including the Web Summit, the Global Forum on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence 2026 in Riadh, the Doha Forum, the World Data Forum, and other relevant regional events.\nExpected results include strengthened capacities of public officials and policymakers, increased awareness of sustainable and inclusive digital transformation approaches, enhanced use of UNESCO’s policy tools and frameworks, stronger regional cooperation networks, and greater readiness of GCC countries to undertake national digital policy assessments and reforms.

title: Surveying Public Attitudes of Security Sector Reforms in the Arab World
description: One constant in the ebb and flow of the Arab Spring has been the increased influence of public opinion on public policy. Few areas of public concern have had more resonance than the role of state security services in shaping and preserving undemocratic regimes. The notion that the security sector's primary responsibility is to protect and preserve autocratic Arab regimes is widely discredited today. Arab citizens are now calling for security sector reform to make security services more accountable to citizens and to democratically elected governments. Through applied survey research, this project will measure public response to security services changes in Egypt, Iraq, Tunisia, Yemen, and West Bank and Gaza. The project will aim to enhance the role of public opinion in security sector reform by providing evidence-based information on public perceptions, and in so doing, encouraging civilian oversight and transparency in the sector. Specifically, it will achieve the following objectives: -build a cumulative, comparative, and policy-relevant knowledge base; -document and expose cases of security services abuse and promote greater accountability; -highlight gender and minority experiences to provide insight into the security sector's effectiveness in providing security to those who need it most; -engage senior policymakers in a discussion about public attitudes and provide oversight tools for a more just and accountable Arab security sector; -share the project findings with policymakers and stakeholders through reports, workshops, and meetings; and, -build security sector reform skills and knowledge in partner institutions in the Arab countries of focus. The Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research, an independent Ramallah-based think tank, will lead the research. The project will build on the center's work on security sector reform in West Bank and Gaza. Through surveys, researchers will capture public perceptions and expectations toward the security sector. The surveys will focus on the sector's performance, capacity, response to developments on-the-ground, and its effectiveness in working with the justice sector. The research team will assess and document vulnerable groups' perspectives, including women and children, to provide insight into how effectively the security sector: -provides security to those who need it most; and, -addresses public security concerns rather than serving the ruling class' interests. Outputs from this three-year project will include a series of country reports, annual comparative reports, and a comprehensive index of public perceptions toward the security sectors of the region.

title: Strengthening the role of women in conflict resolution through natural resources management at the community level in the rural areas of the governorates of Sana’a and Lahj in Yemen
description: This project will help rural communities to better manage natural resources (land and water), strengthen the participation of women in conflict resolution mechanisms at the local community level, and increase economic self-reliance and enhance social cohesion in rural areas of Yemen.
sector_group: I.6. Other social infrastructure and services
sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Strengthening Food Security and Resilience for Conflict-Affected Communities in Yemen
description: The project contributes to restoring lost or affected livelihoods and enhancing the food security of IDPs and conflict affected populations in the governorates of Abyan, Al Jawf, Shabwa, and Lahj (Yemen) In order to do so, IOM will contribute to restoring lost or affected livelihoods of conflict affected populations  in the governorates of Abyan, Al Jawf, Lahj, and Shabwa through provision of solar-powered irrigation systems and agricultural kits, therefore, reducing the impact of agriculture economic losses, and contributing to sustainable livelihoods of farmers and families who engage in agriculture. Moreover, IOM will aim at mitigating the impact of high food prices on IDP populations and enhancing access to food supplies for most vulnerable IDP HHs in the governorates of Abyan and Al Jawf governorates.
sector_group: I.6. Other social infrastructure and services
sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Enhance Self-Reliance of Affected People through Access to Livelihoods Opportunities, Economic Recovery Processes, Community Asset Rehabilitation, and Reintegration of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Shabwa, Hadramout In Yem
description: The proposed project Emergency Employment and Community Rehabilitation for internal displaced persons, returnees and host and return communities in Yemen aims to assist in reducing and preventing the longer-term effects of crises and assist in recovering the community from the conflict. As a result of these activities, targeted communities will have access to cash and services which will empower beneficiaries and reduce the number of unemployment, the risk of famine and diseases outbreaks since there will be rehabilitation of basic services such as sewage systems and garbage removal.
sector_group: I.6. Other social infrastructure and services
sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Reintegration Assistance to Returnee Students and Host Communities in Lahj in Yemen
description: This project aims to improve access to basic (education) services for returnees, host communities and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Lahj governorate, an area facing one of the highest return rates in Yemen. By bringing host communities, IDPs and returnees together in cooperation with local government institutions, this initiative will enhance the social cohesion within the community and support the provision of education services and facilities in areas that were identified by the communities and authorities as most in need.  As part of the community stabilization initiative, this project targets four schools in 3 different districts in Lahj Governorate namely: Tuban, Al-Hota and Al-Muasimer districts, in need of rehabilitation, reconstruction, furniture and equipment.
sector_group: I.6. Other social infrastructure and services
sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Joint Implementation Program for Support of the Humanitarian Response Plan in Yemen 2020
description: The project's activities build on the achievements previously implemented by IOM in the education sector in Yemen, helping to ensure the continuity and expansion of education services in Marib, Hadramout, Aden and Lahj governorates that have some of the highest displacement and return rates in the country.
sector_group: I.6. Other social infrastructure and services
sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Joint Implementation Program for Support of the Humanitarian Response Plan in Yemen 2020
description: This project aims to improve access to basic education services for returnees, host communities and internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Aden, Lahj and Hadramout governorates (Yemen), which are facing some of the highest displacement and return rates in the country. By bringing host communities, IDPs and returnees together in cooperation with local government institutions, this initiative builds on previous interventions to enhance social cohesion within the communities and support the provision of education services and facilities in areas that were identified by the communities and authorities as most in need. This project targets eight schools in need of rehabilitation, reconstruction, furniture and equipment that have deteriorated following years of conflict. The project estimates to target a total of 4,500 students and 400 school staff.

sector_code: Multisector aid for basic social services

title: Life-saving emergency assistance for internally displaced persons and conflict-affected populations in Yemen - 2017-2018
description: The objective of this project is to contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality in conflict-affected areas in both vulnerable IDPs and host community members. This will be achieved through a combined action of emergency humanitarian assistance, life-saving health care and psychosocial support for vulnerable conflict affected children in both urban and marginalized rural areas in the government of Aden, Al-Hudaydah, Sana'a, Abyan, Al Dhale'e, Al Jawf, Hadhramaul, Ibb, Tarzz, Lahj, and Shabwan.

title: Combating Terrorism Fellowship Program (CTFP)
description: The Combating Terrorism Fellowship Program (CTFP) is a Secretary of Defense authority (Title 10) to build partnerships in the struggle against violent extremism through targeted, non-lethal, combating terrorism (CbT) education and training for mid- to senior-level international military officers, ministry of defense civilians, and security officials.

title: Integrated Emergency Response Programme to Improve the Living Conditions of the Most Vulnerable Conflict-affected Populations Across Yemen
description: The objective of this project is to provide integrated, coordinated, and effective lifesaving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable IDP and host community populations affected by crisis in Yemen. This intervention is providing information management, coordination, shelter, WASH, CCCM, health, and non-food item services. Learning from Communication with Communities (CwC) and feedback mechanisms set up across all IOM Yemen programming, this action will improve the overall accountability of the humanitarian response.

title: Integrated protection for vulnerable migrants and displaced populations in Yemen
description: Through this project IOM and DRC propose to continue operating mobile teams – Migrant Response Teams (MRTs) to provide immediate life-saving and protection assistance to newly encountered migrants who have often just arrived in Yemen.  Migrants in need of medical care are referred to IOM.

title: Envelope 2: integrated response in providing lifesaving Protection, Food and Non-Food Items to vulnerable conflict affected individuals with a focus on IDPs,  returnees and vulnerable host community families in Khamir and Huth districts in Amran gove
description: This project aims to provide protection, food and NFIs assistance and services to vulnerable, conflict affected individuals, including women and children. This project ensures the most vulnerable conflict affected IDPs, returnees and host communities meet their basic food needs through distributing food vouchers and NFIs.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to vulnerable migrants, IDPs and host communities in Yemen
description: While the number of new migrant arrivals to Yemen remained unabated in 2016 and 2017, IOM Migrant Assistance and Protection activities continued to expand. Therefore, in line with IOM’s larger migrant assistance and protection portfolio, the activities proposed herewith aim to provide life-saving assistance to vulnerable conflict-affected, destitute and stranded migrants in Yemen, including new arrivals along the country’s vast coastline where IOM would like to strengthen its presence. The project proposes to continue the Organization’s effort to conduct sea and air evacuations, mainly for vulnerable Ethiopian migrants and Somalis, stranded in various parts of the country and desperately wanting to go home.

title: Provision of Life-Saving Humanitarian and Protection Assistance for Stranded and Destitute Migrants in Yemen
description: Since the escalation of the situation in Yemen in March 2015, the overall situation has worsened with the limitation on services impacted by the ongoing conflict. The flows of new arrivals from the Horn of Africa of migrants and refugees continues regardless of the conflict. Through this project, IOM will provide the life-saving assistance including food, Non-Food Items (NFIs), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), health services including sexual and reproductive health care, and support to migrants until they are safely returned home through IOM’s Voluntary Humanitarian Return programme (VHR).

title: Provision of Life-Saving Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Assistance to IDPs and Conflict-Affected Communities in Yemen
description: Information gathered on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) needs for Internally Displaced Populations (IDPs) reveal an increase in the severity of the situation in Yemen, especially in the context of a continued large-scale displacement situation in which many WASH needs for IDPs, returnees and host communities remain unmet. The objective of this project is to contribute to addressing critical needs of IDPs and Conflict-Affected Communities with life-saving WASH interventions. This will be achieved by establishing and maintaining safe, equitable and adequate access to water, sanitation related interventions and hygiene promotion services.

title: Life-Saving Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons and other Conflict-Affected Populations in Yemen
description: With the aim to the strengthening of capacities, awareness, and direct assistance for a greater protection and wellbeing of the most vulnerableconflict-affected populations in Yemen in a timely and responsive manner, IOM will ensure that :1)Conflict-affected people in Yemen have access to life-saving health assistance; 2) Conflict-affected people in Yemen have access to critical life-saving non-food items (NFI); 3) Conflict-affected people in Yemen have access to safe drinking water, sanitation facilities, and hygiene awareness campaigns; 4) Conflict-affected people in Yemen have access to safe and dignified shelter solutions; 5) Rapid Response Teams are ready to support wheneverneeded within 72 hours; 6) Children in Yemen affected by the stressors related to a protracted situation of war are empowered and better able to react to protection threats.

title: Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons in Yemen
description: In response to the crisis in Yemen, IOM is providing multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance within the following sectors of assistance: health, coordination and safety, food security, water, sanitation and hygiene, shelter, camp coordination and camp management, non-food items, and emergency employment and community rehabilitation, and multi-sectoral assistance for migrants.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants in Yemen
description: Through this project, IOM provides multisectoral life-saving assistance to vulnerable conflict-affected, destitute and stranded migrants in Yemen, including new arrivals along the country's vast coastline where IOM is strengthening its presence and broadening the services offered.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons in Yemen
description: IOM will provide multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance in order to address the life-saving needs of internally displaced persons in Yemen. In particular, IOM will support conflict-affected populations on health, coordination and safety, food security, water, sanitation and hygiene, shelter, camp coordination and camp management, non-food items, and emergency employment and community rehabilitation and assistance for stranded migrants.

title: Emergency Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH)and Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Support to Vulnerable Persons in Yemen
description: This project provides multi-sectoral support to the most vulnerable Yemenis through water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions, and through informed and coordinated data collection for the humanitarian community. The complex profile and massive scale of the crisis affecting millions of Yemenis has left the population in dire need of these essential interventions.

title: Emergency Relief and Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Yemen
description: The objective of this action is to provide coordinated and effective lifesaving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable populations affected by the crisis in Yemen, with a focus on Ma’rib, Al Jawf, Al Bayda and Shabwa governorates (Ma’rib Hub) and Abyan, Aden, Al Dhale, Lahj and Taizz governorates (Aden hub). Through this intervention, IOM is providing coordination, information management and emergency relief services that support vulnerable populations and humanitarian actors. This project is advancing humanitarian response in locations which require urgent service provision to acutely displaced populations, migrants, and Yemeni nationals. The locations targeted under this project are prioritized based on existing needs and service gaps, and IOM aims to further tailor response activities under this action to meetand prepare for emergency humanitarian needs. In addition, IOM is forging ahead with plans to integrate assistance and services in Marib and Aden hubs, in line with the current strategies of the humanitarian architecture in Yemen.

title: Provision of Humanitarian Response to Vulnerable Populations in Yemen
description: Through this project, IOM ensures a multi-sector approach to addressing the most pressing humanitarian needs in Yemen – ensuring accountable, needs-based programming and maintaining flexibility and responsiveness to emerging and onset crises. This project provides coordinated multi-sector humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable populations in Yemen—including internally displaced persons, host communities and migrants—affected by the ongoing crisis in response to needs emerging from onset emergencies such as displacement, natural disasters, conflict, through integrated camp coordination and camp management services and water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions.

title: Emergency Assistance – Country Level Funding – IOM 2020
description: This project aims to provide multisector humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations, including internally displaced populations, refugees, migrants, and host communities in Yemen. The activities implemented utilizing these funds are multi-sectoral and closely align with the 2019 Yemen Humanitarian Response Plan, as well as key priorities for 2020. Activities will be adjusted as needed in line with OCHA cluster priorities and needs assessments conducted on the ground to provide key services such as water, sanitation and hygiene, health, protection, shelter and non-food items and camp coordination and camp management, among others.

title: Provision of Integrated Protection and Life-Saving Health Services to Migrants and IDPs in Yemen
description: Through this project, IOM aims to enhance its migrant assistance and response capacity in Yemen to reduce the specific morbidity, mortality, and suffering of vulnerable migrants. This is done through the provision of integrated protection and life-saving health assistance that meets the most critical needs of migrants traveling through Yemen, as well as internally displaced persons, host community members, and other vulnerable populations encountered.

title: Provision of Life-Saving Multi-Sectoral Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPS) And Other Conflict-Affected Communities in Yemen
description: IOM is providing multi-sectoral assistance to the most vulnerable conflict-affected Yemenis through displacement tracking, health, protection, shelter and non-food items, camp coordination and camp management, and water, sanitation and hygiene assistance.

title: Provision of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to Newly Displaced Households in Yemen
description: The project aims to provide first line multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) to newly displaced households in Yemen, affected by natural disaster or stranded/displaced as a result of COVID-19 as part of the rapid response mechanism (RRM) assistance package (including transit and hygiene kits, Immediate Response Rations (IRR) and MPCA).

title: IOM - Multi Country Humanitarian Assistance CAP 2021
description: Yemen, in its seventh year of conflict, continues to face the world’s worst humanitarian crisis. Humanitarian needs continued to grow in 2020, driven by escalating conflict, disease, a declining economy, and the breakdown of public institutions and services. The situation is predicted to worsen in 2021, and it is projected that the population will experience alarming levels of acute malnutrition and food insecurity. In line with humanitarian, national and donor priorities for Yemen, and IOM Yemen’s strategy, IOM ensures a holistic approach to addressing the pressing humanitarian needs in Yemen – ensuring accountable, needs based programming; building local ownership and capacities; maintaining flexibility and responsiveness. The project contributes to the provision of critical multi-sectoral assistance to the most vulnerable conflict-affected Yemenis; including shelter and non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene assistance, and health interventions.

title: Displacement Tracking to Vulnerable Migrants, IDPs and Returnees in Yemen
description: This project, carried out through the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) systems, will consist of the collection, analysis and dissemination of new and pre-existing data on internal displacements and migrant mobility in Yemen to better understand displacement and movement trends, migrants' profiles and needs amongst the mobile vulnerable groups. The objective of this project is to provide a stronger evidence base for humanitarian response, development planning and operations with a comprehensive countrywide analysis generated through the collection of primary data at community level in all the 22 governorates of Yemen. To achieve this objective, IOM aims to collect primary data using baseline assessments (for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees) and flow monitoring (FM) as DTM methodologies. Further, the field teams deployed create a network of key Informants who provides information on the existence of the IDPs and migrants in respective areas. This project will follow a harmonized approach to map and monitor migration trajectories, demographics, associated needs and problems. Data collected will be used to produce regular updates on cross-border and transit mobility, including monitoring trends and movements over time. Data and reports will contribute to a comprehensive analysis of migration flows at the sub-regional level for the counties of Yemen, Djibouti, Somalia and Ethiopia.

title: Properness Actions for the Migrants Response in Yemen
description: This project will enhance the preparedness of IOM to respond to the migrants’ needs in Yemen in a timely manner by enhancing the capacity of the local partners to support the multi-sectorial assistance for the migrants and to support the humanitarian evacuation; stockpiling life-saving materials and kits (including transit, hygiene and shelter kits); providing the needed multi -sectorial assistance like; shelter, water, food; supporting the land transportation for the migrants from the conflict areas to the safe areas inside Yemen; enhancing preparedness further by having a number of boats on standby in the international waters to evacuate the migrants who are willing to return from Yemen to their country of origin, via Djibouti.

title: GEF SGP 7th Operational Phase - Strategic Implementation using STAR Resources mainly in LDCs and SIDs (Part 3)
description: During the project period, the SGP will deliver the following important socio-economic results:  ·        SGP interventions will directly impact 120,000 beneficiaries/community partners, of which 50% are female through enhanced capacities and improved livelihoods and lives;  ·        SGP will support CSO-Government-Private Sector dialogues in at least 10 countries to have scaled up policy impact  ·        Under social inclusion, the SGP will ensure that 30% of its projects are led by women and that at least 50% of all SGP beneficiaries are women;  ·        At least 20% of relevant SGP country programs integrate appropriate models to engage youth and 15% of countries have targeted support for indigenous peoples;   ·        At least 15 countries will undertake South-South exchanges such that cross-fertilization and learnings between communities, CSOs and other partners are promoted;     The interventions from the SGP contribute to global environmental benefits at multiple levels, starting from the global level, prioritized at the national level through the CPS, and translated into small grant actions in the field. Firstly, SGP priorities will be fully aligned to that of the GEF-7 Programming Directions Paper and its outcomes to meet the GEF-7 targets. Secondly, greater attention will be focused on creating synergy among individual projects using landscape or seascape approaches, as well as taking all opportunities for complementation with larger projects of the GEF and other donor agencies. Thirdly, SGP local initiatives will link to global initiatives and platforms, as well as fostering joint efforts with global networks. Finally, the implementation of “Grantmaker+” has been designed to support scaling up, mainstreaming and replication that will provide higher level capacity development (i.e. IP Fellowships), networking and institutional support, knowledge sharing (e.g. through South-South exchanges), and advocacy mechanisms at national levels (i.e. CSO-Government-Private Sector Dialogue Platforms), and where relevant, all of these to extend to regional and global levels. Insofar as the SGP interventions promote local socio-economic benefits such as improvement of local livelihoods and strengthening capacities of local communities, these will take into consideration the underlying aim to reduce threats from the local level to globally important environmental assets, raising awareness and mobilizing civil society and the wider public towards supporting environmentally friendly practices and approaches. In this way, the delivery of the socio-economic and other local benefits contribute towards the delivery of global environmental benefits.

title: Provision of life-saving nutrition, health and WASH assistance to the most vulnerable conflict-affected communities in Abyan and Shabwa in Yemen
description: This project aims to provide life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable in Shabwah (Attaq and Habban districts) and Abyan (Russud and Sarrar districts) governorates through an integrated approach that includes nutrition, health and WASH assistance. This is to contribute in addressing the immediate causes of morbidity, mortality, food insecurity and malnutrition in priority districts identified among the most affected by the crises.

title: Life-saving humanitarian assistance to migrants, IDPs and other conflict affected populations in Yemen
description: The proposed project will enable IOM to continue providing life-saving assistance to vulnerable migrants at locations where the needs are huge,such as Sana’a, Al-Hodeidah, Aden, other coastal governorates as well asinternally displaced persons (IDPs) and other conflict affected people in Shabwah and Sa’adah governorates. Through this project, IOM will ensure migrants’ access to humanitarian assistance and protection through enhanced outreach activities at locations where migrants are known to be present including points of arrivals and transit.

title: Life-Saving Health Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Other Conflict-Affected Populations in Yemen
description: IOM plans to support 37 health facilities including Emergency Mobile Medical Teams (EMMT), fixed health centers and rural level hospitals in 17governorates of Yemen. An estimated over 400,000 IDPs and other conflict-affected Yemenis are expected to benefit from the health services provided by the supported health facilities. Through this project, IOM will improve access to the most vulnerable IDPs and other conflict affected people in the remote and hard to reach communities with a full package of primary health services including sexual and reproductive health care, as well as emergency secondary and tertiary level care through effective patient referral system. IOM will also increase synergies across this project with the MoPHP disease control programmes for TB, HIV/AIDS and malaria which are already supported by IOM Yemen through the Global Fund grant since 2017.

title: Emergency Health Assistance to Yemeni Populations through Implementation of Minimum Service Package (MSP)
description: IOM Yemen will provide health assistance to vulnerable Yemenis through the provisions of the minimum package of health services. This project will also support Yemeni health institutions through the provisions of running and support to health professionals.

title: Emergency Health Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Other Conflict-Effected Yemenis
description: In response to the increasing needs for humanitarian assistance, IOM is implementing a series of actions aimed at reducing suffering, mortality and morbidity among internally displaced persons and host communities. This will be achieved through the implementation of support to primary and secondary healthcare services of government hospitals support to health centers for essential emergency and primary health and nutrition services. IOM will provide these services through supporting two hospitals and four health care centers in Al Mahwit, Sa’adah, Hajjah, Taiz, and Shabwah governorates.

title: Provision of Comprehensive Health Assistance to Displaced and Vulnerable Communities in Ibb, Marib and Dhamar Governorates (Parameter 2)
description: IOM is providing life-saving healthcare assistance-inclusive of primary, secondary, maternal and child, and reproductive healthcare services in Yemen. It also ensures an integrated and comprehensive healthcare response to the needs of the conflict-affected populations in the target areas.

title: Improving the Quality of Maternity and Childcare in Sana’a, Yemen
description: IOM will contribute to improving maternity and child health care by carrying out an in-depth assessment of available maternal and child health care services in Sana’a. IOM will support hospital managers and health professionals identify areas of obstetric and neo-natal care that need to be improved and to develop a plan of action to implement change. IOM will further provide direct capacity building support to one health care facility in Yemen (Mother and Child Health (MCH)) through one targeted training and the provision of medicine, medical equipment and water and sanitation health support.

title: Emergency Health Assistance to IDPs and Other Conflict-Effected Yemenis
description: IOM Yemen will contribute to the reduction of avoidable morbidity and mortality through the provision of primary and secondary health services to vulnerable populations across Marib governorate in response to the acute needs and limited availability of humanitarian actors and services that currently exist in the governorate. Through this project, IOM will contribute to enhancing the lives of an estimated 96,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other conflict-affected populations by supporting two hospitals and three health centres.

title: Emergency Health Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDP’s), Migrants and Conflict-Affected Host Communities
description: IOM Yemen aims to reduce further avoidable morbidity and mortality by providing access to emergency and essential health services to vulnerable populations across Yemen in response to the acute needs and limited availability of humanitarian actors and services that currently exist. Through this project, IOM will contribute to enhancing the lives of an estimated 52,476 conflict-affected and vulnerable population groups including internally displaced persons, migrants and host communities by supporting one health centre and two mobile medical teams where the most prominent needs are in order to complement IOM’s current health programming across Yemen.

title: Water for Peace in Yemen: Strengthening the Role of Women in Water Conflict Resolution and Climate Change Mitigation
description: This project contributes to the mitigation of water-based conflicts that have affected agriculture in Hodaidah Governorate (Yemen). Farming communities (men, women and youth) around the targeted areas are engaged to resolve local conflicts over upstream and downstream water allocation. The intervention is multi-facted and includes: mapping water-based conflict dynamics and drivers, strengthening the participation of women in conflict resolution mechanisms set up at the local community level; undertaking information campaigns; and increasing economic self-reliance and improving livelihood opportunities through critical infrastructure rehabilitation and cash-for-work programming.

title: Emergency Shelter, NFI Kits And Camp Coordination And Camp Management (CCCM) Support for Populations Affected by the Conflict in Yemen
description: This action aims at targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Households in the most affected areas of Yemen with needed Shelter emergency materials and Non-Food Items (NFIs). In addition to the NFI and Shelter support, IOM will support IDPs with cash for rent assistance to provide essential shelter support for extremely vulnerable families. title: SAFER Salvage Operation Project
description:
The Floating Storage and Offloading (FSO) vessel Safer is moored in the Red Sea approximately 8 kilometres off the coast of Yemen. Due to the political situation in the region, UN specialists have not been able to examine the condition of the vessel, but according to expert estimations the risk for oil spill is imminent. A spill could imply up to 186 000 m3 of oil along Yemen's Red Sea coastline and to the Gulf of Aden, which would cause a wast environmental and humanitarian catastrophy.

 

 The goal of the UN-led salvage operation is to prevent a serious oil accident in the Red Sea. The aim is to transfer the oil to  a safe VLCC-vessel (Very Large Crude Container) and to establish conditions for the disposal of the FSO Safer once a longer-term storage solution has been agreed.

 

 Finland's contribution to the UNDP-administered Safer salvage operation in Yemen is 1 MEUR. The overall budget for the operation is approximately 83 MUSD.

title: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES
description: This project contributed to responding to a cholera outbreak in IDP sites and the host communities in Aden and Lahj Governorates, in Yemen. Lack of safe water and the absence of latrines are among the main factors associated with cholera. To improve sanitation conditions in IDP camps, Concern installed 34 emergency fiberglass latrines for IDPs in Al-Salam and Al-Solban IDPs sites in Aden Governorate. The project also supported the rehabilitation of the water well in the Al-Salam IDP site and installed a solar-powered pump motor on the water well. There were critical gaps in community knowledge and practices around health & hygiene, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health so the project supported 45 female Community Health Volunteers in Tuban and Al-Milah districts to conduct health and hygiene awareness sessions. . title: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES
description: This project provided lifesaving emergency assistance to the internally displaced people (IDPs) affected by a sandstorm at the Al-Anad IDP site in Tuban District, Lahj Governorate. The project reached 638 people (325 male and 313 female) with emergency shelter and WASH services. 127 shelters were constructed and because the sandstorm also impacted the emergency latrines, water tanks, and water collection points in the Al-Anad IDP site, Concern installed a water tank within the IDP site, and a pipeline was installed to connect the tank to an existing solar water system outside the site to provide undisrupted and safe access to water for the residents. 15 emergency latrines were also constructed for families without access to latrines, including one latrine designed, especially for a person with a disability in one family. Concern used the latrine design made of fiberglass structure to reduce the heat, and the structure was fixed on the pit to reduce the risk of damage from future storms. . title: Improving Access to Quality Education in Yemen  - School Doors
description: (Yemen):  ...The Improving Access to Quality Education in Yemen- I (IAQY - I) activity is part of the USAID School Doors program. It works through the Ministry of Education (MOE) to strengthen and institutionalize non-formal education programs as a viable pathway for out-of-school children (OOSC), allowing them to resume their education. IAQY-I increases access to safe and quality education through improved service delivery at local and community levels and will expand equal access to an education that meets the needs of crisis-affected OOSC in Sana'a, Hodeidah, and Al Dhale governorates... ..FY 2019 funded activities include:.. ..- Establishing or reactivating Father-Mother councils for parental and community engagement in schools; developing school improvement plans; distributing teaching and learning kits to teachers and students respectively; and conducting back-to-school campaigns; .- Training and support to teachers on aspects of instructional quality and pedagogy, as well as school safety and psychosocial support; .- Providing children with effective psycho-social support through daily social-emotional learning activities; and  .- Developing and establishing guidelines and protocols for community schools to incorporate them into the formal education system including technical assistance on financial and human resource management, procurement, information systems, peer-to-peer networks, and creating policy for accreditation and eventual integration.  . Activities will result in restoring education opportunities for OOSC by increasing access to safe and quality education and expanding equal access to education to meet the needs of crisis-affected children. This directly contributes to objective 1 of the USG Education strategy: Expand access to quality basic education for all, particularly marginalized and vulnerable populations...

title: Peace and Inclusive Political Processes
description: (Yemen):  With FY 2024 funds, the Peace and Inclusive Political Processes in Yemen Program will partner with the Republic of Yemen Government (ROYG) and allies to support its efforts to govern more effectively and responsively and to function as a more productive interlocutor in peace and political processes. The program will also strengthen the capacity of Yemeni civil society, with a particular focus on youth and the private sector, to partake in consensus-building efforts and to meaningfully participate in the public life of Yemen. Finally, the Program will support the safe and meaningful participation of women in both the ROYG and civil society organizations (CSOs) in governance, peace, and political processes, including in leadership positions. .Key interventions will include advancing results-driven dialogue among government and civil society; fostering consensus-based dialogue among political actors; providing training and capacity building opportunities to enhance government effectiveness, oversight, and accountability; fostering networking, relationship-building, and advocacy across different groups; and supporting gender-sensitive policy development. As a whole, these interventions strengthen governance and advance a more inclusive and durable peace process in Yemen. ..

title: Addressing WASH Services in Yemen
description: (Yemen):  Yemen faces one of the world's most severe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) crises. Inadequate WASH access fuels the spread of cholera and diarrhea, worsening malnutrition in a country with high levels of food insecurity and stunting, while also complicating efforts to control other communicable diseases. Females are particularly affected due to their traditional roles in fetching water, cooking, childcare, and caring for the sick and elderly. They are also at increased risk of gender-based violence when forced to seek private areas to use the bathroom after dark. Addressing extreme water scarcity is critical to limiting the spread of communicable diseases in an already fragile context..With FY 2024 funds, the activity will enhance sustainable access to safe water and sanitation, mitigating the impact of communicable diseases on vulnerable Yemenis in conflict-affected areas. Funding will support the rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools, encouraging children and youth to remain in school and reducing the risk of early marriage or recruitment into armed groups. School interventions will also provide facilities that accommodate people with disabilities, helping eliminate bias and stigma while ensuring equal access for all..The project will rehabilitate water and sanitation networks, improving service delivery to the most vulnerable communities. These interventions will focus on internally displaced person communities addressing issues like overflowing sewage systems. Hygiene awareness training will remain an integral part of the program, promoting better health outcomes. Additionally, funds will be used to strengthen the capacity of local water authorities to manage WASH facilities by providing them with essential tools to maintain facilities beyond U.S. Government investments. Most importantly, the program goes beyond service delivery by addressing issues related to safety, security, dignity, and community climate resilience....

title: Systems, Health and Resilience Project (SHARP)
description: (Yemen):  .Yemen's Systems, Health and Resilience Project (SHARP) is based on trust-building, self-reliance, and increased resilience to support stabilization efforts, strengthen systems, and engage local institutions to create the conditions for sustainability. SHARP, USAID's three-year flagship health activity, will take an integrated approach to reducing maternal, newborn, and child morbidity and mortality by focusing on the Minimum Service Package (MSP), emphasizing integrated reproductive, maternal and neonatal and child health (RMNCH) services, coupled with appropriate wrap-around support services that address life-threatening challenges for communities (e.g. malnutrition, cholera, diarrhea) with strong community engagement to change health seeking behaviors and health systems strengthening activities to create local ownership to sustain system enhancements post-project.  SHARP will continue to foster an enabling environment and strengthen the health system by improving policies, strategies, practices, and increasing local ownership. ..With FY21 funds, SHARP will continue implementing core project activities launched last year in target governorates. SHARP will promote community outreach and engagement with quality, evidence-based messages via direct community engagement with local leaders and health care workers as well as media to introduce and reinforce key messages via community health counseling and services. SHARP will continue working both in the community with the help of the community midwives (CMWs) and the community reproductive health volunteers (CRHVs) and in the healthcare facilities to increase the availability of the  MSP in targeted districts through a robust referral system and will continue the piloting of a subsidized voucher program and community-pooled savings plan. SHARP will also continue providing high-quality in-service training, implementing Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI), and strengthening management systems. .

title: Gateway to Education
description: (Yemen):  USAID's Gateway to Education Program supports Yemen's Transition Education Plan-a national policy instrument developed as a multi-stakeholder plan to maintain progress towards literacy and longer-term educational goals in Yemen. Through Gateway, USAID aims to increase access to quality education in Yemen where nearly two million children are out of school and most lack basic services such as clean water and nutrition due to a protracted seven-year conflict...With FY 2022 education-earmarked funds, it is anticipated that the activity will 1) Develop, produce and distribute teaching and learning materials for grade 1-3 literacy and mathematics, including reviewing, updating, and adapting previously developed materials; 2) Integrate current efforts to educate out-of-school children (OOSC) through non-formal education and to prevent dropout through remedial educational programs with efforts to strengthen the formal school system (i.e. supporting entry and retention in the formal system for OOSC); 3) Work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to provide teacher development and training to strengthen education service delivery; 4) Facilitate the involvement of families and communities in supporting their children's education; 5) Rehabilitate and equip learning spaces to support improved education provision; and 6) Increase access for vulnerable groups including support for children with disabilities, girls, and conflict affected youth and their families..Activities will result in a strengthened, more resilient education system that provides a range of services to meet the complex learning needs of the children of Yemen, many of whom have experienced disruptions to their education during the ongoing conflict. The activities directly contribute to USAID's 2018 Global Education Policy and the priorities of the MOE as laid out in its Transition Education Plan..
