Through Gateway, USAID aims to increase access to quality education in Yemen where nearly two million children are out of school and most lack basic services such as clean water and nutrition due to a protracted seven-year conflict...With FY 2022 education-earmarked funds, it is anticipated that the activity will 1) Develop, produce and distribute teaching and learning materials for grade 1-3 literacy and mathematics, including reviewing, updating, and adapting previously developed materials; 2) Integrate current efforts to educate out-of-school children (OOSC) through non-formal education and to prevent dropout through remedial educational programs with efforts to strengthen the formal school system (i.e. supporting entry and retention in the formal system for OOSC); 3) Work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to provide teacher development and training to strengthen education service delivery; 4) Facilitate the involvement of families and communities in supporting their children's education; 5) Rehabilitate and equip learning spaces to support improved education provision; and 6) Increase access for vulnerable groups including support for children with disabilities, girls, and conflict affected youth and their families..Activities will result in a strengthened, more resilient education system that provides a range of services to meet the complex learning needs of the children of Yemen, many of whom have experienced disruptions to their education during the ongoing conflict. The activities directly contribute to USAID's 2018 Global Education Policy and the priorities of the MOE as laid out in its Transition Education Plan..

YCLE will also work to strengthen implementing partner activity monitoring and reporting and to support Mission MEL needs, including setting realistic but ambitious targets and reporting accurate results. ..

title: Yemen Community Resilience
description: (Yemen):  With FY 2024 funds, the activity will strengthen the resistance of communities to trafficking and recruitment-especially of children-into armed groups; the activity will support the reintegration of Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAAFAG) and former combatants back into local communities through individual assistance and community-based support. Interventions under this Program will address a broad range of community, family, and individual needs, including the conflict resolution and reconciliation; support to education, vocational training, and income generation/livelihood opportunities; and the creation of safe spaces and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) centers. All interventions will prioritize support to vulnerable population groups including children, adolescents, women, and marginalized groups and will enhance transparency and human rights, with a special emphasis on protection from sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Interventions include raising awareness of the CAAFAG issue, discussing how to address this threat through child protection mechanisms, early warning systems, service delivery and referral networks, and stakeholders' partnerships. .The activity will support community structures and community-based/civil society organizations to lead prevention mechanisms and support services for CAAFAG reintegration thereby advancing peacebuilding and reconciliation at the local level. Interventions align with the key objectives of the USG Strategy on Women, Peace and Security (WPS): (i) women are more prepared and increasingly able to participate meaningfully in civic and political leadership, in decision-making processes, and in institutions to promote peace and security; and (ii) women and girls have their rights protected and GBV prevention and response in conflict and crisis contexts is strengthened..Of these funds, $450,000 will go towards the Marla Ruzicka earmark.....

title: Strengthening Healthcare Access in Yemen (SHAY)
description: (Yemen):  With FY2024 funds, Strengthening Healthcare Access in Yemen will deepen healthcare coverage and service quality. It will strengthen referral networks for higher levels of Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) care, increase access to and quality of family planning services, strengthen district and local level health governance and healthcare quality and expand community-based approaches to reach vulnerable populations, with the goal of reducing mortality among women of reproductive age, their newborns and children under five as well as increasing community and health system resilience. .The activity will focus on interventions that optimize RMNCH outcomes, taking an integrated approach by focusing on the Minimum Service Package (MSP). This will be coupled with appropriate support services that address life-threatening challenges for communities (e.g. malnutrition, cholera, diarrhea), including immunization and family planning, and encourage strong community engagement to improve health seeking behaviors and strengthen health systems to create local ownership to sustain system enhancements post-project.  .The activity will promote community outreach and engagement with quality, evidence-based messages via direct community engagement with local leaders and health care workers as well as media to introduce and reinforce key messages via community health counseling and services. It will work in the community with the help of community midwives (CMWs) and in health care facilities to increase the availability of the MSP in targeted districts through a robust referral system. It will also build the skills of those midwives and strengthen their links to health care facilities. .The activity will also support sustainable health system improvements through building health management information systems that support better decision-making at the district and national levels....

description: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. title: Education Emergency Response in Yemen
description: (Yemen):  This USAID supported intervention will make significant impact to ongoing education activities in a very difficult situation across the country. Providing continuous support to bridge critical gaps in the Education Response to the crisis, the activity targets the most vulnerable, affected children with particular focus on areas with IDP children. This project restores access and re-entry to basic education with UNICEF and the Ministry of Education (MoE) through Back-to-School Programs (60,000 students are receiving school bags and basic learning supplies), support to administer year-end exams Grade 9 and 12, a Safer School project (planned for 11 governorates), minor physical rehabilitation of schools (200 schools), self-learning (15,000 students targeted) and psychosocial support.

reporting: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
title: UNHCR operation in Yemen (2023)
description: Yemen remains one of the world's largest humanitarian crises. After seven years of devastating and unrelenting conflict, some 23.4 million Yemenis (73% of the country's population) depend on humanitarian assistance to survive, including 4.3 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). The country has the fourth-largest IDP population due to conflict in the world.   Escalation of conflict, ongoing insecurity, embargoes and a collapsed economy have pushed an estimated 80% of the population below the poverty line. The protection environment throughout the country remains dire, and civilians keep bearing the brunt of the conflict.   Yemen hosts 95,815 refugees and asylum-seekers, mainly from Somalia and Ethiopia. It remains the only country in the Arabian Peninsula signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and a geographic crossroad for migratory and transitory movements from the Horn of Africa and beyond.  UNHCR leads the Protection, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), and Shelter/Non-Food Items clusters as part of the inter-agency humanitarian response to assist those most in need in Yemen. In addition, UNHCR remains the only agency addressing the protection and well-being of refugees and asylum-seekers across the country. UNHCR's response focuses primarily on protection interventions, shelter support, CCCM services, cash assistance, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion projects, and comprehensive refugee response.  Today, the Operation has a well-established presence across the country. It covers most of its 22 governorates and 333 districts through its Country Office in Sana'a, a Sub-Office in Aden, field offices in Marib, Al-Hudaydah, Sa'ada and Ibb, and a field unit in Kharaz refugee camp in Lahj Governorate.   At this critical time, humanitarian action in Yemen and the support of the international community to save lives, alleviate suffering, and give a sense of dignity and hope to the displaced remain imperative.  This activity shows details of the UNHCR operation in Yemen for 2023 including the budget, funding, expenditure and results. For specific details on the objectives of this operation, please use the document link "Stategy".

title: YEAR 1 PAYMENT FOR UPR INFO PROJECT ADVANCING HUMAN RIGHTS FROM
description: The overall goal of the project is to strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations (CSO) and NHRIs to effectively advocate for human rights and democratic reform through the UPR. To achieve this goal, UPR Info will provide an advocacy platform called Pre-sessions, consisting of a series of meetings organized in advance of each UPR Working Group (a State-led UN mechanism with little formal opportunity for CSO engagement). Each meeting consists of a panel discussion whereby national CSOs and NHRIs are invited to Geneva to present the human rights situation in the State under Review. Through participation in the platform, civil society can influence the recommendations that States will make at the UPR Working Group, ensuring that the Review reflects the needs of all rights-holders and contributes to sustainable progress on human rights. Participants are provided with training and advocacy opportunities, as well as strategies and tools that can be used in the follow-up phase to monitor the progress of implementation. A stipend will be offered to a small number of CSOs from LDCs to participate in the Pre-sessions.

title: Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen (UNJP with WFP, UNDP and funded by EC)
description: The three-year joint programme “Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen” (ERRY) will be implemented by FAO, ILO, UNDP and WFP in four governorates: Hajjah, Hodeidah, Lahj and Abyan. The overall objective of the programme is to enhance the resilience and self-reliance of crisis-affected rural communities through support to livelihoods stabilisation and recovery, local governance and improved access to sustainable energy. ERRY will achieve two outcomes: Outcome 1: Communities are better able to manage local risks and shocks for increased economic self-reliance and enhanced social cohesion. Outcome 2: Institutions are responsive, accountable and effective to deliver services, build the social contract and meet community identified needs. Within its three year timeframe, the following results will be achieved: • Output 1.1: Community livelihoods and productive assets are improved to strengthen resilience and economic self-reliance • Output 1.2: Communities benefit from improved and more sustainable livelihoods opportunities through better access to solar energy • Output 1.3: Informal networks promote social cohesion through community dialogue and delivery of services • Output 2.1: Functions, financing and capacity of local authorities enabled to deliver improved basic services and respond to public priorities • Output 2.2: Increased capacity of local actors and strengthened partnership of private sector to enhance collective actions, aid delivery and economic recovery Target groups will focus on the most vulnerable such as women, the unemployed, youth, the Muhamasheen, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stressed host communities, using inclusive, participatory and conflict-sensitive tools to mobilise and involve them in the proposed activities. Active partnerships with local authorities, the private sector, communities, the Social Fund for Development (SFD) and NGOs will be sought for the successful implementation of the programme

The proposed intervention, will empower youth at risk, including at least 30% of women, and will contribute to the improved security by creating sustainable and alternative livelihood opportunities for youth at risk of joining armed groups and violent extremism. title: Year 2 Payment CSF 11-21 for the project Peace Building from the Ground Up
description: The ‘Peacebuilding from the ground up in Yemen’ project aims to support civil society organisations and communities in Yemen, with a focus on marginalised groups, such as women and youth, to work together with local authorities to address the root causes of conflict and insecurity and enable them to contribute to longer-term peace and security. The implementing partners are Youth without Borders Organization for Development, National Organization for Community Development Society, and Alf Ba Civilisation and Coexistence Foundation. The objective is to reduce humanitarian need by ensuring conflict-affected communities in Yemen are more stable and resilient to shocks, through contributing to a more inclusive and sustainable political settlement. The key activities include enabling communities to work together with authorities in identifying and addressing the key drivers of conflict in their communities; enabling Yemeni CSOs to influence national and international level peace processes through the delivery of joint advocacy and peacebuilding interventions based on community priorities; enabling Yemeni women activists and women’s rights organisations to influence peace processes at all levels through the delivery of joint peacebuilding interventions; and enabling international stakeholders, including diplomats, policy-makers, and INGOs to develop solutions and policy ideas for a more inclusive long-term peace process and to take decisions on key Yemen policies and strategies informed by peace and security priorities identified by communities and CSOs including women.

title: Women, Peace and Security Research Award
description:
To mark the 20th anniversary of the United Nations Security Council Resolution (UNSCR) 1325 on women, peace, and security, and to strengthen the implementation of the women, peace and security (WPS) agenda, Global Affairs Canada is establishing WPS awards in partnership with IDRC.   
 
The objectives of these awards will be to promote increased knowledge of key challenges and emerging issues in implementing the WPS agenda, with a focus on conflict-affected contexts; to strengthen implementation of the WPS agenda and Canada’s National Action Plan on WPS; to create greater recognition of the important role played by women peacebuilders; and to enhance Canadian WPS leadership globally and at home.   
 
One of the WPS awards, the Women in Peacebuilding Research Award, will be a joint collaboration between Global Affairs Canada and IDRC. The award will have an annual theme. This year, the award will focus on the work and roles played by women peacebuilders, and those advocating for gender-inclusive and gender-transformative conflict prevention and resolution processes. The competition will target early career researchers or research institutions in fragile and conflict-affected states in the Global South.  
 
The winning concept will be awarded a CA$20,000 research grant (provided by IDRC) to conduct policy research for one year. IDRC will grant one award annually for the next five years, and an additional CA$5,000 annually for five years will be provided for an external consultant to assist with managing the call and targeting young scholars from the Global South working on WPS issues to apply.

title: Countering the Recruitment and Use of Child Soldiers in Yemen
description: The project aims at preventing the recruitment of children and youth and to sustainably reintegrate children formally associated with the conflict in Hajjah, Sanaa and Lahj governorates in Yemen (Specific Objective). The socioeconomic integration of children associated with armed forces and armed groups (CAAFAG), vulnerable youth and marginalized groups will contribute to stabilization and security of the targeted areas (Overall Goal). As a first outcome, targeted children and youths will have better access to services and facilities for their social and economic integration. Existing resources around children will be strengthened: labour inspectors at Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour, local councils, members of Social Committees, members of the Higher Council for Childhood and Motherhood, staff of NGOs, and community leaders will be capacitated to educate, inform and change their attitudes and behaviors towards children's use in armed conflict. Four child-friendly spaces in central locations will be created, to mobilize communities around the protection and wellbeing of children while providing recreational, psychosocial and life-skill education support. Four youth clubs will be created to engage target children in recreational activities. Coordination and referral mechanisms will also be set up to provide specialized mental health care support to CAAFAG and to reduce their vulnerability. As a second outcome, former CAAFAG and other children at risk of recruitment above the minimum working age will be reintegrated through access to employable skills for improved working conditions and sustainable income. Three hundred CAAFAG and children at risk (CAR) will be assisted and oriented in matching their skills/aspirations to labour market needs, based on a labour market assessment in four selected communities in the three Governorates. Two-hundred CAAFAG and CAR will acquire vocational skills through ILO upgraded informal apprenticeship system, consisting on on-the-job training in firms and workshops and theoretical training. Where possible, beneficiaries will be linked to ILO’s existing programme on improved informal apprenticeships. Three-hundred CAAFAG and CAR will be empowered with functional literacy and numeracy skills and will be equipped with essential life skills for personal and community development. For youth who demonstrate the potential for entrepreneurship, the project will provide business development services (BDS) with the view of empowering them to set up and run their own small businesses. For the special needs of adolescent girls at risk, the project will roll out a successfully developed and pilot tested “Women Business Owners Training programme in the selected governorates.

title: Provision of Camp Management and Camp Coordination Services in IOM-supported IDP Sites in Yemen, Priority 3
description: An estimated 4 million people have been internally displaced in Yemen since the onset of the conflict. Throughout 2020 and into 2021, internally displaced persons (IDP) camps and displacement sites continue to emerge and grow. The majority of these IDP sites have little to no access to basic services (health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), shelter), with IDPs, in particular women and children, also facing a range of protection concerns within the sites. With this grant, IOM aims to provide Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) activities in 15 IDP sites across Hodaidah, with a view to ensure that IDPs have access to basic humanitarian services, benefit from improved site conditions, and actively participate in site management activities.

title: Enhancing Resilience in Vulnerable Communities in Yemen
description: The project contributes to building resilience in Yemen through supporting the management and reintegration of mobile populations and addressing community recovery needs in targeted communities. In particular, the project aims to improve access to basic services through small-scale community-based projects, provide a stronger evidence base for better understanding displacement and movement trends and empower the local authorities, civil society, and communities and strengthen their capacities.

title: Provide Needs-Based Protection and Medical Assistance to Affected Populations, Returnees, and Migrants in Yemen
description: IOM aims at strengthening of capacities, awareness, and direct assistance for a greater protection and well-being of the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Yemen and to the Yemeni returnees from aboard. This is done through: (1) household assessment in the worst affected districts to gather more in-depth data regarding the shelter, services, and livelihood opportunities available in those areas; (2) life-saving services including immediate food rations such as water and dry food rations; non- food items (NFI) and hygiene kits; medical services, including primary and emergency medical assistance, and multi-purpose cash assistance. This project also contributes to the rehabilitation and expansion of the health intravenous fluid plant in Sanaa. In addition, IOM is working to ensure that migrants have access to humanitarian and protection assistance through ensuring humane and dignified return to their countries of origin.

title: Pre-positioning Critical Emergency Items: Multisectoral Contingency Pipeline Management
description: IOM interventions are supporting the humanitarian response in Aden, Hudaydah, Ibb, Sa’ada and Sana’a (Yemen)through the procurement, pre-positioning and provision of 19,585 non-food items, 8,500 basic hygiene kits, 60,000 mosquito nets and 16,585 emergency shelter kits across five hubs in Yemen (covering seven locations). In addition, IOM will provide 351,662 litres of diesel fuel to water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities across Yemen and provode600 emergency, gender-sensitive sanitation facilities to newly displaced populations.

title: Providing Emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Health Assistance, and a Humanitarian Hub for Aid Operations in \\Ma’rib Governorate
description: IOM was the first UN agency to establish dedicated presence in Ma’rib, Yemen in 2019 after the Organization’s multisectoral assessments demonstrated the widespread needs across the governorate. Since then, IOM has sounded the alarm for the need for scale-up of life-saving humanitarian programming in Ma’rib, and the Organization has been committed to facilitating this by running a humanitarian hub in Ma’rib city. Through this project, IOM is carrying out critical water, sanitation and hygiene and health activities targeting conflict-affected people. This fund is also critical for expanding health services to cover the widespread needs amongst internally displaced persons and host communities in Ma’rib governorate. IOM is also contributing towards reducing avoidable morbidity and mortality through the provision of emergency, primary and secondary health services, including nutrition screenings due to the risk of famine and extreme hunger in Yemen.

title: Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen (UNJP with WFP, UNDP and funded by EC)
description: The three-year joint programme “Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen” (ERRY) will be implemented by FAO, ILO, UNDP and WFP in four governorates: Hajjah, Hodeidah, Lahj and Abyan. The overall objective of the programme is to enhance the resilience and self-reliance of crisis-affected rural communities through support to livelihoods stabilisation and recovery, local governance and improved access to sustainable energy. ERRY will achieve two outcomes: Outcome 1: Communities are better able to manage local risks and shocks for increased economic self-reliance and enhanced social cohesion. Outcome 2: Institutions are responsive, accountable and effective to deliver services, build the social contract and meet community identified needs. Within its three year timeframe, the following results will be achieved: • Output 1.1: Community livelihoods and productive assets are improved to strengthen resilience and economic self-reliance • Output 1.2: Communities benefit from improved and more sustainable livelihoods opportunities through better access to solar energy • Output 1.3: Informal networks promote social cohesion through community dialogue and delivery of services • Output 2.1: Functions, financing and capacity of local authorities enabled to deliver improved basic services and respond to public priorities • Output 2.2: Increased capacity of local actors and strengthened partnership of private sector to enhance collective actions, aid delivery and economic recovery Target groups will focus on the most vulnerable such as women, the unemployed, youth, the Muhamasheen, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stressed host communities, using inclusive, participatory and conflict-sensitive tools to mobilise and involve them in the proposed activities. Active partnerships with local authorities, the private sector, communities, the Social Fund for Development (SFD) and NGOs will be sought for the successful implementation of the programme

title: Provision of Rapid Response Mechanism Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to Newly Displaced Households in Yemen, Priority 3
description: This project aims to provide first line one-off multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) to 2,500 households (17,500 individuals) newly displaced and conflict-affected households and 1,000 most vulnerable households in Yemen. This will be done with multi-month (two additional payments) of MPCA as part of the rapid response mechanism (RRM) assistance package (including transit and hygiene kits, Immediate Response Rations (IRR) and multi-purpose cash assistance) linked to the SO3 of 2021 HRP of “Protecting and Assisting Civilians” and the specific objective 3.1 that “Specific protection risks due to conflict disasters, food insecurity, and epidemics mitigated and addressed. Through to the provision of quality and integrated protection and humanitarian services. Ensuring, attention to specific needs and prioritizing the most vulnerable including displaced persons.”

title: Providing Emergency Multisector Assistance in Response to Displacement Crisis in Marib Governorate, Yemen
description: Since September 2021, the displacement crisis in Marib has progressively worsened following a marked increase in armed violence. The majority of internally displaced persons (IDPs) are seeking refuge in Ma’rib Al Wadi and Ma’rib city, placing immense pressure on public services and fragile infrastructure in already overcrowded IDP sites. In this project, IOM aims to build on gains made through the May 2021 Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) through the scale-up of multisectoral interventions in response to the new displacements in Marib, through a holistic approach and to complement other partners on the ground.

title: Providing Emergency Multipurpose Cash Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations in Yemen
description: Through this project, IOM is contributing to reducing food insecurity for crisis-affected populations through the distribution of one-off and multi-round multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) in Ta’iz and Hajjah governorates, Yemen. In coordination with UNHCR and partner organizations to avoid duplication of assistance, IOM is targeting food insecure households which were recently displaced or live in protracted displacement, as well as food insecure host community households in four districts: Al Ma’afer and Jabal Habashi districts in Ta’iz governorate and Abs and Mustaba districts in Hajjah governorates.

title: Multi-Cluster Location Assessment (MCLA) Yemen Survey Operations
description: The Multi Cluster Locations Assessment (MCLA) is going beyond location-level key informant interviews to gather more granular information on the humanitarian needs of specific population groups directly from households. Through household level interviews, the MCLA identifies individual household level vulnerabilities and humanitarian needs. This data contributes towards enhancing humanitarian needs severity analyses to inform humanitarian programming in 2020. The 2019 MCLA will mirror the 2018 exercise in scope and scale. The goal of the assessment is to identify household level vulnerabilities and humanitarian needs through household-level (HH) interviews in all 333 districts in Yemen. The MCLA also provides some clarity on the humanitarian context in Yemen by assessing the biggest challenges faced by affected populations when trying to access basic services and fulfil fundamental needs.

title: ECONOMIC EMPOWERMENT FOR YEMENI YOUNG MEN AND WOMEN AT RISK
description: This project therefore aims to restore and improve livelihoods, to create productive and decent emergency employment to increase income generation through sustainable enterprise development and by improving the employability of vulnerable groups. The proposed intervention, will empower youth at risk, including at least 30% of women, and will contribute to the improved security by creating sustainable and alternative livelihood opportunities for youth at risk of joining armed groups and violent extremism. The project will also ensure that communities from various factions and groups are to the extent possible involved in joint activities in order to create space for reconciliation. Last, the project will always be clear in its targeting mechanisms for beneficiaries, and will put in place a complaint mechanism so that communities have the necessary trust in its fair implementation .

title: Countering the Recruitment and Use of Child Soldiers in Yemen
description: The project aims at preventing the recruitment of children and youth and to sustainably reintegrate children formally associated with the conflict in Hajjah, Sanaa and Lahj governorates in Yemen (Specific Objective). The socioeconomic integration of children associated with armed forces and armed groups (CAAFAG), vulnerable youth and marginalized groups will contribute to stabilization and security of the targeted areas (Overall Goal). As a first outcome, targeted children and youths will have better access to services and facilities for their social and economic integration. Existing resources around children will be strengthened: labour inspectors at Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour, local councils, members of Social Committees, members of the Higher Council for Childhood and Motherhood, staff of NGOs, and community leaders will be capacitated to educate, inform and change their attitudes and behaviors towards children's use in armed conflict. Four child-friendly spaces in central locations will be created, to mobilize communities around the protection and wellbeing of children while providing recreational, psychosocial and life-skill education support. Four youth clubs will be created to engage target children in recreational activities. Coordination and referral mechanisms will also be set up to provide specialized mental health care support to CAAFAG and to reduce their vulnerability. As a second outcome, former CAAFAG and other children at risk of recruitment above the minimum working age will be reintegrated through access to employable skills for improved working conditions and sustainable income. Three hundred CAAFAG and children at risk (CAR) will be assisted and oriented in matching their skills/aspirations to labour market needs, based on a labour market assessment in four selected communities in the three Governorates. Two-hundred CAAFAG and CAR will acquire vocational skills through ILO upgraded informal apprenticeship system, consisting on on-the-job training in firms and workshops and theoretical training. Where possible, beneficiaries will be linked to ILO’s existing programme on improved informal apprenticeships. Three-hundred CAAFAG and CAR will be empowered with functional literacy and numeracy skills and will be equipped with essential life skills for personal and community development. For youth who demonstrate the potential for entrepreneurship, the project will provide business development services (BDS) with the view of empowering them to set up and run their own small businesses. For the special needs of adolescent girls at risk, the project will roll out a successfully developed and pilot tested “Women Business Owners Training programme in the selected governorates.

title: Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme in Yemen
description: The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service – SMEPS Yemen Social Fund for Development The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service (SMEPS) is a subsidiary of the social fund for development (SFD) was established by the SFD to address the needs of business services for SMEs. The Social Fund for Development was established in 1997 by Law No.10 as one of the measures to cushion the effects of the government’s reform programs on vulnerable groups, especially the poor. The SFD was formed as an autonomous agency with financial and administrative independence, governed by a Board of Directors, representing the government, NGOs, and the private sector under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister. The SFD seeks to reduce poverty by improving living conditions and providing income generating opportunities for the poor. SFD operations are carried out by seven project units: The Education, Cultural Heritage & Rural Roads , Water & Environment , Health & Social Protection , Training & Organizational Support , Agriculture & Rural Development , and Small & Micro Enterprises Development . These Units are responsible for policy setting, providing support to branch offices and monitoring progress within their respective sectors. The Yemen national strategy for small and micro enterprises (SME) development was approved by the council of Ministers on January 17, 2005. It included the establishment of a national agency to promote small and micro enterprises (The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service - SMEPS). SMEPS will be responsible for directing and coordinating activities to provide improved non-financial services for SMEs by planning, directing, coordinating and monitoring several programs with partner organizations. The programs will be aimed at stimulating growth and diversity within the SME sector. The ILO has an on-going project with SMEPS on “entrepreneurship education: KAB” targeting youth which started in 2008 under the patronage of the Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training. This collaboration has so far been successful. An Agreement was signed in May 2008 (copy attached) The website of the SMEPS: http://smeps.org/smeps/index.php The website of SFD: http://www.sfd-yemen.org/aboutSFD.htm

title: Yemen Health & Population
description: The objective of the Health and Population Project (HPP) for Yemen, Republic of is to improve access to and utilization of a package of maternal, neonatal, and child health services in selected governorates with a high concentration of districts with poor health indicators. There are two components to the project, the first component being improving access to maternal, neonatal, and child health services. This component will support initiatives targeted to improve access to Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health (MNCH) services in geographic areas with poor MNCH indicators. Activities will include delivery of outreach services and selected upgrading of first level referral facilities. It will comprise three subcomponents: delivery of outreach services; upgrade of first level referral facilities and provision of community-based health services; and support national public health campaigns. Finally, the second component is the results-based monitoring and evaluation and project administration. The project will finance technical assistance to carry out evaluations of the upgraded MNCH outreach services to measure the results of the project interventions on the access and utilization of women and children in the project governorates. The evaluations will include a baseline survey, mid-term and end of project evaluation. It will also support the implementation of the national demographic health surveys that will be implemented during the duration of the project. In addition, this component will support activities related to the design and implementation of independent monitoring of project targets and audit of outreach services.

title: Yemen Schistosomiasis
description: The development objective of the Schistosomiasis Control Project is to decrease the prevalence and intensity of infection of both urinary and intestinal schistosomiasis among school-age children by 2015 in endemic regions of Yemen. There are two components to the project. The first component of the project is preventive chemotherapy for schistosomiasis control. This component will support two anthelminthic drug delivery strategies (campaign-based preventive chemotherapy using fixed and temporary sites, and routine preventive chemotherapy), as well as technical assistance to support implementation, monitoring and evaluation of these strategies; training; and IEC (information, education, and communication) activities and social mobilization activities to support the effective application of the strategies. The second component of the project is independent monitoring, audit, and project administration. This component will support activities related to the independent monitoring of project targets and audit of project campaigns. The component will include support for mid-term and end-of-project evaluations as well as support for baseline, mid-term, and end of-project parasitological surveys for prevalence mapping used for classification and reclassification of endemic districts. The component will also provide project administration support through a Project Administration Unit (PAU) within the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MoPHP).

title: Emergency Health and Nutrition Project
description: The development objective of Emergency Health and Nutrition Project for Yemen is to contribute to the provision of basic health and essential nutrition services for the benefit of the population. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Improving Access to Health, Nutrition, and Public Health Services, will support the coverage of the population of Yemen with well-defined packages of health and nutrition services at both primary health care (PHC) level and first level of referral centers or secondary care. It has the following three subcomponents: (i) Strengthening the Integration of Primary Health Care Model; (ii) Supporting Health and Nutrition Services at the First Level Referral Centers; and (iii) Sustaining the National Health System Preparedness and Public Health Programs. 2) The second component, Project Support, Management, Evaluation and Administration, will support project administration and monitoring and evaluation activities (M and E) to ensure smooth and satisfactory project implementation. 3) The third component, Contingent Emergency Response, aims to improve the country's response capacity in the event of an emergency, following the procedures governed by OP/BP 10.00 paragraph 12 (Rapid Response to Crises and Emergencies).

title: Yemen Integrated Urban Services Emergency Project
description: The development objective of the  Integrated Urban Services Emergency Project for Yemen is to restore access to critical urban services in selected cities within the Republic of Yemen. The project financing is an IDA grant of SDR 106.2 million, in an amount equivalent to US 150 million dollars. The project will finance activities that support the restoration of critical urban services in selected Yemeni cities. The restoration of urban services, including water and sanitation, transport, energy and solid waste management, will be critical to improve health outcomes, basic living conditions and local economic activity. The project adopts an integrated approach to urban service delivery that provides coordinated, multi-sectoral support to Yemen during the conflict. The project has three components. First component, service restoration will support the restoration of critical urban services in selected cities in Yemen. The targeted services cover five sectors: tertiary municipal services and solid waste management, urban water and sanitation, urban roads, electricity for critical services, and housing. The project will focus on critical investments that can restore services in a short implementation timeframe. This component will finance works, goods, consultants services, non-consultant services, training, and operating costs of the local partners involved in the different subcomponents. All civil works under the project are expected to be undertaken by private sector contractors, thus supporting the revitalization of local economic activity. Second component, implementation support and capacity development will support capacity building activities for the stakeholders who will be involved in the delivery of activities under the project at central and local levels. These activities will focus on technical skills for all sectors involved in the project, including more effective human resource management, coordination, transparency and accountability, safeguards, and public financial management. Third component, contingent emergency response is to improve the country's response capacity in the event of an emergency, following the procedures governed by paragraph 12, Section III of the Bank Policy, Investment Project Financing. There is a possibility that, during project implementation, a natural disaster, epidemic or another emergency may occur, which would cause a major adverse economic and/or social impact.

title: Yemen COVID-19 Response Project
description: The project aims to help Yemen immediately respond and mitigate the risks associated with COVID-19 outbreak in Yemen.  Based on the Yemen Preparedness and Response Plan, WHO will aim to fill critical gaps in technical areas, such as: points of entry interventions; national laboratories; infection prevention and control; case management and isolation; and operational support and logistics.  These technical areas are identified to immediately strengthen the local capacity to respond and address the current COVID-19 potential challenges in timely manner, while working within the country's existing systems and providing technical assistance as needed for local entities. Emphasis will be placed on strengthening capacities at the district level through a model of decentralization.  This plan is designed to leverage the capacities of other key stakeholders to engage multiple actors and sectors active in Yemen.

title: Yemen Food Security Response and Resilience Project
description: The project focuses on building the resilience of Yemeni households to food security crises and improving household food security and nutrition by increasing food availability, access and utilization in the project areas. The project aims to serve as a scalable platform for broad-based support to food security in Yemen going forward. The project encompasses complementary activities to address the three core aspects of food security, including improving household incomes (improved food access), restoring and expanding agricultural production (improving food availability), and enhancing nutrition at the household level (improved nutrition). To achieve these objectives, the project includes five components, including: (1) Improving household incomes through Cash-for-Works and community contracting for agricultural production infrastructure; (2) Increasing production and sale of nutritious crop  and livestock products; (3) Improving the nutritional status of rural households; (4) Capacity building for food security management; and (5) Project management and knowledge management. The project aims to work through several Implementing Agencies – FAO, UNDP, and ICRC which allows for both tailoring and scaling-up interventions based on the needs on the ground in Yemen.

title: Yemen Emergency Human Capital Project
description: The development objective of the Emergency Human Capital Project for Yemen is to provide essential health, nutrition, water, and sanitation services to the population of Yemen. The project comprises of four components. The first component, improving access to healthcare, nutrition, and public health services aims to continue to ensure the delivery of minimum service package (MSP) services and strengthen the integration of the primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare and community levels. It consists of following sub-components: (i) improving access to MSP services at primary healthcare level; (ii) improving access to essential preventive and curative nutrition services; (iii) improving access to the MSP at secondary and tertiary healthcare levels; and (iv) sustaining the national health system preparedness and public health programs. The second component, improving access to water supply and sanitation (WSS) and strengthening local systems aims to support and improve the provision of WSS services for the population of Yemen by rehabilitating medium to large WSS infrastructure, prevention, and response to communicable diseases, and strengthening the capacity of key local water and sanitation institutions in selected urban, pre-urban and rural areas at the decentralized levels. It consists of following sub-components: (i) restoring access to and improving quality of WSS services in selected urban and rural areas; (ii) emergency support for water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to prevent and respond to communicable diseases; and (iii) enhanced capacity building of water and sanitation institutions at the local level. The third component, project support, management, evaluation, and administration will support the implementation, administration, management, monitoring and evaluation, and environmental and social aspects of the project. The fourth component, contingent emergency response will be in place to provide expedited response in case of emergency.

title: Emergency Lifeline Connectivity Project
description: The development objective of the Emergency Lifeline Connectivity Project for Yemen is to provide climate resilient road access and employment and entrepreneurship opportunities to food insecure rural population of Yemen. The project comprises of four components. The first component, rural and village access roads improvement and maintenance comprise of following sub-components: (i) rehabilitation of lifeline rural access roads; and (ii) road maintenance through private sector participation and supply chain enhancement. title: Sustaining Education and Learning
description: The Sustaining Education and Learning (SEAL) Project, with Additional Financing from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), builds on the achievements of the Restoring Education and Learning (REAL) Emergency Project to protect and strengthen basic education in Yemen amid ongoing conflict and fragility. The project's overall objective is to strengthen Yemen's capacity to sustain basic education and learning in targeted schools, while preventing further erosion of human capital.The project combines school-level investments with system-strengthening interventions to improve both access and learning outcomes. It supports the rehabilitation of deteriorated classrooms, construction of new classrooms to reduce overcrowding, and provision of gender-sensitive water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) facilities. Targeted schools receive school grants to sustain operations, strengthen community engagement, and improve learning environments, with school selection guided by a Project Targeting Index and strict Entry Criteria of Access (ECA) to ensure feasibility in the highly fragile operating context.With the Additional Financing, the project expands its focus from access alone to foundational learning and instructional quality. New activities include the large-scale provision of textbooks and learning materials, structured student assessments, and remedial learning programs for children who have not acquired basic skills. Teachers, school principals, and supervisors receive intensive training, coaching, and digital supervision tools to strengthen classroom practice, school leadership, and performance monitoring. The project also places strong emphasis on girls education, including targeted support for Rural Female Teachers (RFTs) and measures to improve girls enrollment, retention, and safety in remote areas.Through this integrated approach, SEAL aims to sustain access, improve foundational learning, advance gender equity, and reinforce education system resilience, helping Yemen's children remain on track for learning and future productivity despite protracted conflict.

title: Yemen Health Nutrition and WASH Project
description: Since 2017, the World Bank has supported Yemen's health sector through large-scale emergency operations that have delivered essential health, nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services to millions, while gradually investing in local institutions and systems. These efforts have sustained human capital in a protracted crisis, reaching nearly 24 million beneficiaries and training over 18,000 health personnel. Despite achievements, challenges in Yemen persist—including low immunization rates, malnutrition, conflict-related access constraints, declining donor funding, and reliance on external third-party implementation. The upcoming operation will prioritize integration, strengthen local capacity, and revamp health workforce development by aligning community cadres with national strategies, improving training systems, and creating job opportunities for health workers.  The project will consist of 5 components: Component 1: Delivery of integrated health, nutrition and WASH servicesComponent 1 will prioritize delivering an integrated minimum service package (MSP) across all levels of care—primary, secondary, and tertiary. Investments will be made to improve water and sanitation infrastructure at primary health centers. A Geographic Accelerator sub-component will tailor area-based interventions to local needs, combining MSP delivery with nutrition, WASH, and social protection interventions.Component 2: Support to prevent and respond to communicable disease outbreaksComponent 2 will retain emergency response capacity through disease surveillance, rapid response teams, laboratory support. It will also deliver emergency water trucking and to hospitals and support water quality testing. Component 3: Systems building for sustainable delivery of health and nutrition servicesComponent 3 focuses on building sustainable systems for health and nutrition service delivery by strengthening sub-national institutions and the health workforce. It includes tailored training for ministries and local health offices in planning, monitoring, and financial management, alongside support for refining national health strategies. A dedicated subcomponent will address critical health workforce reforms, aiming to resolve systemic bottlenecks and establish more sustainable funding mechanisms for health worker salaries. These reforms will also contribute to job creation and retention in the health sector, helping transition from volunteer-based service delivery to a more stable and professionalized workforce.Component 4: Project managementComponent 4 will consist of supervision costs, monitoring and evaluation, third party monitoring and financing of E&S compliance requirements, fiduciary aspects and procurement. Component 5: Contingent emergency response category (CERC)A zero cost CERC component will support the operation in the case of emergencies.

title: Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen (UNJP with WFP, UNDP and funded by EC)
description: The three-year joint programme “Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen” (ERRY) will be implemented by FAO, ILO, UNDP and WFP in four governorates: Hajjah, Hodeidah, Lahj and Abyan. The overall objective of the programme is to enhance the resilience and self-reliance of crisis-affected rural communities through support to livelihoods stabilisation and recovery, local governance and improved access to sustainable energy. ERRY will achieve two outcomes: Outcome 1: Communities are better able to manage local risks and shocks for increased economic self-reliance and enhanced social cohesion. Outcome 2: Institutions are responsive, accountable and effective to deliver services, build the social contract and meet community identified needs. Within its three year timeframe, the following results will be achieved: • Output 1.1: Community livelihoods and productive assets are improved to strengthen resilience and economic self-reliance • Output 1.2: Communities benefit from improved and more sustainable livelihoods opportunities through better access to solar energy • Output 1.3: Informal networks promote social cohesion through community dialogue and delivery of services • Output 2.1: Functions, financing and capacity of local authorities enabled to deliver improved basic services and respond to public priorities • Output 2.2: Increased capacity of local actors and strengthened partnership of private sector to enhance collective actions, aid delivery and economic recovery Target groups will focus on the most vulnerable such as women, the unemployed, youth, the Muhamasheen, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stressed host communities, using inclusive, participatory and conflict-sensitive tools to mobilise and involve them in the proposed activities. Active partnerships with local authorities, the private sector, communities, the Social Fund for Development (SFD) and NGOs will be sought for the successful implementation of the programme

title: Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme in Yemen
description: The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service – SMEPS Yemen Social Fund for Development The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service (SMEPS) is a subsidiary of the social fund for development (SFD) was established by the SFD to address the needs of business services for SMEs. The Social Fund for Development was established in 1997 by Law No.10 as one of the measures to cushion the effects of the government’s reform programs on vulnerable groups, especially the poor. The SFD was formed as an autonomous agency with financial and administrative independence, governed by a Board of Directors, representing the government, NGOs, and the private sector under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister. The SFD seeks to reduce poverty by improving living conditions and providing income generating opportunities for the poor. SFD operations are carried out by seven project units: The Education, Cultural Heritage & Rural Roads , Water & Environment , Health & Social Protection , Training & Organizational Support , Agriculture & Rural Development , and Small & Micro Enterprises Development . These Units are responsible for policy setting, providing support to branch offices and monitoring progress within their respective sectors. The Yemen national strategy for small and micro enterprises (SME) development was approved by the council of Ministers on January 17, 2005. It included the establishment of a national agency to promote small and micro enterprises (The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service - SMEPS). SMEPS will be responsible for directing and coordinating activities to provide improved non-financial services for SMEs by planning, directing, coordinating and monitoring several programs with partner organizations. The programs will be aimed at stimulating growth and diversity within the SME sector. The ILO has an on-going project with SMEPS on “entrepreneurship education: KAB” targeting youth which started in 2008 under the patronage of the Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training. This collaboration has so far been successful. An Agreement was signed in May 2008 (copy attached) The website of the SMEPS: http://smeps.org/smeps/index.php The website of SFD: http://www.sfd-yemen.org/aboutSFD.htm

title: Provision of shelter support, NFIs and protection services to families displaced by conflict in Marib and Hadramaut
description:
Through this project UNHCR implements urgent shelter, non-food items (NFI) and protection engagements to improve the living conditions and wellbeing of displaced Yemenis affected by the recent conflict escalation in Marib and Hadramaut governorates. The proposal is in line with the Operational Plan designed at inter-agency level in November 2021 to face the new wave of displacement in Marib.


Shelter and NFI engagements focus on ensuring the most vulnerable displaced families in Marib and Hadramaut have access to a minimum standard of living, dignified conditions and protection from the elements through the procurement and distribution of localized/emergency shelter kits and NFIs. Newly displaced families are prioritized. UNHCR also assists those in urgent need of support to pay their rent and avoid imminent eviction through rental subsidies.



Via its protection engagements in Marib, UNHCR conducts vulnerability assessments to identify newly displaced families and individuals in need, refer them to lifesaving services and determine eligibility for vital humanitarian assistance, including cash-based support; UNHCR operates two community centres with attached mobile teams from which legal assistance (awareness, counselling, representation) on civil issues, psychological first aid (PFA) and psychosocial support (PSS), child protection and gender-based violence (GBV) services are delivered to those most affected by the conflict.

The project targets 39,450 affected people with its ESNFI engagement and 88,390 affected people with its Protection engagement.

title: Stock replenishment of emergency rations to IDPs, deliver nutrition treatment and prevention activities for children and PLWGs, and provide humanitarian air services in Yemen.
description:
The project responds to the needs of affected through a multi-layered approach, including both operations and operational support through UNHAS.

1) FSA through RRM support: As families are uprooted suddenly from their homes, their most critical immediate needs are food and basic personal items. While fully-fledged emergency response actions through the clusters are being organized, there is an obvious need to provide an immediate life-saving response to newly displaced families. To meet this need, the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) was activated as a first responder until other clusters' humanitarian response could take effect. The component supports the replenishment of stocks of RRM’s food component, already distributed for this situation.

2) Nutrition: Acute malnutrition hits record levels in Yemen with a devastating toll on children under five years of age. The conflict has significantly compounded an already fragile nutrition situation. This contribution supports the delivery of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) treatment and prevention assistance to children and pregnant and lactating women and girls (PLGW). This is accomplished through the procurement, dispatch and distribution of specialized nutrition commodities.

3) UNHAS: One of the main obstacles to immediately mobilizing an adequate response is limited partners presence on the ground. The recent escalation in Ma’rib  has hampered access to the area and affects the capacity of humanitarian actors to deliver assistance in an optimal way. This contribution supports the aviation contracted services (aircraft and support services).

The project targets a total of 109,062 affected people through its FSA/RRM component and 34,516 affected people through its Nutrition component.

2) Nutrition: Acute malnutrition hits record levels in Yemen with a devastating toll on children under five years of age. The conflict has significantly compounded an already fragile nutrition situation. This contribution supports the delivery of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) treatment and prevention assistance to children and pregnant and lactating women and girls (PLGW). This is accomplished through the procurement, dispatch and distribution of specialized nutrition commodities.

3) UNHAS: One of the main obstacles to immediately mobilizing an adequate response is limited partners presence on the ground. The recent escalation in Ma’rib  has hampered access to the area and affects the capacity of humanitarian actors to deliver assistance in an optimal way. This contribution supports the aviation contracted services (aircraft and support services).

The project targets a total of 109,062 affected people through its FSA/RRM component and 34,516 affected people through its Nutrition component.

The project also responds to the current humanitarian emergency health needs of those directly affected people in conflict-affected areas in Marib in Trauma Care Management. WHO deploys four Surgical teams in Marib General Hospitals, Kara Hospital, 26 Sept. Hospital and Hareeb Hospital (one team in each hospital) and also supports referrals by covering operational cost for twelve ambulance vehicles in four conflict affected districts in Marib, in addition to provide regular fuel supply to the above mentioned hospitals to ensure continuous hospitals functioning.\n\nThe project targets a total of 4,000 affected people with its Health component and 1,454 affected people with its Nutrition component.

description: The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service – SMEPS Yemen Social Fund for Development The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service (SMEPS) is a subsidiary of the social fund for development (SFD) was established by the SFD to address the needs of business services for SMEs. The Social Fund for Development was established in 1997 by Law No.10 as one of the measures to cushion the effects of the government’s reform programs on vulnerable groups, especially the poor. The SFD was formed as an autonomous agency with financial and administrative independence, governed by a Board of Directors, representing the government, NGOs, and the private sector under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister. The SFD seeks to reduce poverty by improving living conditions and providing income generating opportunities for the poor. SFD operations are carried out by seven project units: The Education, Cultural Heritage & Rural Roads , Water & Environment , Health & Social Protection , Training & Organizational Support , Agriculture & Rural Development , and Small & Micro Enterprises Development . These Units are responsible for policy setting, providing support to branch offices and monitoring progress within their respective sectors. The Yemen national strategy for small and micro enterprises (SME) development was approved by the council of Ministers on January 17, 2005. It included the establishment of a national agency to promote small and micro enterprises (The Small Micro Enterprise Promotion Service - SMEPS). SMEPS will be responsible for directing and coordinating activities to provide improved non-financial services for SMEs by planning, directing, coordinating and monitoring several programs with partner organizations. The programs will be aimed at stimulating growth and diversity within the SME sector. The ILO has an on-going project with SMEPS on “entrepreneurship education: KAB” targeting youth which started in 2008 under the patronage of the Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training. This collaboration has so far been successful. An Agreement was signed in May 2008 (copy attached) The website of the SMEPS: http://smeps.org/smeps/index.php The website of SFD: http://www.sfd-yemen.org/aboutSFD.htm

title: Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen (UNJP with WFP, UNDP and funded by EC)
description: The three-year joint programme “Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen” (ERRY) will be implemented by FAO, ILO, UNDP and WFP in four governorates: Hajjah, Hodeidah, Lahj and Abyan. The overall objective of the programme is to enhance the resilience and self-reliance of crisis-affected rural communities through support to livelihoods stabilisation and recovery, local governance and improved access to sustainable energy. ERRY will achieve two outcomes: Outcome 1: Communities are better able to manage local risks and shocks for increased economic self-reliance and enhanced social cohesion. Outcome 2: Institutions are responsive, accountable and effective to deliver services, build the social contract and meet community identified needs. Within its three year timeframe, the following results will be achieved: • Output 1.1: Community livelihoods and productive assets are improved to strengthen resilience and economic self-reliance • Output 1.2: Communities benefit from improved and more sustainable livelihoods opportunities through better access to solar energy • Output 1.3: Informal networks promote social cohesion through community dialogue and delivery of services • Output 2.1: Functions, financing and capacity of local authorities enabled to deliver improved basic services and respond to public priorities • Output 2.2: Increased capacity of local actors and strengthened partnership of private sector to enhance collective actions, aid delivery and economic recovery Target groups will focus on the most vulnerable such as women, the unemployed, youth, the Muhamasheen, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stressed host communities, using inclusive, participatory and conflict-sensitive tools to mobilise and involve them in the proposed activities. Active partnerships with local authorities, the private sector, communities, the Social Fund for Development (SFD) and NGOs will be sought for the successful implementation of the programme

title: Provision of emergency food assistance to food insecure populations in northern Yemen
description: The key objective of this project is to address needs related to food-insecurity, especially in northern Yemen, affected by WFP’s suspension of operations targeting a total of 6.5 million affected people across each cycle, which represents a 30% reduction compared to pre-pause levels. To achieve this objective, the project involves procuring wheat flour from WFP's Global Commodity Management Facility (GCMF), shipping it to Yemen, and dispatching it to distribution points for vulnerable Yemenis, in close collaboration with cooperating partners. With a CERF allocation of USD 7,000,000, WFP anticipates supporting 1,000,000 affected people in northern Yemen through activities in the Food Security sector, mainly food distribution.

title: Provision of lifesaving nutrition and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services in districts facing extremely critical acute malnutrition
description: This intervention will focus on underserved areas in Al Mokha and Mawza districts in Taiz, Hays and Al Khohka districts in Hodeidah, addressing gaps in Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) case management in priority locations and improving water and sanitation services for communities affected by malnutrition, and those vulnerable to waterborne diseases and the impact of climate change.The main aim of this project is to reduce mortality related to malnutrition in children under five with SAM with or without complications through the provision of lifesaving nutrition and WASH interventions. An estimated 68,800 children and women will benefit from nutrition services, implemented through health authorities and one implementing partner (FMF). In addition, 16,467 people in four communities in al Mokha district, Taiz, will further benefit from WASH activities to mitigate the risk of spread of water-borne disease; these include Al-Mashqar village, Al Kudaih village and Dar Al Shujah village as well as Al Mokha City where water sources will be rehabilitated/expanded/constructed.

title: Emergency agriculture and nutrition response to support the most vulnerable population in Al Mukha and Misrakh districts of Taiz Governorate
description: Out of the 16 governorates recording returnees and vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs), FAO will utilize this Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) allocation for under-funded emergencies in Yemen to support vulnerable smallholder farming households in Al Makha and Al Misrakh Districts in Taiz Governorate. Th In Al Makha district, the Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate stands at 30.8%, while in Al Misrakh it is 13%. According to WHO thresholds, these rates are classified as extremely critical" and "serious," respectively. According to FAO’s September 2024 high frequency monitoring, 60% of the population in Taiz Governorate are experiencing poor food consumption gaps. Food insecurity is a major driver of malnutrition in Yemen. Malnutrition among children and women is a serious public health problem among children, pregnant and lactating women in the targeted locations. Malnourished children, particularly those with severe acute malnutrition, have a higher risk of death from common childhood illness, such as diarrhea and pneumonia. Nutrition-related factors contribute to about 45% of deaths among children under 5 years of age.  In Yemen, sub-optimal access to quality diets, as well as the lack of knowledge to prepare and consume dietary diversified meals, are major drivers of malnutrition. The overall objective of this proposal is to improve the food security and nutritional well-being of the most vulnerable farming households by providing emergency agricultural assistance and fostering better nutrition awareness. The expected outcome of the proposed intervention is to reduce the impact of food insecurity and malnutrition among the most vulnerable households whilst progressively transitioning to more resilient and sustainable livelihoods. FAO’s support will be channeled through a cash plus approach, which includes the provision of in-kind crop and livestock inputs together with season-specific cash assistance. Time-sensitive emergency livelihood interventions, especially when combined with cash assistance, have demonstrated a significant positive impact on health and nutrition outcomes.The project will support 2,700 vulnerable smallholder farming households (18,900 individuals) from the host communities, IDPs and returnees. The project will target 1,000 households (7,000 individuals) in the district of Al Makha and 1,700 (11,900 individuals) in Al Misrakh.  1,500 households (500 in Al Makha and 1000 in Al Misrakh) will receive cash + vegetable seeds (tomatoes, onions, okra, mallow and hot pepper seeds) and agriculture tools and 1,200 households will receive livestock packages composed of live animals, animal feed and mineral blocks. The Cash+ approach will support beneficiaries receiving crop inputs by improving their food access until the vegetable harvest season. All project beneficiaries will receive training on best practices for crop and livestock production, along with awareness sessions on nutrition to optimize the management of project inputs and improve beneficiaries’ nutrition’ nutrition knowledge.

title: Integrated lifesaving RH and GBV services to the most vulnerable women and girls in the priority districts under the CERF allocation in Yemen, 2024-2025.
description: Yemen's ongoing humanitarian crisis has had a devastating impact on women and girls, exacerbating gender inequalities, increasing their vulnerability to gender-based violence, and limiting their access to essential reproductive health services, often with life-threatening consequences. According to the 2024 HNO, 18.2 million people—over 55 per cent of the population—will need humanitarian assistance and protection services in Yemen. Additionally, in 2024, approximately 17.8 million individuals in Yemen required health assistance, including 3.2 million IDPs. A total of 24 percent of people in need are women, who require access to various medical and reproductive healthcare services, including 4 per cent pregnant women in need of emergency obstetric care. Yemen’s Poly crisis that also includes climate-induced disasters, currency depreciation, limited income opportunities, rising costs of basic commodities, challenges faced by aid agencies, bureaucratic restrictions on female staff, the detention of aid workers in northern Yemen, and the regional escalation of hostilities impacting the Hodeidah port, which supplies 80% of humanitarian assistance to northern Yemen, have further created protection risks, as well as compromised access to life-saving RH services. In response to the escalating humanitarian crisis and its impact on women and girls, UNFPA with funding support from the CERF proposes an integrated one-year project aiming to provide a comprehensive RH and GBV response to the most vulnerable women and girls in underserved districts. Additionally, the integrated project will prioritize "essential lifesaving and life-sustaining activities". Some of the activities will be implemented through forming case-management WG in some selected areas.The CERF will serve two key purposes: as seed money to initiate lifesaving interventions and to scale up existing interventions in others project sites. This will significantly strengthen lifesaving programs through the establishment and enhancement of Women and Girls Safe Spaces, along with bolstering supported Reproductive Health Facilities. These interventions will provide an integrated comprehensive response that is aimed at providing RH and GBV services, both stand-alone activities and integrated, recognizing the strong interconnection between these aspects as essential components in effectively meeting the health and protection needs of women and girls affected by emergencies.The support provided through this funding is set to play a vital role in delivering essential services to some of the most vulnerable populations, with a particular emphasis on women, girls, and IDPs who find themselves residing in informal settings as well as within host communities that were recently affected by the floods. The focus will be directed towards key areas such as multisectoral GBV response, reproductive health care, Mental Health, and MHPSS, in addition to a range of protection and referral services through the support of CVA targeting 1,000 women and girls under GBV and 1,000 under the RH services.A total of 102,385 women and girls will benefit from this fund, with 53,572, receiving essential and life-saving reproductive health services and 48,813 receiving GBV support. Additionally, approximately 12,000 men and boys will indirectly benefit through awareness-raising activities and support for women and girls with delivery complications. CVA will be used as facilitation modality to ensure improved access to RH- GBV integrated servicesThe project will operate in 6 Governorates and 9 districts: Hodieda:Az Zuhra - WGSS + RH supplies (Zuhra hospital), Al Luhaya - referrals + CEmONC (Alluhaya hospital)Hajjah: Abs - WGSS + BEmONC (Robo Matwala HC), Aslam – WGSS + BEmONC (Bani-Zaid Aslm), Mustaba - WGSS+ BEmONC (Al Khames HC)Marib: Marib AlWadi - WGSS + CEmONC (Kara hospital)Lahj: Tuban - WGSS +CVATaizz: AlMakha – GBV and RH referrals +CVA Amanat AlAsimah: Bani AlHarith – referrals +BEmONC (Bait Handal)

title: Protection, shelter/NFI, and CCCM support to vulnerable displaced populations in Yemen
description: This intervention will contribute to scaling-up multi-sectoral support for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host community members and households.UNHCR and partners will promote protection outcomes for vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host community households through protection, shelter and NFI, and CCCM interventions. These interventions will strengthen capacities to exercise rights, to access essential services, to address basic needs, and ensure safer and more dignified living conditions, thus mitigating the need to resort to harmful coping mechanisms. Overall, a total of 11,435 households are expected to benefit from the project’s interventions which will include 2,000 instances of support to access civil documentation, 2,000 instances of legal assistance (including 1,000 instances using a cash modality), MPCA to 3,000 households, provision of 1,800 NFI kits, provision 1,700 emergency shelter kits (using a cash modality), provision of cash for maintenance of 1,200 shelters, and improvements to at least 7 IDP hosting sites benefitting at least 5,000 households (the final interventions will be defined based on the site assessments and based on the needs identified: interventions might, for example, include WASH interventions to improve access to water for the camp population).  The interventions will target IDPs, returnees, and host community members identified as vulnerable and in need of assistance.Legal assistance and civil documentation are crucial in Yemen. Without documentation, vulnerable individuals are often unable to access basic rights and crucial, life-saving public services and humanitarian assistance. For example, documentation is required for IDPs to access WFP’s general food distribution programme. Legal assistance needed is often required in order to obtain civil documentation due to complications and missing pre-requisite documentation.
