title: Provision of Urgent Camp Coordination and Camp Management, Shelter and Health Services in Ma’rib Al Wadi and Hays
description: The proposed intervention will aim to address immediate needs of IDP, and host community populations severely impacted by recent weather incidents (flooding and violent windstorms) and residing in acute watery diarrhea (AWD)/ cholera hotspots. IOM will implement critical Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) and Health assistance in Al Hudaydah (Hays district) and Ma’rib (Ma’rib Alwadi). A total of 36,197 individuals will benefit from these services in target locations.In Hays, to contribute to the broader AWD / cholera response in the district, IOM will support the operation of the established Diarrheal Treatment Center (DTC, previously supported by ICRC) to ensure continued capacity to manage AWD and suspected cholera cases. The DTC services are expected to directly benefit 3,000 IDPs and host community members with AWD treatment, while 2,100 people will benefit from awareness raising.  Further, in recognition of largely unmet needs in informal/ unmanaged settlements in Hays, IOM will provide CCCM and SNFI assistance in two new sites (Al Qulma, and Al Haet). The targeted sites will be supported with site registration, establishment of community management structures and Cash for Shelter/ Transitional Shelter services. A total of 12,005 individuals are expected to benefit from CCCM support in Hays, and 2,898 from shelter support. Overall, a total of 15,005 individuals will benefit from IOM’s multisectoral support in Hays.  In Ma’rib, IOM will implement CCCM activities in Al Ezz camp, Al Ramsah, An Nour, Asit, Saylat Almil, Ma’rib Al Wadi, one of the districts severely impacted by violent windstorms and flooding in August 2024. Activities to be implemented will include essential risk reduction works, such as rehabilitation and/ or construction of risk reduction infrastructure (soil embankments, Gabion walls) as well as awareness raising and deployment of emergency committees to ensure sites have the capacity to mitigate impact of severe weather incidents. In addition, IOM will support target households across displacement sites in Ma’rib Al Wadi with transitional shelters, or Cash for Shelter assistance, restoring safe and dignified living conditions that were destroyed in recent weeks. A total of 17,195 individuals will benefit from CCCM services and 3,997 from shelter services in Ma’rib Al Wadi. Overall, 21,192 individuals in Ma’rib Al Wadi will benefit from activities implemented under this intervention.

title: Provision of targeted emergency food assistance (TEFA) to vulnerable food insecure populations in North Yemen
description: This project aims to support the provision, procurement and distribution of wheat flour to food insecure populations in North Yemen through the Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) activity. Yemen remains among the world's most food insecure countries with 64% of households unable to access food (inadequate food consumption levels). Specifically in the North, 65% of households reported inadequate food consumption levels. As of August, this was the fourth consecutive month of a steady increase in food insecurity. In the North, WFP has implemented a pause in its General Food Distribution activities to agree with authorities on a way forward on a retargeting and registration pilot, while WFP was able to successfully carry out a retargeting pilot, the funding constraints increased, leading WFP to pivot its programming. The previous General Food Assistance activity will not resume and will be replaced by a Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) project. The key drivers of Yemen’s food crisis include the ongoing economic decline caused by conflict, which has led to inflation, currency devaluation, and the collapse of basic services. Compounding this, the pause in humanitarian food assistance since December 2023 has left many vulnerable households without support. Before the pause, half of the population in these areas relied on food distributions, and the suspension of aid has pushed many into extreme coping strategies. Additionally, climate shocks, such as flooding, have heightened food insecurity, particularly in agriculture-dependent households that are highly vulnerable to such disruptions.In response to these hardships, families in northern Yemen are adopting increasingly desperate measures. More than 50 percent of households are resorting to harmful coping strategies, including reducing food portions, skipping meals, borrowing food or money, and sacrificing adult meals so children can eat. Some families are even forced to sell off valuable assets or risk their lives by sending young men to the frontlines to earn an income.The food security crisis in northern Yemen has reached critical levels, with millions of people at risk. Immediate and sustained humanitarian assistance is essential to prevent further deterioration and alleviate the severe suffering caused by widespread hunger and malnutrition.The new Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) activity aims to reach up to 6 million affected people (as opposed to the 9.5 million prior to the pause). This significant reduction would be based on a geographically focused approach aimed at ensuring that aid reaches the most vulnerable while WFP continues the targeting and registration process in prioritized areas for assistance. With current funding, WFP can only provide food assistance for 2.6 million people in the most affected districts. The goal is to gradually increase and expand to 6 million people as resources allow.WFP will procure 4825.4 MT of wheat flour and reach 675,558 affected people with this allocation. The targeted governorates and districts are the following:Al Bayda: Ash Sharyah, Nati, Radman, Numan, As SawadiyahAl Hodeidah: Al Qanawis, Jabal Ras, Bura, Al HujjaylahAmran: Dhulaymat Habur, Al Ashah, Maswar, Qaflat Odhar, Suwayr, As SudahHajjah: Khayran Al Muharraq, Bani Qays, Washhah, Bakil Al Mir, Aflah Ash Sham, Qarah, Al Maghrabah, Aflah Al YamanRaymah: Bilad Attaam, As SalafiyyahAt the operationalization strategy, WFP was planning on using the CERF allocation for the procurement of 3 separate commodities. However, after careful review of the pipeline, the decision was made to focus on the procurement of wheat flour solely to ensure that all gaps are covered. To this end, the planned number of targeted people has been reviewed to reflect the new level of reach, which is slightly over twice the estimate. This will allow WFP to reach more affected people, maximize the impact and effectively manage available funds and delivery of assistance.

title: Lifesaving response to worsening malnutrition, and disease outbreaks in most affected districts of Yemen
description: HealthThrough this project, WHO contributes to controlling outbreaks of cholera, diphtheria, measles, dengue, and other epidemic-prone diseases. Targeting 179,024 individuals across 14 districts in 9 governorates, the project employs an integrated health response to mitigate disease burdens, improve case management, and ultimately reduce morbidity and mortality associated with these diseases.Key Activities:Outbreak Alert Investigation and Detection:Equip 25 RRTs with essential supplies, enabling timely diagnosis and outbreak control in high-risk areas. Each team comprises five health workers and will conduct 318 field missions.Procure and distribute diagnostic testing kits to Central Public Health Laboratories in Sana’a and Aden for rapid identification of cholera, measles, diphtheria, and dengue.Improving Case Management:Provide refresher training for 75 healthcare workers on managing severe cases of communicable diseases to enhance early diagnosis and treatment.Distribute essential medicines, including antibiotics and IV fluids, to targeted health facilities in high-risk areas.Operationalize four DTCs for three months and establish ten additional centers as needed, informed by outbreak dynamics.Conduct regular supervisory visits (252 over six months) by WHO and MOH to monitor response activities.Procure emergency medical supplies to cover the needs of 140,000 individuals for IPC and WASH Practices:Improve WASH and IPC measures in 15 health facilities, including 4 DTCs, through the distribution of necessary supplies.Implement 28 hygiene promotion campaigns across 14 districts to raise awareness about disease prevention, complemented by 100,000 informational materials.Nutrition Under the nutrition sector, the project aims to reduce mortality and morbidity from acute malnutrition in children under five, particularly those facing multiple underlying causes such as childhood diseases, low immunization rates (53%), poor feeding practices, limited access to safe water, inadequate sanitation, and high food insecurity. In response to this critical situation, WHO is leading the provision of care for SAM/MC in inpatient settings across the country, especially in areas with IDPs Key Activities:Provision of operational support for the targeted TFCs: WHO is supporting 14 TFCs in targeted districts, with plans to expand services to an additional facility in Mawzaa, Taiz.Funding will cover performance-based service delivery costs for health workers (pediatricians, nurses, etc.), ensuring TFCs operate 24/7 and can effectively identify and treat children with malnutrition and related medical complications.Comprehensive Support Package:Provision of essential resources to TFCs, including clean water, meals for caregivers, cleaning supplies, laboratory tests, and stationery to maintain quality care.Free medication for all children treated in TFCs through the distribution of SAM/PED kits, ensuring comprehensive medical support for 50 cases per kit.Case Identification and Nutritional Assessment:Targeting a caseload of 5,692 children suffering from SAM/MC, WHO aims to enhance case identification by integrating nutritional assessments into various maternal and child health services across secondary health facilities.Expansion of routine nutrition sentinel sites (NSS) from 17 to 21 facilities in 15 districts, with a goal of assessing 30,000 children under five and 19,974 pregnant and lactating women (PLW) for malnutrition.Inpatient Case Management Training:Capacity-building for health workers on SAM/MC management to improve inpatient care quality, including procurement of necessary kitchenware for therapeutic milk preparation and WASH items to ensure infection control.Ongoing Technical Support and Supervision:WHO will conduct regular on-the-job mentoring and supervision to ensure adherence to operational guidelines in all supported TFCs, including training on identifying and referring women in need of MHPSS.

title: XXX029N Strengthening Community Capacity 3 (implementation)
description:
CARE Nederland and CARE Yemen, together with consortium partners, RNW Media and SOS Center for Youth Capabilities Development (SOS), formed a Consortium’, to implement the program titled ‘Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) in Yemen. The overall aim of this program is to improve women’s meaningful influence in relief, recovery and peace processes in Yemen, in Taiz and Eden. The program will contribute to all three sub-objectives of the Dutch WPS grant instrument, including strengthening the protection for women, addressing harmful social norms, and increasing opportunities for women’s meaningful participation in relief, recovery, and peacebuilding, as well as supporting the priorities of the Netherlands Cooperation in Yemen. The program also supports the implementation of sustainable development goals (SDGs) 5 and 16, focusing on gender equality and on peaceful and inclusive societies, respectively.  
The goals of the NAP are particularly relevant for Yemen’s ongoing, multi-track peace process. To varying degrees, the peace process engages women via Track 1, which involves official diplomatic efforts and formal negotiations; Track 2, which involves consultations with civil society organizations (CSOs). And Track 3, which refers to community-level initiatives for peacebuilding and conflict prevention. The Consortium’s WPS programming aims to strengthen the involvement of women in the different tracks of the peace process (with more emphasis on tracks 2 and 3) and women’s role in relief and recovery. Moreover, it aims to strengthen women’s protection from SGBV and influence social norms that constrain or undermine women’s participation and protection to build a more supportive environment for women’s inclusion in peace and security.

The TOC is built around three sub-objectives and four domains of change.
Sub-Objective 1: More equitable social norms and related practices
Sub-Objective 2: Enhanced protection for women
Sub- Objective 3: More inclusive relief, recovery, and peace processes

Domain of Change 1: Civil society is capable, representative, engaged in collective action
Domain of Change 2: Male awareness and support to women’s contributions and leadership
Domain of Change 3: Powerholders are more supportive to women
Domain of Change 4: Women are empowered to influence relief/recovery/peacebuilding

title: YEM035N Yemen Joint Response 2022-23
description: This is a 2-year Yemen Joint Response, consisting of 7 YJR members and 9 local partners. The Joint Response for 2022-2023 has been designed according to identified priority governorates, based on those where humanitarian needs and gaps are known to be high and where members have access and presence to implement, either directly or with local partners, or a combination. As in previous years of the Yemen JR, the overall objective of this programme is to provide multi-sectoral and integrated life-saving humanitarian support to people in need, prioritising the most vulnerable population, and facilitate early recovery and resilience of conflict population in Yemen, while ensuring that all activities promote equitable access to assistance for women, girls, boys, and men.

title: YEM038N Yemen Joint Response 2024-2026
description:
The 2024–2026 Yemen Joint Response (YJR) is a three-year, multi-sectoral intervention developed to address significant humanitarian needs and persistent gaps identified through individual needs assessments, secondary data analysis, and cluster consultations, particularly in governorates with the highest severity of needs and concentration of affected populations, namely Sa’ada, Hajjah, Marib, Taiz, Lahj, Aden, and Al Dhale’e. 

The response is implemented by a consortium of 20 organizations, including 7 members of the Dutch Relief Alliance (DRA) and 13 partners—12 local and 1 international—reflecting a strong commitment to locally led action within a coordinated international framework. Designed in line with the YJR Protracted Crisis Mechanism (PCM) guidelines, the programme delivers an integrated package of life-saving assistance across Health, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Protection, and Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC), with protection mainstreaming embedded throughout to ensure safe, inclusive, and equitable access for women, girls, boys, men, and persons with disabilities. 

The overall purpose is to provide immediate, life-saving humanitarian support to the most vulnerable populations while simultaneously promoting early recovery and strengthening the resilience of conflict-affected communities. In the longer term, the intervention aims to reduce vulnerability, enhance communities’ capacity to cope with ongoing and future shocks, and support a transition toward more sustainable and self-reliant livelihoods. 

This programme also incorporates the previously named YEM039N project: LOCAL-Lead, which was approved as a top-up to YEM038N by the DRA.

title: Public service infrastructure development project in Yemen
description: More than nine years of conflict in Yemen has destabilized communities, led to mass displacement and left millions of households grappling to meet their most basic needs. Local authorities and public service providers continued to lack resources and capacity to provide basic services, notably in areas hosting large, displaced populations. With the objective of increasing the resilience of communities to destabilizing forces stemming from the ongoing conflict, and competition for scarce resources and services, this project will improve local public service infrastructure and support social cohesion among diverse community members. Through ongoing interventions and existent community networks, IOM has identified water sanitation and hygiene (WASH), health and education infrastructure rehabilitation activities and will conduct further consultations and assessments at the start of the project to select community infrastructure projects that improve service provision and alleviate tensions in communities due to lack thereof. IOM is also conducting community building activities to further support communities in building channels for conflict resolution and trust building, so that communities are equipped to address future conflicts and stay resilient to polarizing influences.

title: Supporting vocational training for youth, including internally displaced persons
description: This project aims to rehabilitate and reactivate six Technical and Vocational Training Centres (TVTCs) in Aden, Lahj, and Ta'iz. This intervention will focus on infrastructure rehabilitation, including classrooms, workshops, and gender-segregated WASH facilities. Additional efforts will include equipping training centres with tools and appliances, improving accessibility for people with disabilities, and installing solar power systems for sustainable electricity. The project will promote sustainable, gender-inclusive livelihoods by providing vocational training and technical skills development to conflict-affected populations. A market-based approach will enhance employment opportunities, particularly for women, fostering inclusive workforce participation. By empowering individuals with practical skills and supporting small businesses, this initiative aims to improve resilience, economic stability, and long-term social development in Yemen's most vulnerable communities. Lastly, the project will ensure the sustainability of the targeted TVTCs by conducting capacity-building trainings for TVTC teaching staff. This will allow to ensure that the teaching staff is supported through the improved infrastructure of TVTCs and capacity-building initiatives, empowering them to deliver lessons that are effective and engaging, and make the most of the school facilities.

title: Supporting the continuity of education services and recovery of the education sector from the impacts of crisis and displacement inAden, Lahj, and Ta’iz governorates
description: The education system in Yemen has suffered from years of conflict and seasonal floods that have caused extensive damage to infrastructure including schools, thereby reducing access to educational services for children. The objective of the project is to contribute to the continuity, improvement of education services in crisis and displacement affected communities in Aden, Lahj and Ta'iz governorates. The project also aims to mitigate tensions in displacement affected communities due to competition for limited services and resources through expanding the capacity of schools to accommodate a larger number of students, including students among internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities.

title: Enhanced water resource management in IDP communities – phase III
description: Despite extensive efforts to improve access to water in Yemen, the country remains one of the most water scarce countries in the world. Depleting natural resources and more frequent cycles of severe weather are making water less available for agricultural and domestic use. The water crisis in Yemen has the potential to contribute to the country's instability and to further exacerbate existing vulnerabilities faced by host, internally displaced persons, and migrant populations. This three-year program improves the immediate access to water supply, irrigation infrastructure at the watershed level, and community-led resource and conflict management to improve the overall resilience of target communities (with a focus on areas hosting large, displaced populations) to cyclical shocks.

title: Meeting critical needs of migrants in situations of vulnerability, internally displaced persons and host communities in Yemen
description: Severe humanitarian needs remain across Yemen, especially for families living in protracted displacement, conflict-affected host community members and vulnerable migrants. In 2024, an escalation in conflict, disease outbreak and severe weather incidents greatly impacted numerous already vulnerable households in Yemen, leading to more than 19 million individuals in need of assistance in 2025. The proposed multisectoral intervention ensures the most vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs), host community members, and migrants throughout the country have access to core services to meet urgent needs and contribute to safe and dignified living conditions. The intervention not only addresses immediate needs but also contributes to reducing dependency on humanitarian assistance by promoting local ownership, integrating progressive exit strategies from emergency solutions, and building productive capacities of vulnerable households, in addition, to supporting displaced populations outside of sites and the surrounding host community.

title: Joint implementation programme for improving access to safe water supply services for internally displaced persons and host communities, Ma'rib, Yemen
description: According to the 2025 Humanitarian Needs Overview, an estimated 19.5 million people need humanitarian assistance in Yemen, among whom 17 million are in need of water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. For more than nine years, the country has been crippled by large-scale displacement driven by conflict and a deteriorating economy in recent times as a result of inflation. In line with the national Cluster WASH strategy, IOM seeks to contribute to safe and dignified living conditions by improving access to water supply services in target areas. IOM's approach under this project will consist of first-line WASH interventions to respond to the immediate water supply needs of target populations in Ma'rib.

title: Improving living conditions for internally displaced persons and their host communities in Ma’rib
description: The multi-sectoral project addresses urgent gaps in Ma'rib City and Ma'rib Alwadi. Ma'rib has become a critical hub for displaced populations in Yemen, hosting one of the largest concentrations of displaced people in the country. The rapid growth of displacement has placed immense pressure on infrastructure and basic services. Through this project, Health services are being strengthened through provision of medical supplies, essential equipment, and mental health and psychosocial support. Rehabilitation of water and sanitation systems will provide safe, sustainable access to clean water and hygiene facilities reducing waterborne disease risks.  In parallel, transitional shelters and essential non-food items will protect vulnerable households from environmental hazards. The project will also rehabilitate and upgrade school facilities, ensuring safe, secure learning spaces for children in displacement-affected communities. Community-led infrastructure upgrades, enhancement of electrical connections and disaster risk reduction interventions will protect internally displaced persons and host communities from natural hazards in flood-prone locations.

title: Life-saving preparedness and response to WASH emergencies through common WASH pipeline and enhanced access to clean water and sanitation facilities
description: Over the past year, multiple emergencies, including acute watery (AWD)/cholera outbreaks, malnutrition crises, and floods caused by heavy rains, have left large segments of the affected population in Yemen without adequate support. This has been particularly due to gaps in the prepositioning of essential items needed for rapid distribution. It is anticipated that this year the humanitarian needs will only increase; however, significant shortages of Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) items persist across several districts. Through this project, IOM is providing essential WASH assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host community members in high-risk areas across nine districts in four governorates: Abyan, Hadramawt, Ibb, and Taiz. This intervention is designed to implement urgent prevention and response measures for waterborne and communicable disease outbreaks, which are exacerbated by flooding, displacement, and poor sanitation. Through the distribution of emergency WASH pipeline supplies—including hygiene kits, water storage items, and water purification tablets prepositioned in IOM warehouses—the project ensures the rapid, efficient, and timely delivery of lifesaving supplies via the WASH Common Pipeline Tracking System, implemented through local WASH Cluster partners.

title: Provision of immediate life-saving food assistance to severely food insecure women, men, girls and boys across Yemen
description: The main objective of this project is to provide life-saving food security assistance to vulnerable communities in 12 governates. This WFP project provides voucher assistance to 2.285 million people, including 607,000 women, 626,000 men, and over 1,000,000 children. This project is part of an $80 million CERF allocation to support cash programming in response to increasing food insecurity in 6 countries.

title: Lifesaving support for nutrition and WASH services in Yemen
description:
Under the proposed activities, UNICEF will provide life-saving nutrition and WASH support to vulnerable communities in Yemen. UNICEF will target 435,394 children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) with activities in support of overall nutritional status and 3 million people will benefit from Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities to support access to safe water. The dual-pronged approach of support to both nutrition and WASH is imperative to support to overall better health of the Yemeni population.

Nutrition activities include screening and referral of children under 5 and pregnant and lactating mothers to prevent further nutritional deterioration. Therapeutic treatment will be provided to children who are referred for treatment, through the procurement and delivery of therapeutic food and medicines.

Building on previous UNICEF WASH intervention achievements in Yemen with different donors’ support, the proposed project aims to enhance UNICEF Emergency WASH interventions to improve and sustain WASH service provision in conflict affected and vulnerable communities in Sana'a, Marib, Mukalla, Lahj, Ataq, Hudaida, Hajjah, Saada, Al Jawf Ibb, Taizz, Dhamar, Amran, Al Mahweet, Raimeh governorates in Yemen  and preventing the disease such as cholera, and COVID_19 spread in at risk communities. WASH service provision is a key underpinning to the general health of the population of Yemen, mitigating risk of disease thorough access to safe drinking water, and sanitation and hygiene.

title: Providing the Minimum Initial Service Package for Reproductive Health (RH) to the most vulnerable women and girls in Yemen
description:
Access to and availability of maternal and new-born health services has been grossly undermined by the protracted crisis.  The combination of YER depreciation, food insecurity, and the COVID-19 pandemic has led to greatly increased vulnerabilities of women of reproductive age particularly pregnant women. According to the WHO Health Resources Availability Monitoring System (HeRAMS) conducted in 2018, only 20 percent of health facilities in Yemen provided maternal and new-born health services, a decrease from 37 percent reported in 2016. UNFPA field assessments have confirmed gaps in RH services that require urgent interventions such as staffing, equipment, and medicine needed for providing life-saving Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (EmONC) services. 

CERF will directly lead to the resumption of critical life-saving RH services in 55 health facilities in districts with the highest severity indices. All the targeted facilities stopped providing these critical services on May 16th due to UNFPA's funding shortage. The supported facilities will provide women and girls with the life-saving essential reproductive health services, particularly those related to complicated deliveries and care for survivors of Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) and Sexual Violence. CERF will also support 100 community midwives and outreach teams. These teams will be reaching the most vulnerable women and girls in the most remote areas.

Additionally, the project will be complemented by GBV mitigation and response interventions within the targeted health facilities. It will also be complemented by the Cash and Voucher Assistance interventions UNFPA implements to enhance the accessibility of those in the most remote areas to services.

title: Provision of essential and lifesaving health services for vulnerable population
description:
The project will support Minimum Services Packages (MSP), Therapeutic Feeding Center(TFC) and Trauma care in targeted health facilities. 

The support to the MSP will focus on 21 health facilities located in Lahji, Ibb and Al Dhale governorates. This intervention will aim to providing essential medical services to over 274,000 people. Essential medical services are those defined as per first line response under the Yemen Humanitarian Response Plan (YHRP): primary care including ante-natal and post-natal care, lifesaving services requiring surgical consultations and treatment of severely acute malnourished children under five.

The CERF allocation will target 90 therapeutic feeding centres directly supported by WHO, covering 222 high priority districts in 22 governorates by providing essential drugs (SAM kits) and admission kits; these kits are gender responsive and child friendly as they include hygiene items for mothers and children when SAM children are admitted to the TFCs and other essential products like baby clothing to reduce the economic burden on families during the SAM children’ admission period. WHO will be targeting 23,428 SAM children along with their caregivers (mothers) with counselling on Infant and Young Child Feeding-IYCF, infection prevention and control measures and for breastfeeding in COVID_19.

The project will ensure access of integrated trauma care through providing trauma care package and continuity of care at supported hospitals setting up life-saving integrated trauma system; strengthen the capacity of trauma surgeons and health staff working in supported hospitals to effectively manage trauma emergency care service; providing trauma medical supplies for 23 hospitals.

description: The overall objective of the project is: 1- Providing basic diagnostic tools for malaria and arthropod-borne viral diseases. 2- Reactivation of quality assurance and quality control for malaria control in 100 health facilities 3- Purchase of 40,000 boxes of malaria rapid diagnostic tests, Pf/Pan antigens, HRP2/pLDH, 25 kit 4- Purchase of 4,000 boxes of rapid diagnostic tests (NS1 and IgM) for detection of severe dengue cases 5- Purchase of ELISA equipment for detection of dengue, chikungunya fever and West Nile virus 6- Purchase of RT-PCR kits (reagents) for arthropod-borne viral diseases. 7. reporting: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre
title: Additional financial support supplement for the project to expand the cholera response throughout Yemen
description: Overall Project Objective: This project provides additional financial support to the project to expand the cholera response throughout Yemen, bringing the total amount allocated to combating the cholera epidemic in Yemen to $5 million. This comes as a result of the continued widespread cholera epidemic in Yemen, which has posed a significant challenge to the Yemeni Ministry of Health and public health programs. The project aims to reduce cholera-related mortality rates and support hospitals and health centers with medicines, intravenous solutions, and antibiotics to treat cases. The project also includes various activities related to investigation, environmental sanitation, water, and community education, in addition to supporting the organization's efforts in vaccination campaigns throughout Yemen.

title: Multi-sectoral Marib crisis response
description:
In response to the crisis, UNICEF will:

- Support the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) as first line WASH response to provide life-saving assistance to newly displaced populations across the active frontlines in Ma’rib.
- Assist vulnerable children with essential child protection services such as lifesaving service provisions through case management systems, psychosocial support, and mine risk education/ awareness. 
- UNICEF will also ensure the availability of life saving health interventions through the provision of vaccination and essential health services in conflict affected areas in Marib and Al Jawf to under five children through Integrated Out Reach (IOR) and Mobile Teams (MT) and Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) services to under five children. title: Providing emergency RH services, GBV mitigation and response services, and RRM for the most vulnerable people from Marib and Al Jawf.
description: Recent trend analyses of gender-based violence indicate increased numbers of women and girls (widows, orphans) engaging in negative coping mechanisms (especially child marriage) and an increase in reported cases of sexual violence, physical and psychological assault. GBV partners have seen an increased demand for GBV services by 37%. Furthermore, the UNFPA-led Rapid Response Mechanism estimates that 23% of those newly displaced are female-headed households. \nWith the current conflict, the health system in Yemen has almost collapsed, with only half of the facilities functional. Majority of those still functional face severe shortages of medicines, equipment and staff. Most of the health staff have not been paid government salaries for the last five years. This has naturally led to a deterioration in all the key reproductive health indicators. \nThe CERF funding will lead to three key outputs. First, it will allow 16 health facilities to provide emergency obstetric and neonatal care services. This will directly lead to the continuation of critical life-saving RH services in health facilities in districts with the highest severity indices in Marib and Al Jawf. CERF will also support seven safe spaces to provide survivor-centered multi-sectoral services (case management, psychosocial, medical, legal, livelihood) and a safe shelter for women and girls, which is a key intervention which can be life-saving. Both safe spaces and shelters provide the multi-sectorial services to the most vulnerable women and girls. However, the safe shelters also provide accommodation for the additionally vulnerable and/or face life-threatening situations or intense forms of GBV, and have no other resort. This project will also support the RRM in assistaing those newly displaced from Marib and Al Jawf with immediate life-saving assistance. The Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) provides immediate in-kind assistance (Immediate Response Rations from WFP, basic hygiene kits from UNICEF and dignity kits from UNFPA) to newly displaced persons and those impacted by natural disasters within 72 hours of receiving the displacement alert.

title: Provide life-saving shelter/NFI assistance and protection services to families displaced by conflict in Marib and Al Jawf
description:
UNHCR will lead urgent interventions to improve the living conditions of 204,000 displaced Yemenis in Marib and 53,000 displaced Yemenis in Al Jawf, affected by the recent conflict escalation.

Through protection interventions, UNHCR will conduct vulnerability assessments as basis for referrals to protection services, operate a community center from which legal assistance, psychosocial support (PSS), child protection and GBV services will be delivered; and provide emergency cash assistance to highly vulnerable displaced persons with specific and urgent needs not covered by the broader multi-purpose cash assistance in Marib governorate.

In Al-Jawf, UNHCR will implement five quick impact projects in the informal IDP hosting sites with the largest population concentration. The projects will promote social cohesion, contribute to address GBV risks faced by women and girls while accessing hygiene facilities (segregated latrines for women) and improve the accessibility on the sites for persons with disabilities, older persons and pregnant women.    The QIPs proposed by UNHCR are focused on enhancing social cohesion among the host community and IDPs while also addressing major critical protection risks. 

With respect to shelter, UNHCR will assist the most vulnerable displaced families in Marib, in urgent need of help to pay their rent and avoid imminent eviction with rental subsidy assistance. Through the procurement and distribution of emergency shelters and NFI kits, UNHCR will support a swift response to families newly displaced in both governorates.

title: Providing emergency water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and health assistance, and a humanitarian hub for aid operations in \\Ma’rib governorate
description:
With support from CERF, IOM will contribute towards improving access and service delivery in conflict affected Ma’rib by operating the humanitarian hub. The humanitarian hub is a critical enabler of the rapid delivery of humanitarian services for internally displaced persons (IDPs), migrants and host communities in Ma’rib. The facility will provide at least 120 office workspaces, 40 accommodation spaces, as well as common services such as security, internet, conference facilities, a clinic, transportation and evacuation capacity, for at least 10 UN Agencies and several other humanitarian partners (INGOs) based on needs.

With support from CERF, and through the hub IOM will also carry out critical WASH and Health activities. Under its WASH programme, IOM will implement first-line WASH interventions to respond to the immediate and lifesaving needs of internally displaced people in Ma’rib. IOM will target 15,500 conflict-affected people  with WASH assistance.

CERF funding will also be critical for expanding critical health services (including the provision and procurement of essential medicines and equipment) to cover the widespread needs amongst IDPs and host communities in Ma’rib. IOM will contribute towards reducing avoidable morbidity and mortality through the provision of emergency, primary and secondary health services (including nutrition screenings due to the risk of famine and extreme hunger in Yemen) to vulnerable populations in response to the acute needs. Project activities (which will include providing a minimum package of services (MSP)  in  two hospitals, one health center, and six mobile teams) will support an estimated 59,663 IDPs, migrants and host community members.

title: Additional security support for expansion of the humanitarian operations in specific area in Yemen
description: The Humanitarian Country Team is addressing the humanitarian situation in Yemen, especially in the Southern and Northern Governorates. One of the components to enable the implementation of the  operation is security support and coordination, which will enable humanitarian missions to be conducted in a safe and secure manner especially in very high security risk areas.\n\nThe objective of the project is to provide dedicated safety security support as facilities assessment, road movements advisories, manual security clearance, organizing and enable security escorts, issuance of security advisories rather than movements, mission tracking, general/particular security assessment for specific areas, advise on personnel ceiling and/or curfew hours, liaison with national authorities in order to facilitate the expanded lifesaving humanitarian operations to create safety and security conditions and to deploy the necessary UN suppor,t enabling effective delivery of humanitarian assistance in the affected regions.

title: Provision of humanitarian air services and emergency telecommunication services to the humanitarian community in Yemen
description: Following escalation of conflict, the lack of provision of air transport and logistics were identified in the Marib response plan as key limitations of effective response. Therefore, WFP UNHAS added a weekly connection to Marib to its routing to allow improved humanitarian access to the area. Part of the requirement to deliver the assistance is to continue the regular air service to Ma’rib and put in place the arrangements required to make the air strip operational. Necessary support requirements to conduct these flights include staff to manage UNHAS operational related tasks in Safer. CERF funds will be complemented by other donor funding to allow for the continuation of the service not only to Marib, but also in and out of the country to allow humanitarian to reach populations in need, in e.g. Marib and Al Jawf. \n\nWith the openings of the hubs/ETC sites in Mokha, Hajjah and Marib, the ETC supports the humanitarian response to vulnerable, conflict affected populations in the most difficult to reach areas. Following the escalation of conflict in Marib, ETC received additional requests such as assist with provision of solar power for the IT equipment in the Marib hub, appoint a dedicated IT staff for user support, set-up the UNDSS radio room. This allocation would support the connectivity contract to ensure connectivity in humanitarian hubs, as well as UNDSS radio rooms, vital to continue the humanitarian response in Yemen.

title: Provision of essential and lifesaving health services in response to the conflict in Marib and Al Jawf
description: The project builds on WHO's previous CERF project (UFE), in particular the support for Minimum Services Package (MSP) and trauma care in targeted health facilities. The project also covesr the provision of basic operational needs (i.e., fuel and water) for the health facilities, trauma care related refresher training, as well as blood bank services supporting trauma care.  \n\nThe support to the MSP focuses on 5 health facilities located in Marib governorate This engagement aims to provide essential medical services to 238,444 affected people. Essential medical services are intended to be in line with the Yemen Humanitarian Response Plan (YHRP), in particular, that access of vulnerable populations including IDPs to the Minimum Health Service Package is increased. The project also aims to strengthen the health system and operational support to health facilities including through fuel and water and the provision of essential support to critically needed lifesaving trauma care services.
