description: Yemen is facing a chronic humanitarian crisis. This is exacerbated by recurring conflict and displacement, water scarcity, soaring food prices and high rates of malnutrition and disease. Given the political and economic instability in country, humanitarian assistance is going to be required in Yemen for the foreseeable future. The scale of need exceeds the capacity of the government, and to some extent the humanitarian community, to respond. This project is therefore being developed to provide further support and development to in country structures for effective humanitarian preparedness and response.

title: Integrated Emergency WASH Response in Abyan-Yemen
description: The project will provide access to the basic water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services, this will be done through construction of new and/or rehabilitation of existing water supply facilities by installing water distribution networks, fittings boreholes and wells with pumps and generators, establishment and capacity building of water management committees, communities training on best hygiene practices, in addition to support communities to construct sanitation facilities.

title: Yemen Crisis Response in Hajjah and Hodeidah Governorates 2015
description: Due to prolonged crisis, malnutrition was prevalent in the country. Oxfam provides cash assistance to vulnerable House Holds to fulfill basic food and non -food needs. These communities are provided hygiene awareness sessions to reduce health risks. Oxfam has comparative advantage because of its organisational competence in cash transfer programming. Through early recovery interventions, Oxfam will also aim at improving the livelihoods conditions of targeted communities through provision of productive assets with required means and skills.

title: Emergency Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Livelihood response in Amran
description: Yemen is facing a chronic humanitarian crisis  owing to the protracted conflict evolved within itself  since a long period of time, however  this situation has  been exacerbated as a result of interference of external factors, particularly Saudi -led coalition airstrikes which began on 26 March 2015,  the United Nation (UN) report issued on 30 June 2015 estimated 1,019,762  people have been internally displaced and 3,083 persons registered dead and 14,324 registered injured resulting from the on -going conflict since beginning of the airstrikes on 26th March. The humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate at alarming rate, as violence increases and basic services grind to a halt. Food, water and health systems are collapsing rapidly as a result of the conflict and the siege imposed by the coalition onto the country including closure of airspace, seaports which prohibit import of critical supplies such as commercial imports of  food, fuel and medical supplies into the country.   Critical fuel shortages are now shutting down Yemen's Local water infrastructures, leaving millions of people without access to clean water. Therefore, the  main objectives of this intervention  is to contribute to diminishing risks related to shortage of water, sanitation ,hygiene and livelihood  for the Internally Displaced Persons and hosting communities in Amran governorate, through set of activities which include emergency water trucking,  rehabilitation/construction of water and sanitation facilities and dissemination of hygiene messages  as well as supporting vulnerable people affected by protracted conflict and economical crisis with emergency food security and livelihood options to recover from their shock.

title: Emergency, Water,Sanitation, Hygiene and livelihood response in Taiz
description: The protracted crisis in Yemen was exacerbated by the latest interference of external factors, i.e. Saudi -led coalition airstrikes and the siege stopping imports of food, fuel and medical supplies, and has made the situation on the ground much worse in the last few months. So, the  main objectives of this intervention  is to contribute to diminishing risks related to shortage of water, sanitation ,hygiene and livelihood  for the Internally Displaced Persons and hosting communities in Amran governorate  , through set of activities which include emergency water trucking,  rehabilitation/construction of water and sanitation facilities and dissemination of hygiene messages  as well as supporting vulnerable people affected by protracted conflict and economical crisis with emergency food security and livelihood options to recover from their shock.

title: Improving the living conditions of the conflict affected population in Taiz
description: Oxfam will build on its ongoing integrated humanitarian programme and presence in Taiz to reach 55,840 women, men, boys and girls in the most food insecure districts of Taiz through an integrated programme of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and food security. Food security will be ensured through the adoption of a nutrition focused approach that will be developed in collaboration with nutrition experts such as IMC and Mercy Corps to ensure targeting of the most vulnerable households. Conditional transfers will be distributed to 1,500 households (HH's) on the condition of their participation in nutrition sessions and referrals to health clinics and will be complemented by awareness raising sessions as part of Oxfam's hygiene activities. Furthermore, 55,000 individuals will benefit from improved access to safe, equitable and sustainable water, sanitation and hygiene facilities. Assistance will be provided 500 HH to purchase hygiene kits and, furthermore, cash for work opportunities will be made available to conflict affected individuals to carry out minor rehabilitation of water supply schemes in order to meet household requirements. Oxfam will also support local water corporations and General Authority for Rural Water Projects (GARWAP) to carry out major rehabilitation of water supply schemes.

title: Yemen Joint Response 3
description: The project will focus on increasing access to basic food needs for most vulnerable conflict affected House Holds (HHs) through conditional and unconditional cash transfer as well as ensuring protection and gender mainstreamed throughout the project.. The project has three main objectives which includes  • Targeting women, men , boys and girls affected by conflict have increased access to food  • Target women, men , boys and girls affected by conflict have protected and restored livelihood opportunities  • Community based protection network improved to reduce the risk among Internally Displaced Persons (IDPS) and Host communities (HC)  .       Improved access to safe water, safe sanitation and hygiene support to IDPs and HC affected by the conflict.  The project is implementing in Yemen, Hajja governorate .

title: Resilience and Peace building
description: This project is part of Oxfam's humanitarian response strategy to meet the needs arising out of this current conflict.

title: Humanitarian assistance to the conflict affected population in Amran, Yemen
description: Improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene promotion materials, increasing Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) capabilities in an integrated manner, mainly in camps as well as in host communities. Provide safe water through water trucking to meet immediate needs of the communities in camps in times of water shortage and increased influx of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). Provide unconditional cash transfers in order to improve food security.

title: Provision of humanitarian assistance to the conflict affected population in Haja
description: This project is financed by European Commission Humanitarian Office (ECHO). It is planned for 12 months to provide humanitarian assistance to the most effected people of Abs district in Hajjah governorate. This intervention will focus on meeting immediate life saving needs of the most vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and conflict affected host communities in the target district. Through this project, targeted population will be assisted with food security, water sanitation and hygiene support in an integrated approach considering gender and protection mainstreaming.  Oxfam will be the direct implementer of two components; food security and water supply while public health promotion activities will be implemented by local partner ‘Yemen Development Network'.

title: Scaling Up Cholera Preparedness, Prevention & Response in Amran and Sa'ada
description: The proposed activities are aligned with the Integrated Cholera/Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD) outbreak Response Plan developed by the Health and WASH cluster and will also contribute to the strategic objectives of the Reserve Allocation Strategy paper and Humanitarian Response Plan 2017 (Revised in January 2017) through the prioritization of interventions that will contribute to reducing the spread of cholera in Amran and Taiz governorates by ensuring access to safe water and in sufficient quantity; access to improved sanitation facilities; and public health campaigns aimed at promoting and facilitating hygienic practices. Furthermore, the project will contribute to Oxfam's' ongoing response in Yemen, which aims to provide life -saving humanitarian assistance and alleviation of suffering of the conflict -affected people in Amran and Sa'ada through an integrated programme of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene services (WASH) and Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods (EFSVL), with gender, protection and advocacy as cross -cutting themes.

title: Humanitarian Response in Hajja and Hodeidah Governorates
description: The project scope is focused on improving access to food and water provision services in a sustainable manner. The targeted communities will be provided with unconditional cash transfer to meet the immediate food needs,  hygiene promotion support to reduce the health risks and, hence, improve the hygiene practice with enhancement of people knowledge on gender and protection issues. The proposed intervention under this project will be implemented by Oxfam in Hajjah and Hodeida governorates.

title: Emergency & Humanitarian Response In Taiz
description: The situation in Taiz governorate remains critical due to the ongoing ground fighting and the emerging epidemic cholera outbreak in addition to the country collapsed economy. The  cholera and acute watery diarrhoea emerged in the community, which is reflected in the general health office daily monitoring report of cholera/Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD) outbreak which shows that 67% of the cases are children less than 15 years and 56% of cases are females from the total of 438 suspected cases inside Taiz city. The number of cases is increasing day by day due to the deteriorating humanitarian situation and ground fighting, and there is growing fear of a catastrophic humanitarian situation due to the current conflicts and limitation of humanitarian aid assistance and market supplies.  Oxfam will work through local partners to reach the affected locations in addition to direct implementation to the Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities. Only the Local Water and Sanitation Corporation (LWSC), Generation without Qat (GWQ) and The General Authority for Rural Water Supply (GARWSP) have been able to access the Taiz city to provide basic humanitarian support. Oxfam from a humanitarian standpoint will not remain indifferent  to areas that are difficult to access and will actively collaborate with LWSC, GWQ and GARWSP to provide emergency WASH assistance to the affected people through water trucking and disinfection of water sources, in order to reduce morbidity and mortality cases resulting from acute watery diarrhoea and other diarrhoea epidemics among members of the community through timely preparedness for epidemics in addition to controlling the extent and spread of AWD/Cholera outbreaks.

title: Saving lives of conflict affected communities through improved food security
description: This is a 3 years program financed by Department For International Development DFID. It is aimed at addressing the needs in Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods (EFSVL) for the people affected by the conflict and protracted economic crisis through established modalities; Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) and Cash for Work. The intervention will be integrated and synergized with existing WaSH programmes funded by different donors to ensure that immediate needs of vulnerable people are met and the level of resilience is increased by improving household (HH) coping mechanisms against stresses and shocks. There are mainly two modalities proposed in this project: • UCT will be targeted towards the most food insecure households with a combination of community participation and oversight following criteria targeting households headed by women, children, the elderly and persons with disabilities, along with households without adults able to work.  • Cash for Work (CfW) will target HH not receiving UCT and give able -bodied members who are able to work for 15 days the equivalent amount as a UCT.

title: Integrated WASH and Food Security Response in Hajjah
description: In this project the below activities will be implemented in an integrated approach: 1 -Sustainable access to safe water the rehabilitation of water supply schemes in urban areas and rural areas, supply and installation of solar systems to reduce the operation and maintenance cost with capacity building of water management committees.  Community Mobilization and engagement to understand the public health current situation, context, prioritize needs, approach, and plan and implement public health promotion. Solid waste management in urban cities in collaboration with cleaning fund to cover the existed gaps and set clear exit strategy in addition to the support of  solid waste management and cleaning campaigns through community groups led by Community Health Volunteer (CHV) in the rural areas.  2 - Adequate sanitation is ensured through supply and installation of appropriate emergency latrines in areas that have been identified as at risk in Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) settlements; latrine kit distribution to ensure cleanliness of latrines; supported by environmental cleaning campaigns and solid and liquid waste management. 3 -Food security: the intervention will address the needs in Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods (EFSVL) for those most affected by the conflict, through a programme of Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) using the established modalities and service providers, Cash For Work (CfW), and Household Livelihood Grants (HHLG) which will target the most vulnerable Households (HHs) to protect and restore the livelihoods and, thus encourage small scale income generating activities. 4 -Gender and protection mainstreaming across the program.

title: HUmanitarian Capacity Development and Response Project
description: Making programme management support available to all programmes and field offices

title: Integrated Food security and WaSH assistance in Lahj, Yemen
description: The project will provide both unconditional cash transfer and cash for work to the targeted vulnerable House Holds (HHs) in  Lahj. The project will also be about the provision of safe drinking water through rehabilitation of water supply systems, provision of sanitation through the construction of wash facilities in schools, environmental sanitation through solid waste management and provision of hygiene kits and hygiene promotion including cholera awareness and key messages.

title: Humanitarian Response In Saada
description: The protracted crisis in Yemen was exacerbated by the latest interference of external factors, i.e. Saudi -led coalition airstrikes and the siege stopping imports of food, fuel and medical supplies, and has made the situation on the ground much worse. So, the  main objectives of this intervention  is to contribute to diminishing risks related to shortage of water, sanitation ,hygiene and livelihood  for the affected communities in Sa'ada province, through a set of activities which include emergency water trucking, rehabilitation/construction of water and sanitation facilities and dissemination of hygiene messages  .

title: Women's Economic Leadership in the Affected Life of the People Yemen-Lahj
description: Oxfam will support the development of women's transformative leadership by organizing women's leaders' groups by providing them with the necessary knowledge on women's rights and leadership skills. We will facilitate the development of the necessary technical and material resources through the creation of spaces (Local resource and information centers) by strengthening their links with the market and service providers. Women leaders in the community will be trained on transformative leadership so that they can pass it on to other women in the community and to project beneficiaries. 300 women will receive 5 days of training on income generation and entrepreneurial skills followed by an allocation of funding. Trained women will also receive technical support for the development and implementation of their income generating activity plans. Oxfam will work with a local Riwaa Youth Development Foundation (RYDF) partner to implement this project with the technical assistance of the Oxfam team. General Objective:  Conflict -affected women and girls can cope with the impacts of economic conflicts and crises and have better control over resources, assets and economic opportunities. Specific objectives: 1 - Women leaders have improved their leadership and advocacy skills and are able to effectively support other women in promoting their socio -economic rights. 2 - Household income and livelihoods of women beneficiaries increased through viable income -generating activities and skills developed through project activities.

title: Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Response In Saada
description: The protracted crisis in Yemen was exacerbated by the latest interference of external factors, i.e. Saudi -led coalition airstrikes and the siege stopping imports of food, fuel and medical supplies, and has made the situation on the ground much worse. So, the  main objectives of this intervention  is to contribute to diminishing risks related to shortage of water, sanitation ,hygiene and livelihood  for the affected communities in Sa'ada province, through a set of activities which include emergency water trucking, rehabilitation/construction of water and sanitation facilities and dissemination of hygiene messages  .

title: Restoring functionality and improving water governance of Aden
description: The project will provide access to the basic water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services, this will be done through construction of new and/or rehabilitation of existing water supply facilities by installing water distribution networks, fittings boreholes and wells with pumps and generators, establishment and capacity building of water management committees, communities training on best hygiene practices, in addition to support communities to construct sanitation facilities.

title: Humanitarian and Resilience Response in Al Dhale, YEMEN
description: The project will provide access to the basic water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services, this will be done through construction of new and/or rehabilitation of existing water supply facilities by installing water distribution networks, fittings boreholes and wells with pumps and generators

title: Life Saving Humanitarian Support in Lahj, Yemen
description: The project will focus on providing immediate life saving assistance to 8,400 (1,200HH) returnees, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities through monthly unconditional cash assistance, so that the benefiting Households (HHs) are enabled to access food and unmet needs.

title: Humanitarian Response in Hajjah and Hudaida
description: The project is designed to respond to the humanitarian needs resulted from emergencies as outbreaks, new displacement and natural disaster. The intervention will include Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) package prioritising the most vulnerable population affected by conflict or natural disasters.

title: Innovation Fund in Hajjah and Hodieda
description: The project is aimed to establish innovative approaches based on feasibility of the context. In this project, a Community Gardening / Vegetable growth will be piloted in two selected villages in Abs district to implement the proposed action which is deemed as new approach in the area of intervention. Through community driven approach, project will enhance the community collaborative methods and contribute to the restoration of livelihoods of affected population both host -community and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) settled in the targeted location.  Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihood and gender are incorporated in this approach through provision of inputs, capacity building and access to resources.

title: Restoring functionality and improving water governance and sanitation, Aden
description: The project will provide access to the basic water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services, this will be done through construction of new and/or rehabilitation of existing water supply facilities by installing water distribution networks, fitting boreholes and wells with pumps and generators, establishment and capacity building of water management committees, communities training on best hygiene practices, in addition to support communities to construct sanitation facilities.

title: Humanitarian Assistance to Conflict Affected Communities in Lahj, Yemen
description: Implement Water supply schemes, train water management committees, distribute hygiene kits, train Community Health Volunteers (CHVs), conduct community health campaigns, conduct environmental cleaning campaigns and conduct cash transfers.

title: Integrated Scaling up WASH food security and protection assistance in Taiz
description: Objective: Increasing access to safe and clean water through rehabilitation and maintenance of the water networks in targeted areas of Taiz governorate.   Output One: Sustainable water systems are maintained and/or restored to improve access and availability of water and sanitation to vulnerable host and Internally Displaced Person (IDP) households Output Two: Targeted IDPs and host communities have access to basic hygiene and sanitation and show an improvement in hygiene practices  Oxfam, in coordination with the local authorities and General Authority for Rural Water Supply (GARWSP), will carry several interventions to facilitate access to and the involvement of the selected water projects (through an initial rapid assessment) of the villages which will benefit from the water network upgrading. In this regard, Oxfam will organise meetings with authorities and community members to present the project and all the different preparatory phases which will occur to accomplish the intervention. Water Facilities Construction/Rehabilitation Construction and related supervision by Oxfam's technical team will be carried on during the entire project implementation. To ensure maintenance and sustainability of the intervention, Oxfam will organise meetings with technical bodies and communities as well as training (for the selected communities) on operation and maintenance.

title: Saving lives & alleviating human suffering of conflict affected IDPs in Hajjah
description: To saving Lives and alleviating human suffering of conflict affect and vulnerable communities through provision of safe and gender sensitive, integrated WASH service in Hajjah Governorate

title: Emergency Response In Amran
description: The project contributes to improved access to education and health for 30,481 conflict -affected children and youth, and 948 teachers in Amran, Yemen through Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) and protection activities in 70 schools. So this will be through supporting safe water and inclusive sanitary facilities for schools, and to enhance the learning facilities, environment, and health for girls and boys along with education personnel. All activities will take into consideration the specific needs of girls and people living with disabilities. Protection activities will aim to reduce the risk of Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV), negative coping mechanisms, and the impact of the conflict on the well -being of school -children, as well as promoting menstrual hygiene among girls. The project will provide psychosocial support and promote gender equality, particularly the needs and rights of girls. Compensation will be given to teachers not receiving salaries in line with authority requirements and standards, to address teacher absenteeism and livelihoods. Finally, the project will build and strengthen local actors and structures to enhance the sustainability of the actions and collective outcomes.

title: WASH and EFSVL Response for IDPs & vulnerable groups in Amran Governorate, Yemen
description: This project aims to provide sufficient, clean, physically accessible and acceptable quality water for vulnerable households in Internally Displaced Person (IDP) camps and host communities in four districts of the province of Amran (Khamer, Bani Suraim, Houth and Algaflah), which lack sufficient water to meet their basic needs. The project will support 88,186 people. All beneficiaries will have improved access to safe drinking water. 26,300 people receive improved access to sanitary facilities. In addition, 63,600 people will be able to improve their hygiene practices and 33,215 people gain knowledge about gender -based violence.

title: Emergency WASH assistance to famine risk population in Lahj under Parameter 1.
description: 8,400 people in famine risk Musaymir District   - Lahj Governorate  have access to improved water, sanitation & hygiene by 2020. Rehabilitation of 3 water supply system (WSS) in Al Musaymir, Lahj including tech investigation. Fuel support to 3 WSS in Al Musaymir, Lahj for 3 months. Supply and support 3 WSS with spare parts and maintenance consumables in Al Musaymir. Up to 200 targeted Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) House Holds (HH) will be provided with family latrine support for construction and or adapting for disability or especially able people as appropriate in Al Musaymir district of Lahj.  HH will also get latrine cleaning kits to maintain will distribute directly with support from Community Health Volunteers (CHVs).  Provide support for solid waste collection & disposal. Solid waste tricycle kits, fuel and operators support for 6 months in Musaymir. This activity targets 7,500 individuals to benefit from Solid waste management support through supply of cleaning tools, environmental campaigns and community mobilisation.

title: Food Assistance for Assets, Resilient Markets & Livelihoods - WFP, Amran
description: This project is to protect and improve food consumption levels of targeted households and strengthen their resilience by Improving access to food for 6,000 households in four districts (Khamer, Bani Suraim in Amran and Sahar and Saad'a districts in Saad'a) through the provision of cash transfers during the period of assistance while 1,250 households will be selected from the Food For Assets (FFA) beneficiaries, and other vulnerable groups in targeted communities to receive livelihoods assistance to start, restart or strengthen agricultural and non -agricultural livelihoods.

title: FFA & Livelihood intervention for vulnerable people in Sa'ada
description: Oxfam will implement the proposed project in Sahar and Sa'adah districts of Saa'dah Governorate. The districts are affected by conflict, massive displacement, destroyed livelihoods, disease, limited access to social services and poverty.  The main objective of the project is to protect and improve food consumption levels of targeted households and strengthen their resilience. Specific objectives include: • Improved access to food for 1200 households through the provision of cash transfers during the period of assistance  • Increased resilience, livelihood opportunities and access to basic services of target communities through the construction and rehabilitation of community assets and social infrastructure;  • Restored livelihoods and income generating activities for the most vulnerable, particularly for women and youth, through trainings, home -based business, small -business support and business management training, etc.     A total of 1200 households will participate in Food for Assets (FFA) activities to fill food consumption gaps and create and rehabilitate community assets and social infrastructure.

title: Emergency WASH assistance to most vulnerable IDPs and host community in Ad Dhali
description: The project aims to contribute to reducing morbidity & mortality by providing the most vulnerable populations with WaSH assistance. Oxfam will rehabilitate 2 water systems that serve both IDPs and host communities in the villages of Al Wa'ara and Al Jalila for the Ad Dhali sub -district and will support the Local Water and Sanitation Corporation (LWSC) in Ad Dhali with 2 months of fuel to power the water pumping systems, a supply for spare parts, and water disinfecting agents and quality testing equipment. This will come alongside a series of capacity building training for the water management committees, including sessions on technical repairs and maintenance, financial management, and administrative management of water supply systems, in addition to sessions on the water chlorination at distribution tank, and the use of the pool testers for quality monitoring.

title: Yemen Joint Response
description: Food security and Livelihoods Component: • Unconditional and unrestricted one -off multipurpose cash grant (MPCG) will be delivered as part of the Rapid Response Mechanism in the targeted districts in Taiz to 720 HHs (5040 individuals). This will target the newly displaced conflict -affected populations (IDPs in collective centres/camps and host communities). Each household will receive one -off MPCG based on MEB transfer value recommended by the Cash and Market Working Group (CMWG) to meet the immediate household basic needs. A multisectoral approach will be adopted to meet the lifesaving needs of IDPs. • Conditional and unrestricted multipurpose cash will be delivered in targeted district Lahj distributed twice to 425 households (2,975 individuals).  • Improved cooking stoves/fuel efficient stoves (FES) to 500 HHs in Lahj. • Provision of Solar lanterns to 500 HHs in targeted districts in Taiz.  WASH Component: • Rehabilitation of one water system benefitting 4,900 individuals in Al Ma'afer district of Taiz governorate.   • Provision of maintenance generators & water pump including supply of standard tool box.

title: Emergency livelihoods assistance for crisis affected vulnerable population Taiz
description: The proposed project aims at providing critically needed emergency livelihoods to support communities affected by the conflict and crisis in the targeted districts of Taiz. Only 14590 individuals (6.5%) out of the 2019 FSAC YHRP target of 221760 individuals have so far received livelihoods in the three districts. Oxfam has a comparative advantage to respond to the most vulnerable in the target districts because it has been operational in the districts providing the most needed humanitarian assistance in the form of food security, livelihoods, protection and WASH services. Oxfam will therefore easily integrate the project with its on -going WASH, and gender and protection activities to address multiple needs of target beneficiaries and increase the impact of the project. The target beneficiaries for food for asset activities are landless men and women headed households depend on agriculture -related services i.e. laborer's workforce. There will be 3 rounds or months of FFA activities during the lean season or period of approaching planting season as land preparation mainly focuses on restoration of the damaged farm due to flooding, eroded soil, and damage irrigation canal and water reservoir. While the small landholding/landowners will be targeted for cash grants and agriculture inputs. During the lean season, the men and women headed farmers will be supported by 3 months' cash grants as conditional cash transfer to prepare their farmland as criteria to qualify for beneficiaries to receive agriculture inputs and skills training.

title: Yemen COVID-19 Preparedness and Response
description: Saving lives and alleviating human suffering of conflict and COVID -19 affected and vulnerable communities through provision of adequate, safe and gender sensitive WASH services to the health facilities, IDPs and vulnerable communities in the 8 governorates of Hajjah, Ibb, Taiz, Sa'ada, Aden, Adhale, Lahj and Amran

title: Integrated WASH and Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods response to conflic
description: To contribute to alleviation of human suffering through increased access to food and essential WASH services for vulnerable women, girls, boys and men affected by the ongoing Yemen conflict in Taiz and Ibb Governates through a  protection and gender sensitive humanitarian response.  Outcome: Increased access to clean water, sanitation  facilities, basic hygiene and food for 105,000 IDPs, and host communities  in Taiz (Dimnat Khadir, Mawiah, Sharab Alrona and AL -Taiziah  ) and Ibb ( Ibb and Al Sabrah  ) Governorates

title: Yemen: Supporting the Judiciary and Building Confidence in the Justice Sector
description: To strengthen the capacity of the Judiciary to improve the functioning and performance of the                justice sector, and enhance access to justice.

title: Yemen: Strengthening Capacity to Investigate Human Rights Violations
description: 1) To enhance quality for monitoring, documenting, investigating and reporting by                the National Commission of human rights violations and violations under international humanitarian law.                2) To enhance preparedness of the National Commission for its potential future role and mandate.
sector_group: I.5.a. Government and civil society, general

title: Protecting most Vulnerable Hosting communities from public health risks of COVID
description: Strengthen (WASH) infection prevention and control measures in health facilities;   Targeted population have equitable access to basic WASH services in community.  Activities contributing to outcomes include:  - WASH facilities in health centers rehabilitated  - Hygiene cleaning and disinfection kits distributed to health centers  - Personal Protection Equipment distributed to support health workers  - Handwashing station established to provide access for handwashing and hygiene practices  - Water points and taps stands quick fixs for safe access to water  - Training to existing Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) on COVID -19 prevention, including the sheiling approach, hygiene promotion and referral pathway  - Hygiene kits distributed to the most vulnerable households using shielding approach  - Awareness raising on COVID -19 prevention, shielding approach and referral pathway  - Latrine construction to support the most vulnerable households and in large IDP resettlement  - IEC materials developed and distributed through social media

title: DEC 2020 Coronavirus Appeal Phase 1- Hajjah Governorate
description: The project scope is focused on protect IDPs and most vulnerable host communities from public health risks of COVID -19 pandemic, through improved access to and knowledge of water, sanitation and positive hygiene behaviours. It will complement existing WASH activities with a strengthened focus on COVID -19 prevention and response to ensure safe access to safe water and promotion of sanitation and hygiene. The proposed intervention under this project will be implemented by Oxfam in Hajjah. Oxfam Yemen COVID -19 response plan is to contribute to the control of the pandemic and to mitigate against its impact; and reducing risk of transmission a within communities, especially for the most vulnerable and displaced people.

title: Yemen LHL Strengthening
description: The overall goals of the projects are:   • To support Local Humanitarian Leadership (LHL) in Yemen through strengthening the capacities and capabilities of local humanitarian actors to deliver better quality responses   • To highlight the role of Yemeni civil society organisations (particularly those led by women) in local -level peace initiatives and promote their priority advocacy asks to ensure that any peace initiatives meaningfully include the views of civil society, including women and youth

title: COVID-19 Response in Hajjah
description: - Wells rehabilitation in Hajjah. Oxfam will target 7 open dug wells in Mabian district. This intervention will benefit from it 717 HHs. Quick assessment confirmed that people in this area collect water from the 7 dug wells for drinking water which considered as contaminated water. In addition, collecting water is a tough job for women and girls as they have to walk more than 2 km to the water source. The intervention need will include excavation and filling around of well  Paving stone; Supply and build solid concrete block to increase the wall of dug well installed  steel/fibber cover; construction of basin for animals drinking; cleaning and chlorination from contamination. Rehabilitate of these sources will reduce the risk of infection and the spread of the COVID -19 as well as other water borne diseases related to water pollution, acute watery diarrhea and cholera.

title: Preparedness and response to the impact of COVID-19 in Yemen
description: To contribute to decreasing the direct and indirect impact of COVID -19's spread amongst the most vulnerable population groups in Yemen and build community resilience through strengthening livelihoods

title: Oxfam Apeal Emergency Food Security Response for Ibb office
description: To contribute to alleviation of human suffering through increased access to food for vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) women, girls, boys and men affected by the ongoing Yemen conflict in Taiz and Ibb Governorates through a  protection and gender sensitive humanitarian response.  Outcome: Increased access to clean water, sanitation  facilities, basic hygiene and food for 105,000 IDPs, and host communities  in Taiz (Dimnat Khadir, Mawiah, Sharab Alrona and AL -Taiziah  ) and Ibb ( Ibb and Al Sabrah  ) Governorate

title: Giro 555 COVID Response - Yemen
description: Top line activities : Activity 1.1: Train health staff on vaccinations / and volunteers engaged in the support to vaccination activities. Activity 1.2: Supply material like Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for medics administering the vaccine. Activity 1.3: Supply vaccination's table including chair with good quality. Activity 2: Information campaigns / awareness raising around vaccinating and advocacy for equitable access as well as building trust on the vaccine including the following activities: 2.1: Capacity building training to community health volunteers to awareness raising around vaccination . 2.2: Monthly incentives for community health volunteers. 2.3: Information campaigns through media Television (TV) or radio. Activity 3:Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities related to vaccination (Solid waste management) including the below activities: 3.1: Provision of solid waste management tools and cleaning materials to the vaccination centres.  3.2: Monthly incentives to waste collection workers . 3.3: Rehabilitation of vaccination centres/construction of medical incinerators.

title: Program Quality enhancement through targeted capacity building to Oxfam Yemen
description: Programme Quality (PQ) quality enhancement initiatives which focuses on building capacity of both Monitoring and Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) and Partners around essential themes and topics which are crucial for delivering high quality program. The proposed initiative will therefore focus at building capacity of the country MEAL teams to ensure high quality data management, visualization and reporting, while taking into consideration foundational/crosscutting themes such as Gender, protection and feminist approaches which are highly sensitive and difficult to implement in the context of Yemen. Learning from these initiatives will be documented to add to enhance programming and contribute to the body of knowledge in the area of program quality Assurance.

title: Empowering communities to respond to conflict-induced protection risks.
description: Oxfam will support existing community structures, or establish a community -based social committee, composed of members from Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and host communities, where these committees should represent most vulnerable people & groups such as (minority groups, internally displaced persons, women, marginalized groups and people with disabilities). This will be achieved through three interconnected outcomes that feed into each other.  Outcome 1 envisages providing protection services through the community -based protection centres and referrals to other service providers by linkages development, and supporting persons with protection risks with accessing legal/civil documentation. title: Cholera Outbreak Responce in the north of Yemen 24/2025.
description: The United Nations (UN) led Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in Yemen declared a cholera outbreak in the north of Yemen on March 19, 2024. Similarly, the Deputy of Ministry for Primary Health Care announced the outbreak of Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD) in the north during the monthly UN Health Cluster meeting. The transmission of cholera/AWD rate is very high, with the reported AWD cases doubling just in one week (from week 11 to week 12). As of the end of March, 2024, there are 7,324 reported AWD cases affecting all 15 governorates in Yemen. When announcing the cholera/AWD outbreak, the Health Cluster announced Sa'dah, Ibb, Hajjah, and Tai'z as priority areas, with Sa'dah  - accounting for 33% of total cases  - being the epicenter of the outbreak. The humanitarian situation in Sa'dah, Ibb, and Hajjah is urgent as communities there face the protracted effects related to conflict, displacement, extreme poverty, climate -related disasters, economic insecurity, and protection risks. The multitude of challenges they face mean they have inadequate access to safe Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services and basic medical services, making them more vulnerable to the cholera/AWD outbreak.  Further, Iftar gathering, incoming rainy season, and potential floods will pose high risk of endemicity and re -emergence. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates there will be more than 50,000 AWD cases in the next six months if the outbreak is not contained.

title: Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD)
description: The Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD) project, funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is a global initiative aimed at advancing anticipatory action (AA) for conflict-induced displacement through a dual workstream approach. First, AHEAD implements pilot interventions in seven countries—Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Yemen, and Myanmar—while applying a robust MEAL approach to generate evidence on the feasibility and value-add of AA compared to traditional emergency response. Second, AHEAD leverages this evidence for policy influence and advocacy, using humanitarian coordination platforms, the cluster system, and bilateral engagements with government and non-government stakeholders to promote the institutionalization of AA within displacement response frameworks. A key component of this second workstream is the development of inclusive, multipartner national-level anticipatory action frameworks relevant to conflict-induced displacement, ensuring that anticipatory approaches are embedded in national disaster risk management and humanitarian systems. The project also prioritizes capacity-building and knowledge transfer, aiming to hand over its predictive modeling algorithms and datasets to external partners—including government agencies and humanitarian actors—while providing training on their application for forecast-based decision-making in conflict settings. Running from 2024 to December 2027, AHEAD is currently in its early setup phase for pilot implementation, focusing on refining its predictive models, establishing partnerships, and laying the groundwork for its anticipatory action interventions. Through this integrated approach, AHEAD seeks to demonstrate the feasability and impact of conflict-relevant anticipatory action, advocate for its adoption at scale, and equip key actors with the tools to sustain its implementation beyond the project lifecycle.

title: Yemen Complex Emergency 2014
description:
After more than four years, the conflict in Yemen that has brought about a man-made humanitarian disaster affecting 22.5 million people.
 
As a result of the protracted violence, thousands of civilians have been killed or injured, and millions displaced. Widespread damage to public infrastructure and severe shortage of supplies, owing to restrictions on the movement of goods into and within the country, make it nearly impossible for the majority of Yemenis to obtain food, water, medical care and other essentials.
 
Wounded and sick people are unable to obtain timely and good-quality health services, because of the dangers associated with seeking such services. Most hospitals are seriously handicapped by the lack of medicines, equipment and trained staff. National capacities for tackling public-health emergencies, such as cholera outbreaks, are very limited.
 
Millions of people have been displaced since the conflicts began; many are still unable to return home. A large part of the population is heavily dependent on humanitarian aid and faces food insecurity. They struggle to obtain or produce food, and to resume or sustain their livelihoods, because of the fighting and movement restrictions. The unavailability of potable water and of adequate sanitation facilities puts many of them at risk of disease or illness.
 
Attacks against humanitarian personnel are not uncommon. Since the escalation of the conflict in March 2015, seven Yemen Red Crescent Society volunteers and three ICRC personnel have been killed while carrying out their duties. The few international organizations present in the country struggle to respond to the outstanding needs of victims.

title: GRC-YRCS Primary Health Centres (Hajjah,Al Dhalee)
description:
Since the escalation of violence in March 2015, the healthcare sector in Yemen has been unable to respond to the rising needs.
This intervention is a continuation of BRC's support to German Red Cross's in YRCS's health facilities in Yemen. It covers YRCS Health Centre and Emergency Obstetrics clinic in Hajjah, which has been supported by BRC since April 2016; and the extended support to the Al Dhalee Health Centre, which GRC has been supporting since 2019.
The project's overall objective is that conflict-affected people have access to emergency medical care and primary health care free of charge at YRCS health facilities. This will be achieved through the provision of drugs/medical supplies and supporting with operating and staff costs.
 
Since April 2016, the British Red Cross (BRC) has been successful in funding the EmOC unit; securing £30,000 from the Jersey Overseas Aid Committee (JOAC) in 2016 and £140,000 from the Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC) (Feb- Dec 2018). Both contributions have supplemented BRC’s own appeal funds. 
 In 2019 BRC has committed to continuing its support to EmOC with £480,000 for a further 24 months until Feb 2021.This is a mixture of restricted funds secured from the Isle of Man government (£81,989), and Volant (£100,000), supplemented bv BRC’s own Emergency Appeal funds.
In 2021, BRC entered a new agreement with GRC to support an additional health centre in Al Dhalee.
