reporting: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
title: Emergency life-saving water supply through water trucking for the vulnerable households living in informal settlements in Al-Hali district of Hodeidah governorate
description:
Through this action Action Contre La Faim aims at continuing to provide access to safe water to inhabitants of informal settlements in Al Hali district of Al Hudaydah though water trucking. These illegal settlements located on a landfill, face very poor sanitary conditions and continue to be first among top five districts with the highest reported cases of cholera (IPC Hotspot Analysis, July, 2019).

While continuing to support water trucking for a period of 12 months, ACF will initiate discussions with local communities, community organizations, local authorities and UN (WASH, Shelter and Protection Clusters) with an objective of bringing them to a consensus on finding a durable solution that ensures basic services and dignified conditions for around 27, 500 people in Al Hali. 

By the end of the project it is expected that solutions will have been identified and implemented to provide durable access to minimum services (including improved water access) for the targeted population

reporting: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
title: Emergency WASH assistance to most vulnerable IDPs and host community in Ad Dhali District of Ad Dhali Governorate Yemen.
description: Oxfam proposes to respond to the needs of 35,000 people (10,115 women, 10,290 men, 7175 girls, 7420 boys) in the Ad Dhali district of the Ad Dhali Governorate, of whom 14,000 persons are IDPs and 21,000 persons are from the hosting community. The project aims to contribute to reducing morbidity amp mortality by providing the most vulnerable populations with WaSH assistance. Oxfam will rehabilitate 2 water systems that serve both IDPs and host communities in the villages of Al Wa’ara and Al Jalila for the Ad Dhali sub-district and will support the Local Water and Sanitation Corporation (LWSC) in Ad Dhali with 2 months of fuel to power the water pumping systems, a supply for spare parts, and water disinfecting agents and quality testing equipment. This will come alongside a series of capacity building training for the water management committees, including sessions on technical repairs and maintenance, financial management, and administrative management of water supply systems, in addition to sessions on the water chlorination at distribution tank, and the use of the pool testers for quality monitoring. Latrines will be constructed to respond to the lack of access to safe sanitation facilities of IDP communities in particular. Latrine leaning kits and hygiene sessions will be provided to households to ensure that newly constructed latrines remain clean and functional, encourage latrine use and ultimately reducing open defecation. To improve the environmental hygienic condition at the Ad Dhali sub-district level, Oxfam will support the Cleaning and Improvement Fund with 2 Tricycles for waste collection and disposal, with 3 months of operational costs in terms of fuel and workforce incentives for a duration of 3 months. Lastly, Oxfam will engage communities and raise their awareness on hygiene risks and preventive measures, through establishing and training Community Hygiene Volunteers (CHVs). These volunteers will be provided with a series of training and will be equipped with communication tools that will increase their knowledge and enable them to reach and communicate with vulnerable groups in both IDP and Host communities, such as women, children, and households with suspected cases of cholera/AWD. To reach the general public and raise awareness on public health and hygiene-related issues, global events will be celebrated. The CHVs will also engage communities and with the participation of community members will lead to environmental cleaning campaigns, for the collection of scattered solid waste and debris to improve the overall cleanliness and hygienic condition.\nOxfam has been working Yemen since 1983 and in the governorate of Ad Dhali since 2016. The Ad Dhali district is accessible for Oxfam staff and is sufficiently distanced from the ongoing conflict in the surrounding areas, allowing for uninterrupted operations. The proposed projects will be implemented out of the Oxfam field offices in Ad Dhali. Oxfam has worked in Ad Dhali since 2016 with effective working relationships with the Governors’ offices, LWSC, GARWSP, the Cleaning and Improvement Funds, and local communities.

reporting: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
title: Emergency WASH support to newly displaced, existing IDPs and host communities who are at high-risk of water-borne disease and in pre-famine areas in Ad Dihar and Al Mashannah Districts, Ibb Governorate, Yemen
description: International Medical Corps UK (IMC) proposes to provide emergency lifesaving WASH interventions to vulnerable comunities in Ad Dihar and Al Mashannah districts in Ibb Governorate through the support of the Yemen Humanitarian Pooled Fund. The Yemen WASH Cluster considers Ad Dihar and Al Mashannah districts among the 169 districts at risk of AWD/cholera outbreak and are classified as IPC 4 and 5. The two districts were selected in coordination with the local authorities and WASH cluster at the subnational level to ensure that newly displaced and host communities at high risk of AWD/Cholera and in pre-famine areas have access to safe water and sanitation services. This intervention aims to reach 57,600 individuals with WASH services, including 20,000 IDPs (51,000‬ in Ad Dihar and 6,600 in Al Mashannah Districts).\n\nThe proposed response will provide newly displaced households and host communities with water vouchers to exchange for safe drinking (chlorinated) water from water vendors. The intervention will incorporate a holistic approach by offering rehabilitation of the water supply and sewage systems as well as desludging of overflowing household and institutional sanitation infrastructures (latrines and septic tanks) in these two communities. Water Management Committees (WMCs) will be created  and provided with capacity building support and the tools required to ensure the continued operations and maintenance of newly rehabilitated water systems. International Medical Corps will conduct regular water quality monitoring focusing on the Free Residual Chlorine (FRC) and fecal coliform bacteria levels. Community mobilization on hygiene promotion and mass information sharing will be undertaken by locally recruited and trained community volunteers in the local language using pictorial messaging to promote positive behavioral changes. In addition, WASH NFIs will be provided with specific focus on hygiene kit materials particularly dignity kits for women and girls under reproductive age using the voucher modality. International Medical Corps will mainstream protection principles in the proposed activities through ensuring gender inclusive WASH committees with a ratio of 60:40 of men to women representation. The committees will be trained on the  operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructures to mitigate conflict around WASH facilities. Prior to the distribution of WASH NFIs kits, women and girls will be consulted with regards to kit contents in coordination with the WASH cluster. As part of the protection mainstreaming and building capacity of International Medical Corps staff on protection issues, WASH committees and Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) will be trained on Protection Principles. This will ensure that  project activities to be implemented will promote meaningful access, safety and dignity to targeted beneficiaries. The proposed project will be funded 100% by OCHA. IMC has not secured other funding  to implement the proposed activities.

description:
RDP has designed a WASH Emergency Response Project for IDPs and most affected host population in Masrooh Sub-district in Khayran Al Muharraq of Hajjah governorate and Bani Saif As Safil and Bani Mubariz Sub-districts in Al Qafr district of Ibb governorate. The project will target 25,266 vulnerable people (4951 Men, 5153 Women, 7426 Boys and 7736 Girls) to increase and improve access to water, improve sanitation standards, and develop people’s knowledge of good hygiene.

The project interventions is in line with allocation strategy and priorities, especially, the first line of effort by Covering Priority Gaps in First and Second Line Responses for critical WASH interventions as it will help to cover gaps in the WASH response population in Masrooh Sub-district in Khayran Al Muharraq of Hajjah governorate and Bani Saif As Safil and Bani Mubariz Sub-districts in Al Qafr district of Ibb governorate which are critically affected and from the 45 districts with pockets of IPC 5 and insecure and hard to reach areas and has received many IDPs, the proposed activities focus on the highest priority life-saving humanitarian response in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) as well as looking affordable sustainable solution in WASH at the targeted district using area-based approach. Also, the proposed interventions are directly aligned with both WASH cluster objectives:
SO1 - Provide emergency water, sanitation and hygiene services to highly vulnerable people.
SO2 - Restore and maintain sustainable water and sanitation systems, particularly in high risk areas. 
The project interventions will be implemented in 9 months period including the following main activities: 
-	Conduct technical feasibility studies for 3 water schemes in the targeted Sub-districts.
-	Conduct water quality tests of 3 water sources in the targeted Sub-districts.
-	Rehabilitate 3 water schemes in the targeted Sub-districts based on the results of the feasibility studies.
-	Select and train 30 water management committee members (WMC) (18 men and 12 women) from the community committees in the fields of management, operation, and maintaining water schemes.
-	Provide communal water tanks and install communal water tanks/taps including the connection to water scheme with piping system to the nearby locations of affected people in the targeted areas.
-	Select and train 40 community volunteers (26 Men and 14 Women) in the targeted areas in hygiene promotion and community engagement to strengthen knowledge and facilitate the adoption of behaviors.
-	Conduct hygiene promotion sessions over different themes by the trained community volunteers.
-	Distribute basic/consumable hygiene kits to most vulnerable HHs .
-	Construction and support of family latrines for 172 HHs (1204 beneficiaries including 236 men, 246 women, 354 boys and 368 girls) in the targeted areas.
The implementation will be coordinated with local authorities to serve as an external quality control measure. RDP will closely coordinate with UN agencies for the de-confliction to be obtained for project implementation sites. To mitigate the risk of government-imposed selection of villages, RDP will follow assessment criteria including, but not limited to water sources likelihood of sustainability, number of beneficiaries from water sources and value for money. The activities proposed based on the results of the needs assessment conducted by RDP in November 2019. RDP will implement the project in total commitment to DO NO Harm Principle through targeting the most vulnerable population based on WASH cluster selection criteria with no discrimination based on age, gender, religion, ethnicity, or disability. Additionally, WASH activities are in line with SPHERE standards, which directly reduces and contributes towards reduction the risk of water and sanitation related diseases.
The project will be implemented according to the terms and conditions of the grant agreement that results from this proposal.

reporting: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
title: Comprehensive WASH Response in Al-Meghlaf District of Al-Hodeidah Governorate
description:
The intervention is a water, sanitation, and hygiene project that is expected to improve the life conditions of about 20511 persons at Al-Maghlaf District in Al-Hodeidah Governorate. The project aims to improve the living conditions in the displacement sites and promote durable solutions with full participation of IDPs and host communities. The intervention targets six water projects in three subdistricts namely Alhabeel, Almahjam, and Kohlan in Bani Mohammed Kofiah amp Alharthah in Bani Alborrah, and Almasloobah in Almahmedah.

The WASH needs of IDPs and communities have been fully identified by a qualified team trained on the principles of water, sanitation, hygiene, and humanitarian action. In addition to closely observation, the team conducted several meetings with the water project managers and interviewed many people in focus group discussions. 

The Needs Assessment (NA) was carried out for 15 days between 3rd through 18th of November 2019.The selection criteria are displacement, severe need, and lack or suspension of nearby water sources or projects where IDPs and communities hosting them are located. The NA shows that the people of the area are in dire need for this WaSH intervention for the frequent suspension of sustainable sources of safe drinking water. All the targeted 6 water project pumps are in very bad conditions, too much consuming for fuel and are in need for expensive repairs and parts. Besides, Kuhlan and Kofiah water projects do not have concrete tanks and the water network in Kohlan is too small and severely damaged. Also, IDPs are in need for many latrines and all areas are polluted with solid waste everywhere. What is more, a considerable percentage of IDPs (40%) practice defecation in the open.

It is planned that the project starts by establishing strong coordination with all relevant stakeholders: NAMCHA and all other governmental authorities of concern at all levels: central, governorate, and district the WaSH Cluster GARWSP OCHA and key leaders of the targeted communities.

The analysis of the disaggregated NA data according to GAM has resulted in tailoring the assistance to the WaSH needs and interests of the targeted groups in a way that can help in mitigating GBV. The project activities include: construction of 2 concrete water tanks, implementation of 1 water network of about 15 km long, implementation of 1 pumping line of about 350m long, testing of pumping and water quality in 6 wells provision of 10 public water points construction of 108 latrines installation of 6 complete solar-powered pumping units on 6 wells collection and disposal of solid waste distribution of 1000 consumer hygiene kits three times  and 1000 essential hygiene kits once training of 12 community volunteers on hygiene promotion and community participation and training of 6 water-project committees of 5 members per each, and hygiene promotion. The work plan of activities shows the number of beneficiaries in each area and the implementation duration in a sequential and logical manner.

AGF has demonstrated its ability to implement water and sanitation projects by having a skilled team consisting of a project manager, 2 engineers, a water and sanitation officer, a logistics officer, a coordinator, an MampE officer, a protection officer, 2 field supervisors, and volunteers. Furthermore, building a variety of practical communications with WaSH service providers, AGF is able to obtain any required stock or service whenever needed.

Finally, it is worthily noted that AGF is well acquainted with Al Hodeidah and the needs of its districts as it has implemented several projects of different sectors including WaSH. Presently, AGF is implementing a huge WaSH project in Az-Zaidiah and Al-Munirah, 2 districts nearby Al-Meghlaf. The WaSH needs, geography, and status of people where AGF is working now are all similar to that in Al-Meghlaf District.

title: Provision of Integrated WASH and Shelter assistance to IDPs and their most vulnerable hosting communities at Jehaf , Juban, Damt and Al-Hushaa districts of Al-Dhale Gov.
description:
In line with 2019 SA2 Strategy objectives and cluster objectives, this project intends to provide comprehensive WASH and Shelter assistance to estimated 115,708 IDPs and most vulnerable affected individuals (27770 men, 30084 women,26613, boys, 31241 girls) from the most vulnerable groups with focus on IDPs and most affected communities hosting IDPs to respond to the humanitarian needs in WASH and Shelter sectors at Jehaf,Damt,Juban and Al-Husha districts of Al-Dhale Gov.

WASH and Shelter interventions will be providing a comprehensive response to 18516 IDPs and 97192 most vulnerable host communities in the 4 targeted districts covering  second line responses for newly accessible locations formed due to  the recent clashing in Aldhale with focus on under-served IDPs within the 2nd line sector response to ensure the functionality of targeted communities’ water assets as well as promoting public hygiene practices. 

The WASH interventions will be provided to conflict- affected beneficiaries to improve their access to safe drinking
water and sanitation services through:
Construction of 50 water harvesting tanks through CFW at HHs level in Jehaf and Al-Hushaa districts by providing the beneficiaries with tools and materials to build the harvesting tanks and supporting them with incentives for unskilled and skilled workers who will perform the construction activities under the supervision of field engineer. 
Rehabilitation/repair of 8 community water assets. 
Provision of operational support for 1 water asset  in Damt.
Conducting Hygiene awareness sessions.
Conducting Solid waste management and disposal in Damt ,Juban districts. 
Construction of 110 Family latrines in the 4 districts.
Distribution of CHK, Jerry can,for SAM, MAM, PLW , cholera cases.
Distributing ceramic filters for SAM, MAM, PLW and cholera cases prevalence: 62% of beneficiaries in 4 districts  don’t use any method to treat their unsafe drinking water as  they cannot afford  the cost.
Conducting CLTs interventions in Al-Husha and Jehaf districts to improve the poor sanitation practices and achieve behavior change and ODF targeting the most affected communities.

Shelter activities will be provided to IDPs at collective centers and among host communities in 3 districts (Alhusha, Damt and Juban) through the provision of EESKs/ NFIs,rental subsidies, support through in-kind and cash/vouchers modality of appropriate shelter and essential household items. 

The targeted districts are located within Aden and Ibb Hubs where YFCA has its two main sub-offices to carry out the main implementation task with backstopping support from the main office in Sana’a. Coordination with WASH, Shelter clusters, RRM, GARWASP , Local authorities has already been done to support and facilitate the planned interventions and to avoid any duplication with other partners .

The possible risks that might face YFCA while preparing and implementing the activities could include the delay in signing and approving the agreement for 3 districts under De facto, security deterioration, airstrikes, prices fluctuation, supplies shortage in the local market and outbreaks of diseases. 
These risks can  be mitigated through close coordination with all stakeholders in the field, obtaining de-confliction from airstrikes for operation sites, contracting with suppliers and staff for the whole period of the project to ensure sustainability of supply and services and avoid any prices fluctuation and finally to coordinate with health cluster and on ground actors regarding the spread of diseases such as cholera.
YFCA will closely coordinate with authorities at Aldhalee in both sides and at central level to obtain the permission and sign the agreements within the first month of the project. 
YFCA will monitor the project activities using concentrated modalities and tools at the central, hub, governorate and field level.

description:
Project Summary :	The project has been designed to meet the WASH amp Shelter clusters guidance amp objectives to respond to the objective of reducing the pressures faced by host communities and IDPs. This proposed Interventions seek to cover gaps in the WASH response in one of the most critically affected districts alleviate some of the IDP amp host communities’ stressors by providing shelter support services.

The WASH interventions will provide conflict- affected beneficiaries improved access to safe drinking water by: 
-Training the water committee to manage water supply amp sanitation services
-Repairing amp rehabilitating 2 harvest water tanks
-Rehabilitating the Sanitation Network in Haydan central butchery 
-Conducting awareness sessions
-Providing cleaning campaigns 

The Shelter support interventions will consist of: providing 2300 NFIs in Haydan and kitaf districts, training for assessment and registration team, and conducting a rapid need assessment including the PDM Report for the shelter interventions. 

The targeted beneficiaries for the WASH interventions will be 10,812 individuals (2120 men, 2206 women, 3178 boys, 3308 girls) in Haydan, and for the Shelter interventions will be 16100 individual beneficiaries (3157 men, 3284 women, 4733 boys, 4926 girls) in Kitaf amp Haydan.

The intervention aims to alleviate suffering for women amp children who are responsible for fetching water used for drinking amp other domestic uses. Women will have more time for taking care of their children amp family members in the time saved from fetching water for their HHs. Equally, children will have more time to be able to join classes amp get an education instead of spend time fetching water. Also, people with disabilities will be provided with safe drinking water, which will protect them from catching water-borne diseases. This project will provide a sustainable healthy environment for 26,912  of the most affected populations, host communities amp IDPs. Furthermore, IDPs in the area will also be provided  NFIs to facilitate their living situation, in addition to having increased access to water. Since many IDPs are vulnerable due to their unstable living situations (either in open settlements or dependent upon host communities), the WASH and Shelter interventions will complement each other to alleviate IDP’s suffering, in facilitating their access to water, offering a cleaner environment for them to live, and alleviate IDP children’s burden of fetching water.

The security situation has deteriorated, amp risks that we may face are: WASH interventions may be targeted, meaning beneficiaries have less access to water beneficiaries demand to add activities that aren’t included in project amp rehabilitation of WASH projects may provoke conflict. NFDHR has faced many similar challenges in the field amp has gathered lessons learnt, so we hold the capacity to solve these challenges amp mitigate the risks.

NFDHR is currently working in Sa’ada in WASH, FSL, Health, Nutrition, Protection amp Education contexts, so we are familiar with the terrain, amp have a great deal of experience with local stakeholders through our field office in Sa’ada. Our access is never restricted due to our diligent implementation amp coordination with all stakeholders. title: Simplified family MUAC integrated nutrition program in Taiz
description: Mercy Corps proposes adoption/ further testing of the uniMUAC bracelet for use by caregivers. Early laboratory tests show it improves on options such as the UNICEF bracelet and clickMUAC, with higher specificity, features to aid use by mothers, and additional measurement for pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) who remain underserved by existing options. This intervention will target nutrition outcomes, but will also impact health, food security, and social cohesion. MUAC is considered a strong indicator for nutrition-related mortality in children.  It is easily used by caregivers with lower literacy and is low-cost. Districts in Taiz carry a heavy burden of malnutrition. This innovation will target communities further from health facilities, allowing them to monitor nutrition status at home. Distribution will layer with existing programming in the same district. Selected Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) from Governorate Health Office (GHO) lists will deliver and educate on the bracelets and provide follow up visits. In order to add to the evidence base, it will be implemented using geographic clusters to compare the uniMUAC and UNICEF bracelets as a first in a field setting.

title: Fragile Borderlands: Drivers of Drought Adaptation and Instability in MENA
description: The “Fragile Borderlands: Drivers of Drought Adaptation and Instability in MENA” project by Mercy Corps examines how drought-driven livelihood stress reshapes informal and illicit cross-border trade across three fragile border regions — the Syria–Iraq borderlands, the Lebanon–Syria frontier, and Yemen’s coastal zones. The study explores how these informal trade networks, involving food, fuel, livestock, and water, can either support climate adaptation or exacerbate insecurity, depending on governance quality, market structures, and local power dynamics. Using a comparative mixed-methods approach combining geospatial analysis, market data, and field-based qualitative research, the project aims to identify the conditions under which drought coping mechanisms stabilize livelihoods or fuel exclusion and conflict. Outputs will include peer-reviewed research, policy briefs, interactive visual maps, and stakeholder events to inform more inclusive and conflict-sensitive climate adaptation policies across the MENA region.

description: The FC project SFD - Education in Rural Areas represents a continuation of the German commitment in the Yemeni education sector and continues the support of the Yemeni Social Fund for Development (SFD) that began in 2003. As part of the national economic and social policy, the SFD finances nationwide measures to rehabilitate and expand the social and economic infrastructure in poor areas. The FC funds are to be used exclusively for SFD education projects. The FC project comprises the expansion, rehabilitation and demand-oriented construction of primary and secondary schools in rural communities in Yemen. In addition, the SFD carries out measures to train teaching staff and raise awareness among the target population with regard to enrolment of girls. The objective of the FC measure is thus to increase access to and use of primary and secondary schools in rural areas. The target group are pupils from grades 1 to 9 in the programme area. We assume that in Phase 1 around 5,500 children will benefit directly from the FC measure. Thus, the project makes a direct contribution to the overall objective of German bilateral DC in the education sector, which summarises the objectives of the national strategies for primary and secondary education: Children and young people receive and use access to an appropriate range of education in primary and secondary education. In a first phase, we propose to co-finance the SFD education programme in the amount of EUR 5.5 million (FC grant). The Yemeni governments own contribution amounts to around EUR 0.55 million. A second phase with an additional EUR 10 million of FC financing (inventory control share) can be implemented in parallel from 2015. Each of the two phases is in itself a completed project that makes sense in developmental terms.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Improving access to basic social services for IDPs and local population
description:
Context: 

War has been raging in Yemen since 2015 and there have been devastating consequences: large parts of the infrastructure have been damaged or destroyed, the majority of the population is dependent on humanitarian aid and millions of people lack adequate access to drinking water, sanitation and health care.
The number of internally displaced persons in the country is estimated at 4.84 million. The local administrations of the host regions are barely able to meet the needs of their own population and therefore cannot respond to the additional requirements and needs of vulnerable groups. The social and psychological well-being of the population suffers as a result.

Ziel: 

Access to health care, water and sanitation, as well as to basic social services, has improved for internally displaced persons and the local population in host communities. In particular, the needs of disadvantaged groups are taken into account.

Vorgehensweise: 

Since 2025, the project has been improving basic services in the southern regions of Taiz, Aden, and Hadramout. It focuses on the needs of internally displaced persons, people with disabilities, women, children and other disadvantaged groups.
The project focuses on inclusive and gender-sensitive implementation, and pursues these priorities:
- It improves the resilience of the target population.
- It systematically supports health care providers in order to counteract the lack of qualified personnel and the destruction of facilities.
- It promotes health training for the prevention and control of infections, and for obstetrics, and it improves sanitation systems and drinking water supplies and makes them barrier-free and inclusive.
- It raises the population’s hygiene awareness and improves the management and administrative skills of local authorities in the areas of water, sanitation and hygiene.
- It offers psychosocial services, primarily for women, children and people with disabilities.

title: Reproductive Health VI, Social Marketing III (Yamaan)
description: The project Reproductive Health VI, Social Marketing III continues the German FC commitment to improving the reproductive health of the Yemeni population in a third phase (previous phases were BMZ no.: 2007.6523.0 and 2011.6546.3). The aim of the project is to improve the target groups knowledge of reproductive health and modern family planning and attitudes and behaviour with regard to avoiding unwanted pregnancies. At the same time, the demand for and use of modern contraceptive methods is to be increased and stable access to modern contraceptive methods ensured even in the current crisis situation. The target group is the sexually active population, with special emphasis on young people and women. The programme measures include the procurement and distribution of subsidised contraceptives via the private sector, as well as information campaigns via channels such as social media, call centres, interpersonal communication by community-based volunteers and lobbying activities. The measures are implemented by the Yamaan Foundation based in Sanaa. The total costs for a planned duration of 3.5 years are estimated at EUR 6.2 million. The FC contribution amounts to EUR 5 million. Additional costs of EUR 1.2 million are to be covered by sales revenues.

title: Reproductive Health VII (Voucher Project Mother and Child Health)
description: The project Reproductive Health VII, Voucher Project Mother and Child Health III continues the German Financial Cooperation commitment to improve reproductive health and mother and child health in a third phase (previous phases were BMZ no. 2007.6523.0 and 2013.6526.1). The objective of the voucher project is to increase the use of health services related to safe childbirth and family planning services by poor women, with the focus in Phase 3 being on urban areas with a high concentration of IDPs (module objective). The programme thus contributes to reducing maternal and child mortality (programme objective). The project measures include the provision and distribution of voucher booklets for safe maternity, which can be redeemed to finance transport to the health facility, pre- and post-natal examinations, a professionally assisted birth and the treatment of possible complications. Vouchers for long-term family planning are distributed at the same time. In addition, the project contributes to improving the quality of services in public and private health care facilities. In Phase 3, the project area is to be expanded to include additional urban districts in the governorates of Ibb and Sanaa, where many IDPs live. The project is being implemented by the Yemeni Yamaan Foundation. The total costs of Phase 3 for a duration of 2 years and 3 months are estimated at around EUR 5.02 million. The FC contribution amounts to EUR 5 million. Costs exceeding this amount are to be covered by sales revenues.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Strengthening resilience and participation at local level
description:
Context: 

Yemen is one of the worlds least developed countries. It is struggling with the devastating consequences of the civil war that has been going on since 2014. Two thirds of the population require humanitarian aid and food shortages result in malnutrition and diseases, especially among children.

The physical and social infrastructure is outdated in many places and partially destroyed in the war zones. More than half of all Yemenis have no access to clean water and sanitation, causing diseases to spread rapidly. Vulnerable groups such as children, young people, women, people with disabilities and the Muhamasheen ethnic minority are particularly affected. The cholera epidemic and the ongoing military conflicts complicate the situation.

Objective: 

Local institutions and vulnerable population groups in selected governorates are more resilient.

Approach: 

The transitional development assistance programme combines humanitarian aid and development cooperation as follows:

It contributes to the improvement of basic services by rehabilitating destroyed infrastructure such as schools, health centres and water pipes.

At the same time, the project promotes food security and the livelihoods of rural households, for example, by training farmers in innovative farming and irrigation techniques. Cash-for-work measures such as the construction of irrigation systems provide direct income and contribute to the temporary stabilisation of rural households.

Building fish landing sites and marketing structures promotes the livelihoods of fishers and strengthens food security in the coastal region. Fishers also receive training in sustainable fishing and processing methods as well as boat repair.

Small-scale projects with local civil society organisations further promote the social cohesion of communities.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Strengthening Resilience through Enhancing Health Service Facilities in Yemen
description: The project objective is to contribute to strengthening the resilience of health care facilities and the population in the project area with regard to health risks. To this end, measures to stabilize and improve access to and quality of public health facilities, probably district and general hospitals, are financed. On the other hand, accompanying community mobilization activities involving representatives of vulnerable population groups are to be carried out in all project locations, with the aim of adequately addressing the central needs of vulnerable groups and increasing the use by vulnerable population groups. The project is being implemented to complement other German DC approaches in the health sector in Yemen. It is an important addition to the demand-side FC voucher project for reproductive health and contributes to addressing priority rehabilitation and equipment needs that can only be covered to a limited extent within the framework of FC and TC projects. In the context of an increase, measures to prepare health care facilities for the treatment of COVID-19 patients are also expected to be integrated into the project from mid-2020. The project will run for 33 months, starting at the end of 2019. The project is financed under the title of Transitional Assistance, for which EUR 20 million in transition assistance funds have been made available. In addition, the project includes a stock assessment in the amount of EUR 10 million.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Quality of Education Improvement Programme III
description:
War has affected Yemen since 2015. The severe political, economic and social problems have led to the worst humanitarian crisis of current times. Providing social services such as education is difficult. Staff turnover in administrations and schools is high, lessons are cancelled and classrooms are overcrowded. War-related damage to the education infrastructure, the requisition of schools for other purposes and attacks on school staff are seriously disrupting primary and secondary school education.
The project strengthens the capacity of educational institutions and thereby ensures access to quality education. By taking action to combat falling school enrolment rates and retain children in schools, especially girls, Yemen can mitigate the impacts of war.

National and regional educational institutions in Yemen have greater organisational and institutional capacity to ensure good educational opportunities in crisis situations.

The programme trains personnel at the educational authorities. The aim is to equip them to plan, steer and implement education more effectively at national and regional level during crises. It also provides advice on coordination between national, regional and local authorities, thereby improving structures for school management processes.
The programme works on school development plans with local communities to incorporate priorities that help keep schools running in crisis situations. There is a particular focus on girls’ education.
The programme offers in-service training for school personnel and management. It also provides training on water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), psychosocial support (PSES) and school-based health measures.
In conjunction with the World Food Programme (WFP), the programme is improving school meals.

description: The goal of the proposal is to strengthen the resilience of the local population to the current crisis by rehabilitating infrastructure within the areas water and agriculture. The measures are implemented in such a way that simultaneously employment and income opportunities are created for poor parts of the population in rural areas of Yemen. A central aspect of the proposal, which aims to strengthen the resilience of the population, is the fact that a significant share of measures is implemented using the Cash for Work method.  The target group of the proposal is the rural population in various locations in North and in South Yemen.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: SFD - Strengthening Resilience through Labor Intensive Works Program V
description: Phase V of the Labour Intensive Works Programme (LIWP) is part of the Special Initiative for Stabilization and Development in the Middle East and North Africa (SI MENA), which was launched by the BMZ in 2014.The project will be implemented by the FC partner Social Fund for Development (SFD) across Yemen using a cash-for-work approach to support vulnerable population groups in predominantly rural areas. The aim of the FC project is to contribute to the stabilization of Yemen in the current crisis and to improving the resilience of the target groups. By providing poverty-oriented basic infrastructure in various fields (such as latrines, rainwater collection systems, rural roads, rehabilitation of agricultural lands) the SFD makes a significant contribution to alleviating poverty and improving livelihoods of the crisis affected population. The project thus contributes to economic and social stabilization across the whole of Yemen.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Reproductive Health IX (Voucher Programme IV)
description: The proposal Reproductive Health IX continues the German FC involvement in the sector regarding the improvement of reproductive and mother-child health in a fourth phase. The objective of the voucher program is the vast, inclusive and impartial provision of high-quality health services regarding safe childbirth and family planning in the beneficiary governorates (module objective). This contributes to the strengthening of the sexual and reproductive health and respective rights of women and girls in Yemen (program objective). Moreover, the proposal includes a contribution to the prevention of COVID-19.The method to reach said objectives is the distribution of vouchers for safe maternity, which among other things finance the transportation to health facilities, professionally supervised childbirth and the treatment of complications. At the same time, vouchers for long-term family planning are distributed and support measures for qualified health facilities are implemented. The latter receive payments to improve the quality of their services through a performance-based financing mechanism. Also, measures to protect the population and health works from COVID-19 are implemented (e.g. distribution of protective equipment). The project-executing partner is the Yemeni Yamaan Foundation in the governorates Ibb, Aden, Lahj and Al Hudaydah. For the project duration of 36 months total costs of EUR 11.02 mil. are estimated. The FC contribution sums up to EUR 11 mil. Further costs are planned to be covered by the sale of contraceptives.

title: SFD Water/Wastewater Programme (VPT III)
description: The SFD WASH program seeks to rehabilitate and expand basic water supply and sanitation in the areas particularly affected by the current conflict in Yemen. In particular, the FZ-measure wishes to contribute to securing the supply of drinking water and to ensuring the access to adequate sanitation. This is expected to ameliorate the overall health as well as the living conditions of the beneficaries and thus, also contributes to alleviating the Covid-crisis in Yemen. The program covers the whole of Yemen. Although the individual measures are implemented in urban and rural areas, the emphasis is on rural areas. The target group is composed of city dwellers as well as rural residents in those governorates particularly affected by the conflict. In total, 88,000 beneficiaries are assumed to be reached by the measures of the current phase.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Strengthening resilience by improving the capacities of health facilities in Yemen, phase III
description: In Yemen, around 20.7 million people - 66 percent of the population - are in need of humanitarian assistance in 2021. Access to basic health services is either limited or non-existent for large parts of the population.The project is intended to contribute to strengthening the resilience of health facilities and the population in the project areas (impact). This is to be achieved by stabilizing and improving access to and use of public health facilities. In addition, the project contributes to strengthening social cohesion with the aim of addressing the key needs of vulnerable population groups in particular and increasing the use of health services in the financed facilities across all population groups (outcome).Key measures and outcomes are: Rehabilitation and repair of health facilities including stabilization of the functionality of drinking water and sanitation, waste disposal and electricity, construction of isolation wards for the treatment of infectious diseases, in particular COVID-19 training measures for health personnel. The target group of the project is the population of the selected districts with a special focus on vulnerable groups such as women. The project executing agency is the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS).

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Support to peaceful co-existence in Yemen
description:
The ongoing war in Yemen has worsened the situation of women, young people and civil society actors. For them, opportunities for participation in society are few. Whilst being a much needed force for peace in the country, they are also affected by multiple forms of violence. To realize the peace-building potential of women, young people and civil society actors, they need support and spaces for the exchange of experiences. This way, inclusive and conflict-reducing measures can be implemented more effectively

Women, young people and civil society actors play an active role in shaping peaceful coexistence in their communities.

In line with the German Cooperation’s Whole of Yemen approach, project activities are carried out throughout all of Yemen, targeting groups affected by multiple forms of discrimination. The measures address three interlinked fields of Activity:

1. Supporting women: the project supports women in conflict situations and facilitates various exchange formats to promote networking between women and women’s organizations.
2. Supporting young people: using innovative approaches and digital methods, the project raises awareness of peaceful coexistence among young people in Yemen whilst improving their media information literacy skills. The project develops serious game apps for mobile devices and promotes creative contributions from young people.
3. Capacity building of civil society actors: actors of the civil society receive support in building institutional, technical and methodological skills, enabling them to better implement specific measures to reach their target groups. Together with Deutsche Welle Akademie, the project also strengthens the media and information skills of young Yemeni media professionals and enhances their journalistic skills.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Supporting Good Governance  Accountability and Inclusiveness in Yemen
description:
The ongoing armed conflict in Yemen has resulted in deep political and institutional divides in the country. This poses major challenges for state structures and affects the population’s opportunities to participate in public life.
Local government structures are still in place nationwide, however resources and the quality of governance vary in the different regions.
At the same time, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and grassroots initiatives are working to expand participation opportunities for the population and to ensure that their needs and interests are taken into account to a greater extent in local decision-making processes. The main challenges facing civil society actors include a lack of skills and resources, in addition to administrative constraints.

Local governance in the project areas is supported and public services have improved.


The project contributes to the development of evidence-based approaches for good local governance. Based on lessons learned by national and international development actors, it compiles six short studies with strategic and methodological recommendations to promote good local governance in Yemen.
The project strengthens the capacities for cooperation and coordination of local government structures by supporting them through suitable measures as required. For instance, it works with representatives of local authorities to build the capacities they need to fulfil their roles and responsibilities and carry out integrative and participative planning, enabling them to provide better services.
The project supports civil society actors in developing their competencies, particularly in requesting local authorities to share information on and justification for their decisions on service provision. Using innovative methods, civil society projects contribute to increasing local authorities’ awareness of the needs of Yemen’s citizens..

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: UNICEF support to internally displaced in Yemen Phase V
description: Due to the ongoing conflict the number of internally displaced persons in Yemen has grown to more than 4 million people. The fragile and overburdened public structures can not sufficiently guarantee the basic needs of internally displaced persons (IDP) and their host communities.The overarching objective of the project is to improve the living conditions of internally displaced people and the local population. The project is divided into three components: Education (i) with the aim of improving access to high-quality education for children that have been affected by the conflict, (ii) Child Protection to increase the resilience of children and WASH (ii) with the aims of improving access to clean potable water, improving wastewater systems and also improving hygienic conditions for children and families in regions with a high risk of cholera. Examples of project measures include the rehabilitation of schools, school supplies, various measures to assist children and and also the rehabilitation of drinking water supply and wasterwater systems in urban areas. The target group are internally displaced people and the local population in the targeted provinces. The project executing agency is the United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF).

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Increasing Integrated Health Resilience in Yemen
description: In the Yemeni health system, health services in the areas of sexual and reproductive health and communicable diseases including COVID-19 and non-communicable diseases are not sufficiently available to ensure basic care for the population.The objective of the project is to increase the health resilience of people and institutions in fragile contexts with a focus on reproductive health, non-communicable diseases and infectious diseases, in particular COVID-19. This is a coherent continuation and expansion of the German FC commitment to improve health care in Yemen. The project is designed as an open program and will take place in parallel with the ongoing phases of the voucher project (BMZ 2013.6526.1, BMZ 2017.6836.5 and BMZ 2020.6770.0) and the social marketing project (BMZ 2017.6546.3 and BMZ 2019.6763.7). The simultaneous implementation allows for efficiency gains in terms of implementation costs and enables synergies with regard to joint training and monitoring activities, among others.The elementary measures are the following: - Distribution of vouchers for health services and consultations on family planning.- Distribution of contraceptives and implementation of family planning awareness activities. - Treatment of people with non-communicable diseases. - Prevention measures for infectious diseases. The target group is the Yemeni population, including mainly young couples and chronically ill people. The project is implemented by the project executing agency Yamaan Foundation for Health and Social Development.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: SFD equal access to education I
description: The project addresses core problems in Yemen. It strengthens educational opportunities, primarily in rural areas. It pursues a dual objective: to promote empowerment of girls and strengthen the resilience of young Yemenis by providing social, educational, and economic opportunities. Schools are being rehabilitated and expanded, and Community Learning Centers (CLCs) with one to two classrooms are being established in rural areas. In addition, numerous training measures are being carried out in order to improve the capacities of school staff and teachers and thus also to increase the quality of formal school education. In addition, young people at risk are trained and employed as volunteer teachers to fill the shortage of teachers in schools and to provide educational services in the CLCs. The training and income generated for young people is also a preventative measure against manipulation and radicalization of young Yemenis by radical groups. Further training measures are aimed at the local communities to convey the relevance of education, also and especially for girls, and to train parents to actively participate in the learning development of their children (by establishing parent councils). The project executing agency is the Yemeni Social Fund for Development (SFD).

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: SFD Water/Wastewater Programme V
description: Yemen suffers from water shortages and inadequate supply infrastructure in the WASH sector (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene). The precarious situation has a negative impact on the health situation and food security. The FC project continues the support of the WASH program of the Yemeni Social Fund for Development (SFD) with another module (Phase 5). Aim of the project is to provide access to improved water sources and safe sanitation facilities.The project finances, among other things, cisterns on house roofs, water catch basins, latrines, hygiene campaigns and local water/sanitation systems (some of them solar-powered). Much of the interventions are implemented at community level, led by SFD and in direct collaboration with community representatives, particularly with cash-for-work approach, where households receive money to implement the interventions. Larger construction measures are implemented jointly with local water suppliers and construction companies. Households or communities are selected in a multi-stage process based initially on data on needs in the governorates and on a selection of districts by SFD. The individual sub-projects are then selected by SFD through so-called Participatory Rapid Assessments, which determine the needs at the community level and select appropriate measures.Through poverty-oriented provision of basic infrastructure, SFD makes a significant contribution to improving the living conditions of impoverished population groups in large parts of Yemen. The target group of the project includes both rural and urban households throughout Yemen.

title: Promotion of the Financial Sector and MSME III
description: Due to the ongoing crisis in Yemen, many micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are struggling to survive. They lack access to financing because the microfinance sector is underdeveloped.The projects target at outcome-level is to provide refinancing for microfinance institutions (MFI) to support the sustainable access of MSME to financial services. Furthermore, the project aims at maintaining the microfinance sectors business activity, develop the sectors abilities further and hence securing the immediate survival of existing structures and mid-term stabilization of the sector. The projects target at impact level is to support the private sectors business activity, securing jobs, and hence to generate income and reduce poverty. Target group are MSME, possible start-ups in this segment as well as family members and employees of the MSME. At the financial sector level, the target group are MFI. The project executing agency is the Yemeni Social Fund for Development (SFD). The project aims at achieving its objectives by providing grant-financing to SFD-SMED which in turn channels the funds to MFI. The project extends an existing phase by 4.5 Mio. EUR.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Improving food security for resilience in Yemen
description:
Context: 

Yemen has been close to the bottom of the Global Hunger Index (GHI) rankings for years. According to the GHI 2023, the hunger situation is categorised as ‘very serious’. In the light of the devastating civil war of recent years, the social and economic situation of the population is steadily deteriorating. More frequent extreme weather events are exacerbating the situation. The United Nations International Childrens Emergency Fund (UNICEF) estimates that around three quarters of the population depend on humanitarian assistance.

Women and girls are particularly affected. According to UNICEF, every ten minutes a child dies of a preventable disease. 2.2 million children under the age of five and around 1.3 million pregnant or breastfeeding women are suffering from acute undernutrition.

Objective: 

The food and nutrition security of vulnerable households in the target governorates has improved.

Approach: 

The project encourages vulnerable households to become more resilient to crises through climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture. Promoting a healthy and balanced diet is a core element.

The project supports farmers who are or will be active in dairy farming and crop cultivation. Training and material goods increase the availability of nutritious food, as well as income.

The project provides training and advice on skills for a hygienic and nutrient-rich diet. This includes production, storage, further processing and consumption.

Resilience to extreme weather events in smallholder agriculture is increased through training, small-scale construction measures and remunerated jobs (cash-for-work).

Cooperation with local companies enables the development of structures that can anchor and expand the measures in the country in the long term.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: UNDP - Rehabilitation in the Fishery Sector
description: The project is intended to contribute to stabilizing the economic situation and securing the food supply of the population in the project area (impact). In doing so, the project contributes to enabling people and structures to adapt to long-term changes and to cushion and minimize negative impacts (adaptive capacity). This is to be achieved by improving the utilization possibilities of the fishing port in Aden. In addition, the project contributes to strengthening social cohesion with the aim of paying special attention to the key needs of vulnerable population groups such as young people and women, and leveraging the potential of the fisheries sector to stabilize the precarious situation of various population groups. The primary objective of the project is thus to improve the nutritional situation of particularly vulnerable population groups in Yemen and to create economic prospects in the fisheries sector (outcome). The project is an open program with a comprehensive approach that includes a package of measures based on needs analyses. At the selected project site in Aden, this includes needs-oriented rehabilitation measures for the fishing port, the provision of equipment and training. In this way, the project addresses the specific bottlenecks and key obstacles to the revitalization and use of the fishing port and the associated new employment opportunities, especially for women. At the same time, the project contributes to stabilizing food security.

description: In Yemen, about 20.7 million people - 66% of the population - are in need of humanitarian assistance in the year 2021. reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Strengthening the health system in Yemen III
description:
Context: 

Yemen presently encounters difficulties in delivering quality healthcare services, signalling a need for improvement in its medical facilities. To this end, the Health System Strengthening Project aims to maintain essential healthcare services at an acceptable standard for the entire population across five governorates. 

Objective: 

The third project phase from August 2022 to December 2025 targets essential healthcare services in the governorates and also aims to improve referrals from the primary health care level to the relevant referral hospital.

Approach: 

The project builds on the results achieved in the second phase by adopting the Quality Improvement Program (QIP), which is designed to ensure the provision of improved care by health workers and facilities. For this, it builds up the capabilities of hospitals, improves the performance of health care providers and provides essential medical equipment and materials. It also carries out planning and cooperation activities with governorate health offices (GHO) and supervises district health offices and facilities. The project work includes assisting health managers in improving both health planning and services.
To take advantage of the German expertise, the Akkon University of Human Sciences with its Institute for Research in International Assistance (IRIA) plays a leading role in improving the capabilities of the national academic institutions to ensure long-term success of quality and performance improvement.
The project sustains the continuity of quality improvement of health care services by encouraging the quality team to develop quality circles on a regular basis to identify gaps, analyse daily challenges and follow up on key performance indicators.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Strengthening the resilience of the water sector in Yemen
description:
Context: 

Yemen ranks among the driest countries in the world. Its already critical water situation has worsened dramatically since civil war broke out in 2015. The countrys infrastructure has been severely damaged, and inadequate power supply for drinking water pumps and sewage systems pose significant challenges for municipal water and wastewater companies. The country lacks the resources, materials and skilled workers to repair and maintain the damaged infrastructure.

Objective: 

The resilience of urban water and wastewater companies in Yemen has improved, enabling safe water and sanitation services.

Approach: 

The project is active in three areas:

1. Planning and monitoring
The project is supporting water and wastewater companies in recording current data and using a digital information system to transmit their financial, technical and operational data to the Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE). The MWE then uses this data to formulate specific policy measures and improve its institutional supervisory framework.

2. Improving the resilience of wastewater management
The project is taking a range of measures to improve the revenues of the municipal wastewater disposal system. It is especially supporting workplace health and safety, human resources, maintenance and operations, and quality assurance.

3. Developing skills
The project is improving the skills of personnel in water and wastewater services through a South–South cooperation in knowledge exchange between representatives of various water and wastewater companies in Yemen and Jordan. The establishment of a Yemeni-Jordanian women’s network is particularly improving the skills of women in the water sector.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: IOM - Enhanced water resource management in IDP communities
description: Due to the destruction of war, climate change and economic decline, basic services have collapsed in many regions across Yemen. At the same time, many people are no longer able to make a living due to a general shortage in income opportunities. Fueled by a continuous influx of internally displaced persons (IDP), these circumstances lead to resource-related distribution conflicts, especially in the host communities. The project offers approaches for conflict resolution by improving basic infrastructure in the water sector and by providing income-generating measures. The target group are IDP and host communities. The planned measures include:1) Financing of drinking water supply systems for households (e.g. solar-powered pumps, water pipes, house connections) and irrigation infrastructure for agricultural use as well as flood protection (e.g. rainwater reservoirs, irrigation ditches, dams, flood protection walls),2) Lifelihood measures to generate income (essentially cash-for-work and skills training for long-term integration into the labor market),3) Peace-building measures for conflict mediation (including support to community-based Water User Associations (WUAs), Conflict Resolution Committees (CRCs) and training and awareness-raising campaigns for a fair distribution and sustainable use of the scarce water resources).The project is supported by a EUR 10 million grant financed through KfW from the BMZs Special Initiative to Support Refugees and implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). IOM is both a direct recipient of funds and project implementer.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Increasing Integrated Health Resilience in Yemen II
description: In the Yemeni healthcare system, health services in the areas of sexual and reproductive health and psychosocial treatments are not sufficiently available to ensure basic care for the population. The project aims to improve the delivery of these services. It funds voucher booklets for health services for safe motherhood, long-term family planning, and psychosocial treatments. It also carries out performance-based payments to health facilities and finances training programs for health workers.The goal of the project is to increase the health resilience of people and institutions in fragile contexts with a focus on reproductive health and psychosocial diseases. This is a coherent continuation and expansion of the German FC commitment to improving healthcare in Yemen. The project is designed as an open program and will take place in parallel to the ongoing phases of the voucher project and the social marketing project. The project represents the second phase of the health resilience building project that commenced in December 2021. The simultaneous implementation allows for efficiency gains in terms of implementation costs and enables synergies regarding joint training as well as monitoring activities. Elementary measures of the project:   - Voucher distribution for health services and consultations on family planning and treatment of psychosocial diseases, - Support for healthcare facilities to ensure the quality of their services, including rehabilitation measures, - Training and education measures for healthcare personnel.The target group is the Yemeni population, including in particular young couples and people with psychosocial illnesses. The project is implemented by the project executing agency Yamaan Foundation.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Building resilience in the vaccine supply chain in Yemen
description: The project is an open program with a comprehensive approach that includes a package of measures based on needs assessments. This includes rehabilitation measures at Yemeni health logistics facilities (storage facilities), the provision of equipment and training measures. The project complements FC projects already underway with UNOPS (Übergangshilfe) (BMZ 2019.1866.3, BMZ 2020.1804.2, BMZ 2021.1808.1). The objective of the project is to support health logistics in Yemen, in particular to enable the distribution of COVID-19 vaccines nationwide. The target group of the project is the population of the catchment area of the facilities that receive COVID-19 vaccine as well as other medical products from the selected warehouses. Thus, the project addresses the specific shortages as well as key barriers to stabilizing access to COVID-19 vaccine and other medical products for the population.  Specifically, the activities include the rehabilitation and equipping of up to 22 warehouses, as well as training for up to 300 employees of the warehouses and women-owned businesses. The rehabilitation measures will be implemented by national construction companies selected in a public tendering process in accordance with UNOPS procurement guidelines. These are given the requirement to use unskilled labor from the local population for selected simple tasks. Equipment, supplies, and furniture are procured for the selected storage facilities to maintain basic functions and improve operational capacity. Examples of equipment include IT equipment/systems and ultra-low temperature cold chain systems (i.e., cold rooms, refrigerated containers). The project also includes training opportunities for staff at the supported storage facilities, including training on the operation of the procured equipment as well as vaccine handling and management. In addition, special training is provided for women-owned enterprises to facilitate their participation in tenders in the project.

description: The project is intended to contribute to stabilizing the economic situation and securing the food supply of the population in the project area (impact). In doing so, the project contributes to enabling people and structures to adapt to long-term changes and to cushion and minimize negative impacts (adaptive capacity). This is to be achieved by improving the utilization possibilities of the fishing port in Aden. In addition, the project contributes to strengthening social cohesion with the aim of paying special attention to the key needs of vulnerable population groups such as young people and women, and leveraging the potential of the fisheries sector to stabilize the precarious situation of various population groups. The primary objective of the project is thus to improve the nutritional situation of particularly vulnerable population groups in Yemen and to create economic prospects in the fisheries sector (outcome). The project is an open program with a comprehensive approach that includes a package of measures based on needs analyses. At the selected project site in Aden, this includes needs-oriented rehabilitation measures for the fishing port, the provision of equipment and training. In this way, the project addresses the specific bottlenecks and key obstacles to the revitalization and use of the fishing port and the associated new employment opportunities, especially for women. At the same time, the project contributes to stabilizing food security.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: UNDP - Strengthening agricultural resilience and food security through improved water resource management
description: The overall objective of the project is to enhance the livelihood resilience of vulnerable groups especially women in selected locations in Yemen through the development and rehabilitation of infrastructure aimed to enhance water availability in support of sustainable agriculture, implemented at key priority areas within a catchment. The first phase of the project will be implemented in the two governorates of Taiz (South) and Lahj.This project objective will be achieved through investment in 3 different components:1) by investing in new water storage and distribution infrastructure as well as rehabilitating existing agricultural water related old systems. Sustainability of water resources made available from this project will be ensured by adopting Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) strategies. Infrastructure conceptualisation will be based on catchment based hydrological assessments.2) to alleviate poverty by creating additional income generating opportunities achieved by initiating small value adding activities to agricultural products such as drying, canning, cheese making as well as enhancing market accessibility equitably to local communities.3) The participatory nature of project implementation will contribute to empowerment, trust building and social cohesion. Sustaining the infrastructure is an integral aim for sustainable agriculture and will be fulfilled by creating the enabling environment for local management of assets including institutional strengthening of both public national, provincial and district partners as well as local community-based structures such as Water User Associations (WUAs).The project will also contribute to generating new knowledge and understanding of water resources centrality in regional and local planning for sustainable development and stability in Yemen.The first project phase will be financed through KfW by a EUR 19 million grant from the BMZ transitional development assistance fund.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Promotion of the private sector and employment
description:
Context: 

Due to the civil war, more than two-thirds of Yemen’s population rely on humanitarian assistance. The unstable economic and political situation means that young people, in particular, lack job prospects. Even university graduates often struggle to find employment. In 2021, youth unemployment in Yemen was around 26 per cent. Women face additional hurdles to earning their own income due to traditional gender roles.
The economy has also suffered heavily as a result of the war. Companies in Yemen have significant difficulty achieving long-term economic growth. They often lack access to investments and loans. The conflict has also destroyed a lot of infrastructure, and many parts of the country have limited access to electricity and the internet. This particularly affects companies and self-employed people working in digital products and services.

Objective: 

Further training for workers and better access to finance for companies could create more jobs in Yemen’s digital economy. Cooperation with the private sector is also needed in order to improve prospects for young people.

Approach: 

Yemen’s digital economy provides young people with jobs that pay a living wage and allows women, in particular, to earn their own income.
The project operates in three fields of activity:
1. It improves the career prospects of young graduates and entrepreneurs by providing them with further training and networking opportunities. It promotes employment in the digital economy, in particular.
2. It also trains entrepreneurs in finance and improves their access to financial services such as loans.
3. The project works with the private sector to offer young people employment.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Vocational training in Yemen
description:
Context: 

The ongoing armed conflict in Yemen that began in 2014 has resulted in a serious economic and political crisis. Die to the continuing recession, the labour market can no longer accommodate the young people that enter it every year. A quarter of young adults are unemployed.
There is a lack of basic qualifications and practical skills. The vocational education and training system is deficient and underfunded, and equipment and facilities at vocational schools are obsolete or non-existent. Teachers have substandard specialist and teaching expertise, while learning methods and content are outdated and impractical. Moreover, teachers receive their salaries irregularly or not at all.

Objective: 

The regional vocational school administrations can better fulfil their mandate as supervisory authorities thanks to training and advisory services, and vocational schools are holding short courses geared to the needs of the labour market.

Approach: 

The project operates in the following priority areas:
- It systematically involves the private sector in TVET through dialogue platforms, which allow it to identify labour market needs and better tailor training courses to suit them.
- It offers short courses geared to labour market needs that teach technical skills, soft skills and entrepreneurial expertise.
- It provides the necessary infrastructure and equipment for the short courses.
- It trains staff at regional vocational school administrations on topics such as gender-sensitive school management and budget and financial planning.
- It trains heads of vocational schools in how to perform their roles with greater effectiveness and gender sensitivity.
- It provides teachers with specialist teacher training and practical training.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: Economic Empowerment of Rural Women and their Communities
description: The FC measure aims at the economic empowerment of women in Yemen who are massively excluded from participating in economic life by power structures, discriminatory norms, and preconceived role models in their households and communities. In terms of feminist development policy, the project addresses structural inequalities and inequity and aims to eliminate them in the long term. By reducing domestic workloads and gender barriers, as well as providing access to markets and financial resources, the livelihoods of women in the target communities shall be improved in the long term. The project takes an integrative approach to various interventions that include small-scale infrastructure activities as well as training, awareness-raising, and structure-building activities at the community level and will be implemented primarily in rural areas of the governorates of Hodeidah, Hajjah, Saada, Lahj and Taiz.

reporting: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
title: SFD Strengthening Educational Opportunities in Yemen II (VPT 1)
description: The project addresses core problems in Yemen. It strengthens educational opportunities, primarily in rural areas. It pursues a dual objective: to promote empowerment of girls and strengthen the resilience of young Yemenis by providing social, educational, and economic opportunities. Schools are being rehabilitated and expanded, and Community Learning Centers (CLCs) with one to two classrooms are being established in rural areas. In addition, numerous training measures are being carried out in order to improve the capacities of school staff and teachers and thus to increase the quality of formal school education. In addition, young people at risk are trained and employed as volunteer teachers to fill the shortage of teachers in schools and to provide educational services in the CLCs. The training and income generated for young people is also a preventative measure against manipulation and radicalization of young Yemenis by radical groups. Further training measures are aimed at the local communities to convey the relevance of education, also and especially for girls, and to train parents to actively participate in the learning development of their children (by establishing parent councils). The project executing agency is the Yemeni Social Fund for Development (SFD).
